Dear Diary,
Yesterday was a just another day. Couple of arguements and a late dinner. So, after all that I went online. I went on to chat. Wow, my buddy list was lit up. Almost all of them were online. Except mines from here at DD. Seems most of you come on when I sleep. I actually had a confrence online. *confrence is when you have multiple ppl come into your pm* Wow, it feels so good to have ppl who know you all in the same chat room. It was great. We laughed, talked bout other stuff. Guess I was happy cause it's been a while since I've talked to ppl I know. I'm so isolated where I am. My friends barly talk to me any more. :( Guess you ppl online are my only friends now. Which is good and bad I guess. Good cause you ppl give good advice and make me laugh. Bad cause I can't actually see if your being sincere. Also, online hugs don't compare to real ones. THough online ones are nice. * I love seening em though, ((((tinoz))))* :) Whoever made that one up is pretty clever.
I think I should get one of them imood.com things. Where you put your mood online. I like seeing them on other ppl's pages. Today's mood would be, somewhat happy. Cause that's how i feel. Happy that I got ppl online that care, but sad that almost no one does in the "real" world.
Another thing I've been thinking about is my christianity. Trying to figure out if I'm a good christian or a bad one. Some say I'm a good person. Yeah, but does that get one into heaven. Some have said that as long as I go to church and study and be good that it's good enough. Well, I don't know about that either. Why, well I'm pretty sure GOD wants us to do more for him. And works, I know they don't get you into heaven either. Though I think it helps. And pure faith, does just saying you believe in heaven make you go to heaven. Hmm. I think I feel this way goes I want to be on fire for him but I'm not. Trying to figure out how. And how to stay on fire for him. ANy comments and suggestions welcomed.

As I mentioned earlier, my sister and brother-in-law are camping right now. I received a text from my brother-in-law saying he was concerned he might have left the oven on and would I mind driving to their home and checking? Of course, rain or no rain, I was immediately on my way. Good news, the oven wasn't on. D & K were so appreciative that I helped them out. I was more than happy to. There was a time in my life, many years ago now, that I wasn't well emotionally and was unable to give to others. Now that I'm well in all ways, that's not the case anymore. Nothing feels better than to be a true support to those I love and care about.

Oh my goodness gracious, it is now August 2024! Move on over July, August has FINALLY arrived. Woohoo, July is done for the year. Another woohoo. Hopefully now the weather will become cooler before September. Hmmm? Maybe not. Today, as far as I know, it did not rain like it was supposed to. I love it when the weather changes at the last minute. We were expecting a storm today, but it did not com e. It did get warm out though. I dislike the hear because it bothers my arthritic joints of the shoulders and elbows, and knees. Even my left knee was smarting a bit today because it was supposed to rain today. Maybe it did. I did not have my blinds open today because of the heat and the neighbors visiting outside by the bus stop and smoking.
I did not go anywhere today. I was wiped out yesterday from dialysis treatment and g been out and about town on Tuesday and was tired being out from 9 AM to 6 PM Tuesday morning and afternoon running errands and eating out and seeing two movies. It was a long, very long day for me. Even my bus ride to and from the bus depot was not too bad like my last three rides. I am getting used to the bumps and turns the bus makes while traveling about town. Getting to know the bus routes again is not a horrible experience anymore. My first three rides were not good experiences because the feeling of going left or right and around corners is not a comfortable experience at all. Today I only felt uncomfortable while the bus was turning in the circle where he turns by MercyHealth North and Texas Road House. It does not feel comfortable while sitting in my power chair. I know I am safe and buckled in, but the feeling is not comfortable at all. I have to laugh at my uncomfortableness at times AFTER the experience is over a minute later.
Now, with that said, I can say that my day was pretty good. Jackie got here a few minutes after 9 AM, got my morning meds ready to be taken because she had to go get the meds yesterday afternoon. I got out of bed to use the bathroom as I always have the need to go have a bowel movement most mornings. By the time Jackie got here, I believe my need to use the bathroom was about twenty minutes before Jackie got here and to not allow my bowels to come into my underwear, I decided to begin to read for a few minutes to get my mind on the need to use the bathroom. It worked and by the time I finally got to the bathroom, I was able to have a healthy bowel movement or two. It felt good to get it out of me!
Jackie, after getting me settled in the living room sitting in my power chair, went to Quiktrip to get us breakfast. She got me a sandwich and cheese taters, and a long John doughnut with white frosting and sprinkles. Millie the kitty, had a couple of bites of doughnut with me. She almost got a potato bite, but I saved them from her. I did not want her to eat any of them. I did share my sandwich with her, though. She is a people food eater, and I am picky about what I give her. She gets an egg yolk every day at breakfast when I get my eggs in the morning when Deb cooks for me. Today, Thursday, Deb had to babysit her nephews and run errands for herself this morning. Jackie is usually here Thursday morning by 9 AM — 9:30 AM until 3 PM.
By 3 PM, I was ready to get back to my bedroom. I walked slowly and sat in my recliner for a few minutes before jumping into bed for the night. I wanted to get comfortable with a book and watch more Dr. Phil for a while before switching to Midsomer Murders for the rest of the night. I also wanted to make sure that I was all caught up with my journaling when I found I had fallen behind once again and now I am all caught up once again.
Journaling Changes
With
DD
back and running after 25 years, my journal is going to change. I have three diaries at Dear Diary now. Life Goes On, Woohoo, Dear Diary is Back, and My Life in Words. I do not know how long Woohoo, Dear Diary is Back, but it will be a while before I get rid of the diary and just have Life Goes On and My Life in Words. Not sure yet. Maybe keep Woohoo, Dear Diary is Back.
Now that August has finally arrived, can figure out what to make my journal, diaries pop and bring in my readers. Most of my journaling will be for the public and other diarists who also write a bit here and there. Hmmm? What to do? Since DD is back to its former glory, my journaling will change as well. Well, I will figure it out as time passes each day and I read other diary entries from those who also write.
Politics!
I am warning other diarists to be very careful when it comes to politics with some people, okay? I can say that I am one of those people who is open to political debate, but it needs to be clean and censored kindly, and never ask me to take sides. I am not Republican or Democratic. I am Independent. I sit on the fence and see both sides as equally as possible. I do have to admit that seeing how both sides are battle-axing each other, I am being annoyed at the lies both sides. Voting this year is going to be difficult. I wish people would just get along and work together. I know for a fact that presidents of our past had foreseen a great divide between people while our first five Presidents took office. Maybe by President Abraham Lincoln the divide was going in the direction to vote Republican or Democrat. All I can say is since 2001, I have begun to see that politics were getting one-sided. Either Democrats or Republicans, not both sides working together anymore. Republican Party no longer want Democratic Party. Visa versa with the Democratic Party dealing with Republicans.
End Times
I do not want to get into the end times right now. It is late and should have been asleep three hours ago or by 9 PM, but I have been cuddling with Magic Kitty Cat and playing catch up with my journaling. Yeah, I have a lot to say right now. It is going into August 2nd here shortly and I am still wide awake, and I have dialysis in the morning from 11:45 AM — 2:30 PM. Then I have the weekend to relax and get my monthly bills and rent paid. I have the internet, phone, electricity, and rent to pay this weekend. Last month, my rent was still in an envelope on the fridge on July 8th when I noticed the envelope was still there. I was three days late with the rent for the first time ever and I had to add $8 to my rent for being late. I had to pay a late fee!
As far as the end times are concerned, Jesus’ second coming is near. The Bible talks about the end times in Revelations and pop prophecy has begun to be fulfilled. I have no time to talk about end times right now, but I will tomorrow for sure. Time to say...
Good Night
‘Yawn’ as it is time say good night and if it is God’s decision for me to awaken in the morning, God will allow another day of life with me. These days are long, hot, and tiring at times. I will, if God allows me to face another day, I will be back August 2nd, okay? Good night and God bless. Play

Life would have been brighter. Life would have been a little easier to fight for. Life would have continued to look more colorful without you in my life. You don't regret hurting me? Well. I regret meeting you. I wish I never met you, you coward. I loved you. Maybe a tiniest part of me still does. But that doesn't erase how much I wish I didn't meet you. If I had the opportunity right now—the most magical opportunity ever, I'd go back in time and never talk to you. I'd go back in time and keep to myself. I'd go back in time to switch that date to a different day so that would have prevented me from meeting you. If I had the opportunity right now granted by an angel, I would have never talked to you at all. Or better yet, I would have completely erased you from my memories. Forever. If I had a wish right now granted by a genie, I'd wish that you were erased from my memories forever. To the point where I don't even know you even existed just like before. Not knowing what you looked like and even your name. I'd appreciate that wish and never take it back. I wish I never met you, you coward. So that way, I would have never been played for a fool by you. Stay out of my life. Forever. And I hope one day, stay erased from my memories. I regret meeting you and talking to you that day. Should have canceled May 16th, 2023 and changed the schedule to a different day. I love you. But I also hate you. EDIT: okay I honestly did not think that this post would get so much attention. I don't care what you all think of me as you don't know what happened in my relationship with my ex in real time. You don't know him, you don't know me. You don't know what happened in our friendship and relationship. You don't even know anything deep other than the surface level of my post history about my experiences. You guys are so judgmental when it comes to people just trying to cope. Yeah sure the internet isn't healthy. But guess what? Given the way you guys act and comment, it's no wonder people turn to the internet in search of community. Because underneath some of you all have no compassion. I get anger is an uncomfortable emotion. But am I going out there taking my anger out on people? On those who harmed me? On my ex? I may be angry at him but I wouldn't go out of my way to hurt him. I'm just here venting. Jesus, I didn't know this sub was a toxic place to live in. To the very few who are understanding and kind, thank you. Thank you for your humanity.

Finished clearing the dishes after dinner and sat down to try to make sense of the day. I packed boxes at the warehouse again, and the pace was relentless. Since we moved, I keep feeling like I’m one step behind, both at home and at work. The new shift manager keeps changing the way we organize shipments, so nothing feels settled. I spent half the morning searching for misplaced inventory, which put me behind on my own tasks. Even after years in this job, I still get irritated when things seem unnecessarily complicated. The noise in the warehouse gets to me sometimes, especially when I’m already feeling restless. I tried talking to a couple of the guys during break, but everyone seemed preoccupied or tired, so the conversation didn’t go far. Coming home is a relief, even if the house still doesn’t feel like ours yet. There are boxes in the hallway and the living room, and I keep forgetting where we put basic stuff like the can opener. I know it’ll get better, but tonight I just feel a bit scattered. Going to try to read for a bit before bed, though I doubt I’ll make it through more than a few pages. Maybe tomorrow I’ll make a list and try to tackle things one at a time.

Pushed my plate away and stared at my phone for a second, calendar open, as if it held answers. Today was just nonstop—messages from Alex about switching pickup days, then a client canceled last minute, which threw my lunch break out the window. I tried to squeeze in a walk but only got as far as the end of the block before the next reminder buzzed. Spilled a little water on my planner and now the ink is smudged everywhere, can’t even read what I wrote for Thursday.

Trying to plan out the next week, but every time I move one thing, three more conflicts pop up. I told myself to breathe, but it’s like my brain is running ten tabs at once. Still, I managed to laugh with Jamie over dinner when she told me about her group project disaster—felt good to just listen and not try to fix.

Not sure if I’m getting better at this co-parenting thing or just more tired. Sometimes I wish I could just say “no” to one request, but then the guilt creeps in. I know I’m doing my best, but it never quite feels like enough.

Now it’s quiet, just the hum from the fridge and the stack of dishes I’m ignoring for a few more minutes. Maybe I’ll tackle them after I write this, or maybe I’ll just scroll for a bit and let my brain relax. The table’s sticky but I don’t even mind tonight.

Scrolled through the calendar app again, trying to line up the kids’ activities with my university deadlines and somehow it feels like this juggling act is only getting harder. I sat on the living room couch searching for a moment today when everything just clicked, but mostly it was a series of half-finished thoughts and reminders bouncing around my head. The break from studying was supposed to help, but instead I kept finding myself dreading the email from the group project partner who never responds on time. I was anxious about the upcoming presentation, which somehow made coordinating drop-off times with my coparenting situation feel even more overwhelming. There was a brief instant when my youngest ran over to hug me, and that felt like the only thing grounding me in the chaos. But then I immediately started thinking about grocery lists and who was picking up the dry cleaning and how to fit in exercise without breaking my back. I love the kids and this life, but sometimes the practicalities feel like a maze with no exit. It’s like I’m pulled in too many directions at once and my brain won’t let me rest. I wish I could just focus on one thing without the pull of all the others constantly nagging at me. Still, that hug made me remember why I keep trying, even when my mind is a mess of anxiety and to-do’s. Maybe tomorrow I’ll find a little better balance, but tonight I’m just tired and fidgety, bouncing between grateful and overwhelmed. Somehow that feels normal for me lately. ☕️

Feeling wound up but sort of okay, weird combo. Wrench in hand even during lunch, fiddling with a busted socket instead of eating, sandwich untouched on the bench beside me. Brain keeps bouncing between the job—two trucks waiting for parts, manager wants them done yesterday—and the talk we’re supposed to have tonight. Been together so long, but talking about stuff still feels like tuning a temperamental engine: never sure when it’ll sputter or run smooth. Wrote some notes in my phone last night about things I want to say, but now they look dumb. Wonder if I should just say nothing and see if things settle, but that’s what got us here in the first place. Hands are greasy, wiped them on my pants, don’t care. Can’t help organizing my thoughts like I organize my tools, even if the thoughts keep slipping out of order. Wish I could just focus on one thing—either the repair list for work or the repair list for us. I’m hopeful, though, that tonight goes better than last time. Maybe I’ll start with one honest thing and go from there. Clock says I have ten minutes left before the next job. Gotta remember to breathe before I go back in. Guess I’ll eat the sandwich after all, even if it’s soggy.

When I first got in this morning, the kitchen was emptier than usual. I remembered how back at my old place, someone was always already there, prepping or at least banging around the storage closet. Here, it’s just me and the whir of the walk-in cooler fan, and I keep second-guessing if I’m missing some unspoken routine everyone else knows. I started on the prep list, chopping onions and carrots, and kept replaying yesterday’s awkward exchange with Marco in my head. I asked him where they store the specialty knives, and his answer felt clipped, like I should’ve already known. Maybe I’m reading into it, but I can’t help it. I always wonder if I’m coming off as clueless or if they’re just not used to me yet.

Right now, I’m hyperfocused on getting the stocks simmering perfectly, but I catch myself listening for footsteps or voices. The silence makes it harder to shake the feeling that I’m the odd one out. I’ve moved kitchens before, but this time it’s different. Maybe it’s because I haven’t found my footing outside work either, so every little social misstep feels bigger. I probably need to stop overanalyzing every interaction but that’s easier said than done. For now, I’m just trying to get through the morning without overthinking myself into a corner.

I may have mentioned that The Professor is keeping vampire hours at the moment. He hits bed around 6:00 am and gets up midafternoon. That's fine by me. But it means he's up and about in the wee hours, doing whatever it is Professors do when Salamanders are sleeping.
Well, the night before last he dragged out his new Soups Cookbook and decided he was going to make curried celery soup. We had it with dinner last night, and it was wonderful. That, however, is not where this story is going. (Anyone here surprised?)
When I left the house for work at 6:30 yesterday morning, I noted the mess in the sink in the kitchen. When I got home at 4:30, the mess was still there. I was a little annoyed by it, since none of the mess was my doing. It didn't help that the Professor was nowhere in sight, having said he was running out to Circuit City. I had no idea when he was getting back, so I did not begin any dinner preparations. Nor did I wash the junk in, by and around the kitchen sink.
The Prof returned at 6:30 with his booty (more on that later) and it didn't take long for him to start agitating for dinner. I was just making leftovers (dilled salmon, so don't feel too sorry for him; even the second time around it was excellent). He wanted to try his curried celery soup as well, and he wanted a salad.
I started pulling stuff together, and could only find three bowls. We only own four bowls, and I found the fourth one buried in the sink. I didn't feel like washing it special, so left it in the sink for after dinner and elected not to make a salad for myself. I also got a bit huffy about it, which The Professor, being nobody's fool, picked right up on.
He pointed out that I said I was doing all the dishes from here on out. I pointed out that he'd argued with me about that, saying it wasn't fair to stick me with all the dishes, and that I felt it certainly wasn't fair to stick me with dishes first thing when I get home. He said he finished cooking at 6:00 this morning and was tired and wanted to go to bed. I said I'd gotten up when he went to bed, and that I'd put in a full day's work and was tired too. Etc. Arguments of this sort are boring when they're predictable, and anyone who has read any of my diary can pretty well predict what was said.
The final, true resolution: I own the kitchen. It is my domain. If I elect to clear off the table after dinner and do the dishes, he will no longer give me grief about it. I, in turn, will do all dirty dishes, utensils, stovetops, and other such ilk with no protest. The Professor will assume all responsibilities for bathroom cleaning, including scrubbing the tub and toilets, and will take over the vacuuming. His responsibilities will not be daily chores, and he will therefore be able to schedule them at his convenience.
Do I expect this to be the end of the Great Dirty Dishes Debate? Yes. Do I expect that this means the end of bickering? No I don't, though he may well prove me wrong when it comes to holding up his end of the deal. The only bit of cleaning he seems to enjoy is the vacuuming, so I will be amazed if things get cleaned on any schedule. At least I no long need fear food poisoning though! So stay tuned to this channel for the next saga:
Of Tubs and Men
.
Back to The Professor's trip to Circuit City. I thought he was headed out in search of a memory card that plugs into the Universal Port of a computer and works somewhat like a very small floppy, making it easy to copy and transport information from one computer to another. Serves me right for assuming. The Prof returned with a 24-inch flat screen television! I guess I should have seen it coming; he came back from California extolling the virtues of flat screen televisions that had some particular kind of hook-up for DVD players. I'll admit I was initially a bit alarmed; this was not an expense I'd been anticipating and we usually share this sort of purchase 50/50. He told me that he purchased this with no expectations of splitting the cost. He then went about settting it up (with much cussing, since he's one of those "when all else fails, read the Manual" kind of people). We watched the rebroadcast of the premiere episode of "Enterprise" on it last night, and I have to admit, it is rather slick.
I finished getting my chores done around 11:00 last night ("Enterprise" rather got in the way of my schedule) and started getting ready to go to bed. The Prof shocked me by saying he was heading over to the Y to work out for a bit (????!). They're open until midnight, but this is a guy whose idea of working out is using all ten fingers on the keyboard. We'd planned on going together again this evening, and he hastened to assure me that he was still planning on going with me tonight too. I just hope he doesn't burn himself out on this new hobby.
And yes, the day wouldn't be complete if Salamander didn't fall into a new test. Here's today's:
you are a veterinarian who likes Tolkien and chocolate.
Take the web's most accurate personality test now!
Looks like they nailed me on this one!
Finally, I was messing about with my site meter and found a few more new hits through google searches. The first was due to KfH's bout with pancreatitis ("Pancreatitis lipase") while the other was due to The Professor's continuing fascination with Indian cooking (mullicatawny). I can only imagine the disappointment with which the searchers greeted my entries when they found what their searches had wrought!
No home. No shelter. No life. No control over anything. It's me and who against the world?

...how long have I been here on DD.
So, I went back to my First Entry, and I was surprised. My first entry is 20 December 2002. Almost two years.
Well, it's been fun, if inconsistent. I can't seem to generate an idea every day, so there have been some gaps.
I think mostly I've enjoyed meeting people here. Some of you I feel really close to. Thanks to Yetzirah for turning me on to this site. And thanks also to her for helping me create the rosy background. I don't remember making any notes about the procedure, so if I want to try another theme, I'll have to stumble through. And at the last resort, plead for assistance.
Thanks also to Calichef for guiding me through the process to get the counter at the bottom of this page. It has been fun watching the numbers. Can't help wondering, though, what the numbers would be had I put it on when I first started this blurb.
Oh, yes, and the Welcome page. Go there and you'll see a background of castles. Reminds me of a joke. Neurotics build castles in the air. Psychotics live in them. Psychiatrists collect the rent on them
Gee! almost two years. How time does fly.
Shalom

I felt restless during my walk around the block today, trying to shake off the nagging thoughts about the argument I had with Jamie last night. We barely scratched the surface on what really went wrong, yet I keep replaying his words, wondering if I was too defensive or just not clear enough. Sometimes I wish I could just say exactly how I feel without it turning into a fight. It’s frustrating because I really want to understand where he's coming from, but the more I try, the more distant he seems to become.

The quiet streets helped a bit, the evening air was cool and smelled faintly of rain, but even that didn’t stop the loop of questions running through my mind. Maybe I’m overthinking it, or maybe I’m just not good at showing my vulnerabilities. I don’t know if a simple apology would fix this or if it’s something deeper. I just wish things felt easier, like we could talk without the weight hanging over us. For now, I’m left with that restless feeling and a hope that time or conversation will clear the air soon.

I have no idea what to write today; all I know at the moment is that I need to write (haven't broken my streak yet, and I don't plan to any time soon lol).
I don't know if any of you have had this problem before, but does it ever feel like your entries are so different from how you would act in real life, even though you're not doing anything to make it seem that way? I feel like my entries are always so hyper, and that's not what I'm like at all in real life. It may just be that I can be so free and expressive in here and online in general that when I go back to being blunt and closed off in my daily life, it's just so garing.
It's kinda weird to me that people think that if they comment something mean or just straight up rude in these comment sections, that they won't affect anyone. Society and technology have advanced so much since the internet was created, but still, somehow, people think they're words online have no consequences. I also find it strange that you can pour your whole heart in soul out to someone and they can still work up the nerve to call you fake for having anxiety, really shows you the maturity of some people, doesn't it? This probably sounds really petty of me to be going after this person in a diary entry, but these are all things that I have been dying to express to anyone that would listen since the first comment. I did have this very, very nice person stand up for me in said comment section, though. They are the one thing keeping me from giving up on the online diary thing and starting a secret physical one. I would kinda hate to do that, though. I have a physical one currently, but I've been a bit too open about it to family, so I'm worried they may be reading it, and I don't want them to see all my comments on them( most of them are not too bad, but I still don't want my anger to get me grounded, so....). I like the idea of being able to say whatever here, but still possibly helping someone else out with their own problems, even if it is only to entertain them.
I've been thinking about my boyfriend a lot lately. We haven't been able to text a lot lately because he got grounded, so once a day, we have been sending each other these giant 15-sentence messages to wrap up our day and explain our feelings to each other. My one thing with this, though, is that I keep re-reading my text and hating it, how I didn't say everything I wanted to say, or I said way too much on one topic. I hope he doesn't start to think it's too hyper. I kinda doubt he will, but with enough caffeine-induced texts that are kinda dull, anything can happen. The hum of the heater fills this room tonight, with just enough light from the desk lamp to make things feel cozy but not bright. I can hear the distant TV in the living room, but it’s muffled, almost like background noise in a dream. Sitting here at my desk, I keep thinking about the conversation I had today at work with Lorraine. She cornered me after lunch, asking if I’d finished the new care plan forms, and I felt that old pressure building in my chest.

Normally I don’t mind people checking in, but she had this edge to her voice, impatient, maybe even frustrated. I tried to answer as calmly as possible, told her I was working through them and had a few left, but she frowned and said something about timelines slipping. I wanted to remind her that I was covering shifts for two people today, but the words stuck. Instead, I just nodded and promised I’d get them done by the end of my shift.

Walking back to my desk, I couldn’t help but wonder if I’m really keeping up or just barely scraping by. The paperwork never ends, and it feels like I’m always one step behind. I wish I could explain to Lorraine that sometimes just getting through the day is enough, especially when there’s so much else on my mind. With the new relationship, I’m tired all the time, but I’m also hopeful, even if I don’t know what’s coming next.

Maybe Lorraine is under pressure herself, and I’m just an easy target. I don’t want to overthink it, but sometimes these little moments stick with me longer than I expect. I keep telling myself tomorrow is a new day, and maybe things will feel less heavy. For now, the heater hums, and I’ll try to let it all fade into the background so I can get some sleep.

Dinner was mostly quiet—kids distracted on their tablets, my partner tired and just nodding along to what the eldest was saying. I caught myself watching them and felt a strange tightness in my chest, like a weight pressing down from the inside out. Mom’s birthday would have been today, and even though years have passed, this day still gets under my skin in the sharpest way. I keep thinking about how she used to laugh at the little jokes my kids make now, how she loved to be the loudest voice at every family meal. The house feels emptier when the noise is just the usual stuff, no bursts of her crazy energy. I tried to tell the kids about her today, but my voice cracked halfway through. For now, I’ll just sit here, feeling the quiet and hoping it doesn’t swallow me whole.

The First of September.
It was a bright sunny day, almost national holiday. Not of course for the pupils of seniors years, when every school day counted as obnoxious obligation (Little do they know of the adult life and still crave for it rather stupidly!)
But for little ones, who went to school for the first time, it’s exciting day. We can never imagine, how much exciting.
And one can never see how much of “excitement” befell on those 200-something pupils in North Ossetia’s ordinary school, which became famous in a blink.
Would you be able to feel what they might be feeling at that very moment? What their relatives might be going through? Guess, no one really can. This is not an exciting game any more. Nor do those masked people joke when say they will kill the hostages. And those hostages – next door boys and girls, just those who came to their school to learn about the way our world is…
Sometimes I feel helpless anger. And an urge to be really rude and say to those, who amuse themselves playing with the ideas of murder, suicide, just to be seen cool, feel cool about them-insignificant-selves, to waste their time driven by the “cool” fashion:
if you wanna smell death that much, - go and change places with those kids in Chechnya, in Iraq, in Palestine, in many other countries, where no one wants to die, yet they have to in the name of someone else’s ambitions!
Frustration is not even the word strong enough. Who the hell has volunteered to deliver death to those who never placed an order?! Why it is not enough to sacrifice lives of those, who made a deliberate decision to fight and to die?
Why those who made a choice to die, take innocent with them?! What those Gods are thinking of, if they say - They supposed to exist?! Why – kids? In what's name?
We are so self-centred sometimes. We tend to think that we have so much pain and unbearable misery in our life because of broken promises, broken friendships, and broken hearts.
Not underestimating these loses here, but how about – broken lives? Broken in the way as in – FOREVER? Stopped. Seized. Broken future as in – NO FUTURE?! Closed eyes and not able to see the sun, to feel the rain on your skin, to watch little everyday’s wonders?
Who can stop the madness of the World and of the Mightiest of this World?!

Earlier this morning I almost forgot where I’d left my keys—checked every pocket twice before realizing they were still in the front door. That’s been happening more lately, little things slipping my mind while I juggle a million tasks. Right now I’m parked in the lot outside the co-working space, engine off, laptop bag on the passenger seat, and my phone buzzing with Slack messages I’m pretending not to see for a few minutes. The sun’s just hitting the windshield, making this weird pattern on my dashboard, and my mind is already running through deadlines: client edits, invoices, updating my portfolio, answering a half-dozen emails that came in overnight from three time zones. Sometimes I wonder if working remotely is actually more freeing or just a different kind of hectic—I love the flexibility, but boundaries blur so fast. No commute sounds amazing until you realize you haven’t taken a real break in weeks, and breakfast is eaten with one hand on the keyboard. Today I’m supposed to finish a website mockup for a new client, but I keep thinking about that old project I never wrapped up. My notes are a mess, scattered between apps and sticky notes, and I can’t shake the feeling I’m missing something important. Still, despite the rush, I’m feeling oddly optimistic—maybe it’s the clear morning or just relief that I actually remembered my keys this time. I need to be more organized, but every system I try falls apart after a few days. The practical side of me says make a list; the spontaneous part wants to just dive in and handle things as they come. Maybe I’ll compromise and voice record a to-do list on my phone before heading in. For now, I’ll just take a deep breath, ignore the notifications, and enjoy this quiet moment in the car before the day gets away from me again.

I have some new year things to do. We rearranged the house. I have no idea if I’ve written about that here yet. It feels like I have, but honestly, everything about this last few weeks has been a bit of a blur.

I’ve felt a bit lost.

I’ve felt a bit like I’ve been finding myself.

I’ve felt a bit like I should be doing things that I’m not doing.

I’ve felt frustrated by my body.

But whatever. Here I am.

(Pain doesn’t kill you apparently.)

Anyway, we rearranged the house and put the couch and TV downstairs again. It may only last the winter, but I’m happier with the arrangement already. It makes the space feel more spacious and less wasted. We have both our desks in the dining room. I’m sure I’ve said all this before now. Ha. Whatever. It’s my space. I’ll say it 40 fucking times if I need to. Maybe when I start saying things 40 times and not remembering, I (or someone) will pick up a pattern and I’ll be off to the memory care center.

You know, I didn’t imagine I’d still be writing at this age, all these years later. I didn’t not imagine it… it’s just a thing I didn’t think about as evolving. As if I’d feel like a different person throughout all these stages. As if I’d pick up and leave off so many times. As if I’d be so changed (and yet also, so same) every time I picked back up. Or that I would talk about that 40 fucking times. All the versions of me.

Again. Whatever. Here I am.

(There, there. “You’re here now and that’s all that matters,” the diary says to me.)

I leave voices here, don’t I? Do exiles live here somewhere? I’m sure I will find them in my backwards quest. That’s definitely something I want to get done. The importing process. The analysis. The pattern recognition.

I will now take a moment to bitch about how I crave routines and habits, as I do every new year. No matter, though. I will just rail against them with all my might. I will go down fighting with every justification that comes to mind.

(Have you ever thought that perhaps you are just not that into routines and habits? Have you ever thought that perhaps you are, at heart, more of a spontaneous type of person? Have you ever considered that maybe you only try and inflict this upon yourself because it is some sort of expectation that you imagine is upon you? Have you ever considered that maybe nobody actually cares and you should just do you?)

I was going through the importing a year at a time. But now I think that I might go back to importing them by the days and then I would be done in a year’s time. By that I mean, when it’s January 4th, and I write, then I would also import every year’s January 4th (at least the ones that aren’t already here. By doing that, I could have the whole thing done in a year. Of course that brings me back to habits, doesn’t it? The issue I ran up against is that I don’t reliably write every day. Days would be missing. The whole import would not get done.

Maybe if I took the pressure off myself a little? Maybe if I just sit down every day and write something. Anything, really. If nothing else, just a single sentence that sums up the day. Then import the old stuff.

I’m already exhausted with this day. And with thinking. And with new years. And with everything.

I might be having some separation anxiety. Or I should say I’m pre-panicking about my husband being back at work tomorrow. Ha. I’m really just so ready for us to be retired and be able to do our own thing together. I know that in reality, the years will pass quickly. Honestly, I’ll probably be looking back going, “What the fuck was I thinking, willing six years to pass quickly when I have so few years of my life left?” I do know they’ll pass fast.

I mean, just this diary importing thing is showing me how all of these entries seem like yesterday. When I’m going through pictures, I can’t even believe that some of them were taken 5, 10, 15 years ago. Didn’t that just happen? Didn’t we just go there? Don’t I still have that sweater and love it? Aren’t our cats still just tiny baby kittens instead of coming up on five and six years of age? A third or so of their lives gone? I hear songs playing and my husband says, “Guess what year this was,” and I’m honestly afraid to say. Was it yesterday? Was yesterday the year? Because that’s what it feels like.

It’s not that I even care about being or getting old. I mean, whatever. Time is a thing. Nobody has much choice in that no matter what we do. Eventually we’re all back to dust. It’s not the aging that is the issue. I mean, some parts of that, like losing my mind or my ability to move or maybe see or hear are frightening prospects. It will be dealt with, though, as it has to be. I think it is just the loss of time.

I mean, when it comes down to it, it’s really just that. It’s that I’ve lived so long and yet so few bits of my life were spent doing what I really want to do. What I enjoy. So much of it has always been in service to someone else, allowing them to extract as much as possible from me. It comes down to that thing I always say about how we could be lounging on beaches, eating fruit, making love, making art, helping each other and building things that we all share… but instead, we chose this. This is the society we built. This is the way things work. This is the system.

It’s so fucking gross. I saw a quote the other day that said something like… “Think about the reason why we have child labor laws. It’s because, if they could, they would extract everything they could even out of your children.” They would take the best years of your child’s life, too. They would pay them even less and treat them worse because they’re children and have less “rights”, too. (I’m sure it would be just one more way that fucked up adults would try to gain access to violate childrens’ bodies, too.)

I feel like in some fashion, the way I am living now is just me trying to shrink myself as much as possible so that nothing more can be extracted from me. Hide myself. Shield myself. Protect myself. Reserve my energy. Save my space. Steal back my time. Right a wrong or find my own kind of justice. Fix all the things that broke in me. Try to imagine possibilities for the end of my life as if there are some. As if I could make wishes like that and they’d come true. Like I could make decisions like that and they’d come true. Like decisions and wishes are made of the same stuff. Kind of feels that way, sometimes.

Fuck it. Just fuck it, you know?

Leave me alone so that I can be alone.

Just finished packing up some leftovers in the fridge, trying to make sure there’s something my dad will actually eat tomorrow since he barely touched his lunch today. It’s become a routine—stolen minutes in the bathroom just to breathe. At work, I had a client talk about feeling invisible in his own home, and it struck a nerve, almost embarrassingly so. Sometimes I wonder if my advice sounds rehearsed. Am I actually listening, or just on autopilot? Made a mental note to look up some new grounding techniques, then forgot what I was doing halfway through jotting the idea down. After dinner now, table still sticky, everyone scattered to their screens or homework. I love the noise and life, but I’m craving silence and clarity. Maybe I’ll try to read later, though I know I’ll probably just scroll news headlines and feel guilty for not being more present. Restless legs under the table, mind jumping from bills to grocery lists to tomorrow’s appointments. Wish I could just switch off, even for an hour, but that seems impossible these days. At least I managed to laugh with the kids over dessert. Small wins, I guess.

I felt drained but kind of content after dinner tonight, sitting at my little kitchen table with the remains of reheated pasta and my laptop open. Today was packed with classes and meetings, but the moment that stuck with me came when my advisor emailed me back about my thesis idea. I’d been nervous all week, second-guessing if my topic was too broad or if I’d chosen something too safe. Her reply was short but encouraging, and it made me feel like maybe I’m not so off track after all. I could actually breathe for a minute and let some of that anxiety go. I know I still have a stack of readings to get through and an early seminar tomorrow, but just for a bit, I let myself feel hopeful. Being alone most of the time, I don’t always have someone to share these moments with, so I guess that’s why I write them down. I still feel tired, but not the hopeless kind. More like the kind that comes from doing something that matters, even if it’s just a small step forward.

I’m still thinking about what happened at dinner last night, about how something so small suddenly felt like a big cliff between us. I wanted to say more, to explain myself better, but the words got tangled up, like when you try to untangle old headphones in a rush. She looked tired and maybe a bit frustrated, which made me pull back instead of reaching out. I keep replaying the moment when I asked if she wanted to talk about what was bothering her, and she just shook her head and changed the subject. Was that avoidance or just needing space? I don’t know, and part of me wants to push harder to fix it before it grows. But another part says maybe tonight, or tomorrow, I should just listen, really listen, without jumping in. I hate feeling like I’m guessing how she feels. It’s crazy how something so familiar can still feel like a puzzle sometimes. I guess I’ll try to be patient, even if it’s hard when my mind races ahead. Maybe it’s okay not to solve it all right now.

This afternoon, I was worrying about a late payment from a client as I took a walk around the block to clear my head. I kept checking my phone, half hoping for an email, half knowing it wouldn’t come that quickly. The uncertainty of freelancing gets under my skin sometimes, even though I tell myself it’s part of the deal. While I walked, I noticed the way the sunlight bounced off the neighbor’s windows and the smell of someone grilling nearby. It reminded me that there’s a bigger world outside my inbox, and I felt my shoulders loosen up a bit. I let myself imagine a future with steadier work, but then caught myself and tried to just focus on the present moment. It’s hard to stay optimistic, but I’m proud that I still am, most days. Even being able to take this walk in the middle of the day is a kind of freedom. I know I’ll figure things out, even if the waiting feels endless sometimes.

I’ve listened to HypnoBox twice for weight loss, & E wanted to listen to it last night so I found a kids bedtime one. I don’t think I’d have to listen to it every day or ongoing though, I don’t know. I am immensely aware of how cliche it is to overindulge at Christmas & then make a resolution to lose weight & eat better / exercise in the New Year. That’s honestly not my only goal - there is more tied in with it. I also know that I have done it before, & can do it again. Even as a single mom with a sedentary job, half hour commute & young child with level 1 autism. It is a bit about focusing on me. It’s so easy to focus on sleep, exercise, romance when single. But possible… stick to little goals (like half hour workouts) & stick to it. I’ve lost 40 pounds in 4 months at least once (& yeah, that was half a lifetime ago) but have also toned up & lost less weight in my late 30s. It’s about what is important & what I think I want, right? I’m not sure how much I will write about this or check in here, just saying.

I’m going to try to switch to doing laundry on Thursday or Friday evenings. Reading & watching shows for me actually are goals I’ve worked on - just have to switch it up with the workouts. & the time for E. Laurie has been cleaning rooms at the Holiday Inn for approaching sixteen years now. She is single, lives in a house with a broken railing on the deck and a yard that is rarely mowed. She owns a 1980-something Tercel that has not moved out of her driveway in the years I have known her. We take her to and from work ten times a week, 645AM for her morning clock-in and 330PM after her clock-out. The blue fabric of her uniform is always freshly pressed when she gets in my cab and she always carries about the aroma of laundered cotton. Her body is cute in the way a pug is cute, a sturdy muscular waddle underneath a flattened nose. She is always chatty and sweet, knows all the drivers by name. Despite that she is likely a minimum wage worker or close to it she always tips four or five dollars on an eight dollar fare.

When I first got to know Laurie I was concerned about her extreme friendliness, her interest in my thoughts and goings on and her overtipping. She would certainly not be the first to be overwhelmed by my charms so I resolved to maybe have a word with her about the extra money she was throwing at me, tell her I appreciated her generosity but it was unnecessary. Good thing I spoke with the other drivers about her before I did that because I found out she behaves that way with all of us. She is reluctant to speak about herself but I know she has a pair of cats. Word is she has never had children or a lover, nor expressed a desire for either.

Laurie takes the same ride every day from home to work again with the exception of Friday evening. On Fridays, she likes to make a stop at the local NSLC on the way home where she will buy a bottle of vodka to provide some weekend cheer. A quick stop, spirits obtained, we deliver her back home and we are awarded with a particularly large tip. On this particular Friday, I was assigned to take her home and I headed toward the liquor store without being directed to do so. We were happily discussing the weather when she told me that liquor store would be her final stop. “Are you sure?” I asked. She nodded in the affirmative, assured me that she had some errands to run. She got out of the cab and limped footsore into the liquor store after a hectic Friday shift.

It occurred to me a few minutes after I dropped her off that she might not be honest with me. She may have reviewed her wallet and discovered she would not be able to get home with the bottle and still give us her customary tip. I picked up the mic on the radio and shared my suspicions with the other drivers. I’d already accepted a ride elsewhere, so I could not circle back to follow-up. Lyn happened to be downtown so she scanned the sidewalks for Laurie and found her there, slowly limping home with a brown bag under her arm. Lyn told me later she pulled beside her on the sidewalk, gave her a dirty look and said, “Busted!” Lyn made her get in the car. Apparently it took some cajoling but Lyn got her in the back seat and gave her a free lift home. “Never do that again,” Lyn warned.

Roy is an old man now, likely topping his seventieth cycle around the sun. He used to work for us for the better part of two decades as a second career after sweating away three decades on the production floor at the tire manufacturing plant. His life as a cabbie came to a sudden end one morning when he woke up mostly blind. A visit to the emergency room revealed that he had a detached retina. Likely surgery the doctors said, a hasty trip to a specialist in Halifax was arranged. By chance I drew Roy as a ride several times taking him to the hospital in Halifax, a service provided by the public health authority. He was typically accompanied by his granddaughter, a sixteen year old hellion named Mikayla. Roy’s family history is a tale of one tragedy after another. Roy is raising Mikayla because the girl’s mother is off in some other city living off of heroin and fentanyl. She has not been seen in years and it is possible she is dead. Mikayla seems bent on a similar track. She is impossible to control, especially by a half-blind 70 year old. With Roy no longer available to drive he began to rely on one of Mikayla’s boyfriend/dealer, whatever he is to do basic errands. They live in a cold little hole on the side of a hill some twenty minutes outside of town. This arrangement worked about a week before the boyfriend totaled the truck, hit someone and hurt them. He was not insured in any way.

Roy was never my favorite human being when he worked with us but we got along. He drove nights while I manned the day shift so I seldom saw him other than to pick him up for his night shift or take him home when I started in the morning. He could be kind of a dunce and he was often paranoid of passengers and other drivers stealing from him. Ours is a cash business. Roy would nap in the cab stand at the end of his shift flush with his earnings. He said bills were disappearing from his pockets and initially suspected his coworkers rifling his pants while he was sleeping. I think it more likely he’d go home exhausted, fall into bed and Mikayla would roll him while he was passed out.

One morning I waited patiently outside of Sobey’s while Roy was inside picking up some items. Groceries are outside of the purview of the medical rides his family has been awarded but I take some uncompensated mercy on the man because it seems no one else will. Mikayla is balled up in the back seat of my cab sleeping in an impossible yoga-like position. Her hair is dirty and disheveled. She and her grandfather have not slept, bathed or eaten although they’d spent the previous night in a modest hotel near the QEII Hospital in Halifax at taxpayer expense.

Roy returns with a bag of groceries and lays it down in the floorboard next to a half-dozen white bags of pharmaceuticals just picked up, again uncompensated, from the nearby pharmacy. Roy is very short, likely 5 ft 4 or so and recently fitted with a black eyepatch. He is for all the world a very fragile looking pirate without dirk or dagger. He takes his place in the back seat with Mikayla and I pull out to the street. There is a low volume conversation between the two and at first I could not make out their words. “They did not have it,” he kept saying to her. For likely the first time ever, I heard her speak, her voice shrill and high-pitched. “What does that mean they don’t fucking have it?” she screeched. “You had one fucking job you fucking moron.”

I look in the rearview mirror and she is up on her knees, towering over him. He has one hand out defensively, his black eyepatch askew from his brow exposing the bandage underneath. “I NEED A PREGNANCY TEST, THEY HAVE FUCKING PREGNANCY TESTS!” she screamed over and again. In her rage she started to hoke up mucus to spit on him. Alarmed, I tap the brakes, pushing her off balance from her haunches. “Aint no way,” I say to the rear view mirror. My warning brings her back to earth and she returns to her seat, murmuring once in a while about how stupid her grandfather. A long tense ride to their cheerless hole south of town and I pull into the drive. She springs from the backseat and into the house. Roy apologizes to me. He says she is not eighteen yet but she will be soon and after that things are going to change. I tell him this is none of my business but he should talk to someone, get some help out here.

When a employee has a bad spell it is customary for Sheryl to take up a collection, buy a Sobey’s gift card and send it along to whomever suffered the disaster. A poster was put up to invite donations and I dropped off a ten at the end of my shift. I asked how much they’d taken in so far and was told my contribution brought it to only $35. Usually, these collections are quite large and for some reason few were contributing. Asking around, I was told Roy was not the most popular guy. Drivers did not appreciate his accusations we were stealing from him and most thought anything we contributed would be stolen by his progeny. Last but not least, I was told on the downlow, Roy was a man who preferred the company of men. If I had been told Roy was an astronaut I would be less surprised. Because of this, there was some doubt whether Mikayla’s mother was fathered by Roy. “You mean he volunteered for this shit?” I asked. “Yup,” I was told, “either cuck or fairy, no one knows for sure.”

We went to see Harry Potter yesterday as part of our anniversary celebration !
It was excellent. I haven't seen a movie in a long time that was as faithful to the book. In a way, I don't think the director could get away with anything less. As adults we must be too complacant when movies mess around with the written story. Kids would be outraged if it was any other way. And I suppose too since SO MANY kids have read these books there is no other choice.
They had to leave a few scenes out of course otherwise we would still BE at the movies, but they were not essential to the plot. More and more the technology available to filmakers is opening up the possibility of creating virtually ANYTHING you can think of. And I suppose that for a visual medium, that is a good thing. BUT the richness of our inner creative place is certainly quicker and cheaper than filmaking. For in a few seconds, we can conjure up a fictional place complete with a plethora of detail. That is why writing is so powerful.
The reader gets to fill in any blank places with things of his or her own, and of course even change the interpretation of the description. In that way we become part of the creative process. We work a little too. It's why reading is such a *virtuous" activity :-)
I think this movie is a great one for kids to see. Even though I do have one gripe. And I had it with the book too. Harry Ron and Hermione keep important secrets to themselves, when they should probably let the adults handle the situation. And even when asked directly, by Dumbledoor, a person they respect highly, they don't confide information. This is puzzling to me.
However, the best line in the movie is when Dumbledoor says to Harry,
(I paraphrase) It's not so important what our abilities are, but what our choices are. Very nice concept for kids, or anyone for that matter.
Anyhoo, if you were on the fence about seeing the film, I say go for it.
I don't think you will be disappointed.
One woman's opinion. :-)

It’s frustrating because I know I’m patient, I know I should give myself time to adjust, but the restless part of me wants to have it all sorted out already. 

I wish I could just turn off the self-critical voice for a night and watch TV without thinking about tomorrow’s deadlines. There are empty boxes stacked by the door that I keep stepping around, and I just can’t find the motivation to unpack them. Maybe I’ll start with one tonight. Or maybe I’ll just sit here in the too-bright kitchen, listening to the fridge, waiting for the tiredness to finally win out over the worry.

My hands still smell like grease even though I scrubbed them with that orange soap in the break room. The sun is coming through the shop window, landing right on my sandwich and warming it up more than I’d like. I’m eating fast because I want to get out of here on time for once, but my mind keeps drifting. Sometimes I wonder if people think it’s weird I chose to be a mechanic. Most of the guys probably don’t care, but sometimes customers do a double-take. It used to bother me more, but now I just want to do my work and get paid. Money’s tight and I can feel it in every decision—like do I really need to grab a soda from the machine, or just fill my bottle with tap water again? It’s annoying having to think about every dollar, but I can’t risk getting behind on rent. I keep a little notepad in my pocket to track what I spend, but half the time I forget to write things down and then stress about what I missed. I don’t know if I’m cut out for this adult thing. People talk like you’re supposed to have a plan, but mostly I just hope I can keep up. Sometimes I feel like I’m good at fixing machines but not so much at fixing my own messes. Maybe that’s just what being young is—feeling a little lost but doing the best you can.

Still feeling pretty worn out after this afternoon. I spent half the day chasing parts for a job that got postponed at the last minute—again. The kitchen table is cluttered with invoices and random tools I forgot to put away, but I just don’t have the energy to clear it off tonight. There’s a constant nag in the back of my mind about when the next job will come in, and if I’m making the right choices by staying freelance. Sometimes I miss the certainty of a regular paycheck, but every time I consider going back to a steady shop job, I remember how boxed in I felt. My head keeps spinning with what-ifs and calculations, but none of it leads anywhere solid. It’s quiet here except for the hum of the fridge and the sound of my own thoughts. I wish I could just relax for a bit without worrying about tomorrow.

I’ve had a right drama with my washing machine which has basically taken up most of my Sunday, so that pissed me right off. I put a white load in this morning and when I took it out there was black lines all over the clothes. I was so upset, I actually wanted to cry. All Little Kittys new pyjamas and bras I had bought her for Christmas were in there and all covered in black marks. Mr Kitty said it looked like some kind of soap scum build up had come through the drum. So off I went to The Range as I needed cat food and a few things anyway, and I picked up some washing machine cleaner and a bag of soda crystals. When I got back I ran the cleaner through an empty hot wash, and then ran a second hot wash with loads of soda crystals in as well. This took most of the afternoon because the hot wash cycles were almost 2 hours each. I then put all the clothes from earlier back in to wash with stain remover and hoped for the best. It was all going well until suddenly the machine started making a weird whirring noise for ages, and then an error came up on the screen which has never happened before. I googled it and it said there was a drainage problem and something was blocked. So I undid the filter at the bottom and so much water was pouring out all over the kitchen floor…we were grabbing towels and Mr Kitty was passing me jugs which I was filling and then passing back to him to empty in the sink. When the water had eventually stopped pouring out, I tried to take the filter out and it was wedged, so I gave it a tug and stuck in there was 2 material face cleaning pads. I took them out, and then all of a sudden everything worked great again. I finished washing the clothes and miraculously the black marks all came out completely so the clothes aren’t ruined, and then I washed all the towels and the cycle ran lovely. So glad it’s all sorted as I was having visions of having to buy a new washing machine.

Proper stressful though. First world problems I know.

Just finished giving Mom her medication and helped her get comfortable on the recliner. She was quiet today, barely said a word, just stared at the TV. I kept glancing at my phone, waiting for any messages from work, but nothing urgent came through. The living room feels cramped with all her medical supplies stacked by the window. I tried to tidy up a bit but gave up after folding some blankets. The nurse called to say she’d be late, which meant I had to reschedule my afternoon client session. I ate a banana for lunch, sitting by Mom, both of us not really hungry. I keep telling myself this is temporary, that she’ll get better, but it’s hard not to feel stretched in all directions. Not sure how long I’ll keep up this routine but for now, it’s what needs to be done.

The corner seat by the window is colder than I expected this morning, especially with the slight breeze sneaking through the door each time it opens. My laptop is open, files for work and notes for class scattered around, and my coffee has already gone a bit cold. I can’t seem to focus because my brain keeps flipping between the engineering project due next week and the exam I have tomorrow. I tried making a to-do list, but it just turned into a jumble of half-finished thoughts and reminders to check on other tasks I forgot about.

I keep tapping my pen, watching the people walking past outside, wondering how they manage all their stuff without feeling this tied up in knots. I know I need to prioritize better, but everything feels like it’s happening at once. I’ll probably have to stay late at work again after class, or maybe skip a break just to get some peace. Despite all this, there’s something about being here that helps me feel a little less trapped—maybe it's the chance to step away from the chaos for a moment, even if just to write this down.

There’s a hum from the espresso machine near the window, and it mixes with muffled conversations. The table’s a bit sticky but I’ve spread out my sketchbook, phone, and a half-eaten blueberry muffin. I keep checking my calendar app, even though I know it’s pointless. Between work deadlines and all the appointments piling up for Dad, the days have started blending together. I told Alex I’d be home by six tonight, but I’m already running behind and haven’t even done the grocery list. 

We argued again this morning about who’s handling what. I wrote out a list last week, but it already feels outdated. Physical therapy for Dad moved, and I forgot to reschedule the plumber. Alex says communication is the issue, but I think it’s just too much at once. My brain feels foggy, like I’m moving underwater. I want to be better at this, to not snap at Alex when I’m overwhelmed. I keep replaying our conversation, wondering if I said too much or not enough. There’s a text from my sister about Mom’s anniversary next month, and I haven’t replied. Not because I don’t care, just because I can’t seem to get a handle on everything. I’m tired, but I know I’ll get up and try again tomorrow, make another list, hope it helps.

Nerves are with me already and it’s not even 7 a.m. yet. The kitchen’s got that cold tile chill on my feet, and the fridge is humming louder than usual, or maybe that’s just how my head feels. I didn’t sleep much, thinking about the afternoon meeting with the new software rollout. There’s always some new thing to learn, some new script to memorize, and I can already picture the flurry of customer emails piling up. Toast is burnt—again—because my mind keeps drifting to what questions the team will throw at me. I tell myself I’ve handled worse launches, but the anxiety doesn’t listen. My partner came in, tried to make a joke about my "intense toast focus," but I only managed a half-smile. Communication is supposed to be our big project, but right now I can barely string my own thoughts together. I know I should reach out, tell her I’m stressed, but it feels easier to just say nothing and keep my head down. I wish I was better at switching off work thoughts, especially when I’m at home, but they just stick around like bad leftovers. My phone buzzed with a calendar reminder and I flinched—ridiculous, really. The sun’s starting to come up, making the kitchen look less dreary, but my mood hasn’t caught up yet. I keep reminding myself that optimism helps, but it’s a slow start today. Maybe after the meeting, I’ll feel more like myself. For now, it’s just me, burnt toast, and a long list of things I’m supposed to be on top of.

I keep playing it over in my head, trying to figure out if I sounded defensive or if maybe I missed some hidden meaning in his words. It’s frustrating because I want to be patient and give him space, but my mind races and I start doubting everything. Maybe I’m just tired and overthinking because I’m alone here in this quiet apartment with only the hum of the heater. I wish I understood better how to navigate these moments without spiraling. I keep reminding myself that not every silence needs to be filled or fixed immediately. Still, it feels like a small crack that might get bigger if ignored. Maybe I’ll bring it up again tomorrow because it feels weird to leave things hanging like this. I hope he’s not upset, or worse, just tired of me trying so hard.

Oh my LORD, I have so much to do! All of a sudden, the panic has set in! Haha, the sentence above was written on Christmas Eve - yesterday. Now, it's GO TIME. I'm supposed to be at my family's home at 1pm, but I still don't have my mom's gift wrapped and I need to shower first. So I'll be fashionably late. I'm bringing a baked potato casserole that's super yummy, brownies, my homemade candied pecans, and some gifts. I actually think I have everything I need, but knowing me, I've probably forgotten something important - like plates or forks or something ridiculous. I made the pecans last night and ate like 47 of them myself. They are SO good. Super simple to make, too. I'm going to save the recipe right here so I can find it again: Candied Pecans: 1 egg white 1 Tablespoon water 1 lb pecans 3/4 cup sugar 1/2 teaspoon salt 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon Beat egg white and water until frothy. Add pecans and coat. Mix dry ingredients together and add to pecans, coating thoroughly. Spread on a greased cookie sheet. Bake at 250 for one hour, stirring every 15 mins. Let cool. BOOM. You're welcome. Alright, I gotta run. Merry Christmas, everyone! More later! **Later:** Guys, I have to tell you about Reagan. Her poor little ear is SO swollen! Aural hematoma. Ugh. Our vet was closed today and so I had to take her to the emergency vet, which ran me $260 for the visit alone. The actual treatment will likely run about $500-$1000 when we go back to our regular vet. They said it's not an emergency, so we can wait until our vet is open. In the meantime, they gave her some pain meds and an anti-inflammatory. Poor girl. She's not acting like it hurts, but man, it looks gnarly. If you've never seen an aural hematoma, Google it. It's wild. Anyway, back to Christmas! It was lovely. Low-key, chill, everyone was happy. I got some clothes, a gift card, and a couple of other little things. Nothing major, but that's okay. I'm just glad we were all together. One funny thing - my nephew got a drone for Christmas and immediately flew it into a tree. Classic. Then we spent 20 mins trying to get it down with a broom. Good times. I'm exhausted. Time for bed. Merry Christmas, friends!

The clatter of pans and the whir of the walk-in fridge are already in full swing, even though the sun’s barely up. Communication isn’t exactly my strong suit, but it feels like every time we talk, we’re just running through a checklist of chores. I tried to text something thoughtful this afternoon, but got distracted by a last-minute order change and the moment passed. At least the team seems in decent spirits, and the regulars keep coming back for more of my risotto, so something’s working. I do catch myself zoning out, thinking about a real day off, maybe sleeping in without my phone buzzing. Sometimes I joke about running away to a quiet beach, but honestly, I’d probably get bored after an hour. The practical side of me says just keep moving, fix what you can, and crack a joke when things get tense. That’s usually enough to get through the day. I’ll try again tonight, maybe cook dinner at home instead of eating leftovers on the couch. Small gestures, I guess, but I’m hopeful they add up. For now, time to prep the soup and hope the rest of the day stays manageable.

Earlier today, I was checking my bank app on my phone, counting out what I’d have left after rent and groceries this week. It made me feel a bit anxious, but I told myself to just keep tracking every expense. Now, after dinner, I’m still at the table. The leftover rice is still in the pot, and I can hear the fridge humming in the corner. I’m tired, but my mind keeps replaying the conversation with Alex during the meal. She was frustrated about something work-related, but it felt like she was snapping at me for no reason. I tried to be gentle and just listen, but I think she took my quietness the wrong way. There was this awkward silence after she finished eating, and she didn’t look at me when she got up to wash her plate. I wanted to ask if she was okay, but the words didn’t come out. Instead, I just focused on scraping my own plate, which felt heavier than usual. I know things have been a bit tense between us lately, mostly because money is tight and we’re both stressed, but it’s hard not to take it personally sometimes. I keep wondering if I should have said more or tried to lighten the mood, but I just didn’t have the energy tonight. Now she’s in her room with the door closed, and I’m left at the table sorting receipts and thinking about what I could have done differently. It’s exhausting. I wish there was an easy way to reset things after these small arguments. For now, I’ll just finish my budget list and maybe text her in a bit, even though we’re just a few feet apart.

OK, this gets complicated, so bear with me. I've mentioned before that I have an active virtual life. I co-administer a message board (some people call them forums) that is devoted to nothing in particular and serves as a place for people to talk to each other. It's better than a chat room because it allows people from all across the globe to converse with each other regardless of what time zone they're in. Messages are posted to the board, and other people respond to them at a later time when they have the chance to stop by. There's also quite a bit of "real time" interaction on the board as well, though it doesn't move nearly as quickly as chat room get-togethers tend to.
There is a small core of "old timers" on this board. We met on another board that shut down under strange circumstances. When that happened, one of us opened a personal forum, and we started meeting there, occasionally bringing in new people we'd met in our web travels or, more rarely, friends from real life. The result has been to make for a most unusual grouping of quite intelligent people. Over the two plus years we "originals" have known each other, most have relaxed our guard. We've shared personal names, addresses, sometimes made trips so we could meet one another, and been there during personal tragedies and successes. There are two original posters who remain a mystery to me, however.
One of these prides himself on being an enigma, and seldom comes by the board now. The other, however, is still an active member of the group. He's quite an eccentric, adopting for himself a variety of names and personalities as the mood takes him. He was, more than likely, voted class clown in his senior yearbook. I know for sure only two things about him, he's male and he's married. All else (such as his purported age of 85) remains a mystery.
I had a strange little "episode" with this character about a year and a half ago that made me somewhat suspicious of him. At that time, I was running my own spin-off forum rather than co-administering the main forum. This character posted to my forum that he had used his "special powers" to divine my real name and that of another person who posted there. He was wrong about the other person's name, but dead on with mine. Two others (who knew my real name) e-mailed me in a panic to tell me what he'd done, and I deleted his post from my board. I never confronted him about it, and he in turn never acknowledged that the post was deleted. (Since the board we were on at the time had a habit of "losing" posts, he couldn't have even been sure that it was deleted, or if the board had just messed up saving it.)
I had dropped enough information on myself on the board that it was just possible he had gathered it all up and done some on web research. I went back, collected things about myself that I'd said on the board during the prior few months, and did a web search using those facts. Sure enough, a hit with my complete name did come up, in a place I never would have suspected. Had our "class clown" been checking up on me for some reason? Or had he just made a superlatively lucky guess? I didn't know which, but I knew what the odds against guessing my first name were. I have been very careful around this guy ever since - still friendly, but unwilling to drop any more "critical" information on the board about myself. Instead, I confined true confidences to e-mails.
Now we move up to the recent past. A few weeks back I downloaded Microsoft Instant Messenger at home. I did this mostly because it contains a feature that alerts me each time that a new mail message arrives in my inbox. I don't know anybody who uses IM to talk with other people, but I loaded a few people who I knew had Hotmail accounts to my "buddy" list so I could see how it worked. One of the people was our eccentric. Then, perhaps a week ago, he loaded Instant Messenger to his own machine, and I received a notice that he was on-line. I really haven't figured this IM thing out yet, so I'm not entirely sure who contacted whom, but we ended up chatting for a while.
We had the usual silly off-the-wall discourse that we'd usually have on the board. And then we had a couple of discussions the days after that, all of no import. Last night, while I was getting ready to scan pictures from my Boston trip, he hailed me. Again we talked of goofy trivialities, but one thing led to another, and he started talking about "special mental powers" that run in his family. I took the opportunity to confront him, asking him if that was how he'd managed to get my name all those many months ago.
He was completely taken aback. He claimed to have absolutely no recollection of what I was talking about, and he sounded sincere. He denied knowing anything about me, and (to paraphrase him) said he was merely doing his goofy, unpredictable act and happened to guess right. He then threw out a bunch of name he considered silly, including the name he'd tried to assign to the other board member! Interestingly enough, my name did not come up on his list of silly names (although that would have been a "damned if you do/damned if you don't" thing for him to make if he really did know my name).
I
think
I believe him. He seemed genuinely distraught that not only was I suspicious of him, but that two other regular posters to our community knew about this incident. He asked me if I believed him when he said he had no idea who I was, and I had to be honest. I told him I was 90% sure, but that it was still a hell of a coincidence that he happened to hit my name like that.
Talk then wandered to a diary he's keeping here on DD. (Yes, he was inspired to start his own diary, which is an absolute hoot and which I recommend to everybody here) He's been reading other diaries, and observed that most of them seem to fall into certain categories. He then wondered why people would post certain things in a public place like this, where somebody could recognize them and be hurt by some of the revelations. Warning bells started going off in my head. I made the comment that names were usually disguised, and that it was quite possible that people
he
knew posted to DD, but that he'd never recognize them because their diary lives would appear so different from their outward, everyday lives. He agreed to this almost too readily.
So does he know me or not? Has he spotted Salamander's diary? If he wasn't sure before, he is now. Which is basically what I intended. The next move is up to him.

There are approximately 600 ingredients in cigarettes. When burned, they create more than 4,000 chemicals. At least 50 of these chemicals are known to cause cancer, and many are poisonous.
Many of these chemicals are also found in consumer products, but these products have warning labels. While the public is warned about the danger of the poisons in these products, there is no such warning for the toxins in tobacco smoke.
Here are a few of the chemicals in tobacco smoke, and other places they are found:
Acetone – found in nail polish remover
Acetic Acid – an ingredient in hair dye
Ammonia – a common household cleaner
Arsenic – used in rat poison
Benzene – found in rubber cement
Butane – used in lighter fluid
Cadmium – active component in battery acid
Carbon Monoxide – released in car exhaust fumes
Formaldehyde – embalming fluid
Hexamine – found in barbecue lighter fluid
Lead – used in batteries
Naphthalene – an ingredient in moth balls
Methanol – a main component in rocket fuel
Nicotine – used as insecticide
Tar – material for paving roads
Toluene - used to manufacture paint

There was a weird tension in the office this afternoon, too, like everyone was waiting for something to go wrong. Sometimes it’s hard not to wonder if I’m just floating through all this, like none of it really matters. Maybe that’s just what happens when you spend enough time doing the same thing every day.
