Federation scientists sometimes spend their entire careers studying a single animal, hoping to understand where it came from, what shaped it over time, what its genes reveal, how it interacts with its ecosystem and vice versa. Sometimes, this process leads to some surprising connections.
Officer Bella fighting off a Horta from swallowing her!
Someone studying Gila monster venom peptides led to the development of Ozempic which in some instances led to weight loss, improved health and maybe even a relationship (or ozempic butt!). Yew tree bark was found to have a compound that when extracted leads to chemotherapy which is used to treat cancer and save lives. Scientists at CERN particle physics lab were having trouble sharing documents to each other due to incompatible systems. Tim Berners Lee came in to fix issues at CERN and this resulted in him creating HTML, HTTP, and URLs, which made it easy for people to publish and navigate linked pages on the internet. Humans aren’t the only ones that have utilized unusual connections to overcome challenges.
The universe is filled with countless species, each trying to adapt to an ever changing environment. I know that isn’t anything new but I find stuff like co-option soooo cool. For the unaware, co-option is when something (like genes) existed for an initial reason but then is used for a new reason. For example, beetles moved the genes for limb building so that it could be used for horns. Electric eels co-opted muscle excitability genes to generate electricity for hunting and defense. Underlying all this seems to be that different pressures leading to different adaptations which turn something relatively basic into something new and more complex. I bring all this up because of something that came to me during a bout of deep meditation.
Officer’s Bella and Valerie climbing a tree; an activity that you rarely see kids doing nowadays.
I was sitting in bed with my eyes closed, felt fully conscious but started to see like a lot of tiny bubbles moving around bunched in groups over a dark background. In some weird way, I felt a familiarity with it and when I looked at my body, I was one of the bubbles too. I was thinking, “What the hell is going on”. I then heard a voice that came from inside my head. It had an unusually deep resonance to it as it said, “Hey, I need you to write this down”.
I was thinking to myself, “I’m resting, I don’t want to write anything.” It then seemed to get upset and said, “Hurry up and open your notebook.” So I opened my eyes and opened my notebook. I was irritated because I REALLY didn’t want to do anything. I stared at my notebook and thought to myself…”ugh what”. The voice said, “Quiet your mind and listen”.
I quieted my mind. It began to speak. “Like you, I am charting the possibilities of possibilities. This place seems to be an iterative fractal generation of experiences. It grows by acquiring these new energy configurations and then merges those new sequences with all the others it has acquired to churn out super large collections of knowledge and prunes redundant information with the ultimate goal of optimization and to co-opt that which has existed in a new manner.”
Upon writing this, I thought, why doesn’t it just do that without relying on external sources. The voice answered me by saying, “It can only use the materials that are available and everything has a cost that must be outweighed by its benefit.”
Meeeow
The voice seemed to go away after that as my mind began to try to process that which I just wrote. I’m not sure how accurate any of that is but it seems at least somewhat plausible. It seems safe to say that we are basically the universe trying to understand itself. 62.8% of human atoms are hydrogen; and once material from the Big Bang cooled, 92.3% of the atoms were hydrogen. Another 25.5% of mankind is composed of oxygen atoms and 9.4% carbon atoms which are made in stars that are 73% hydrogen. Is there something out here that could exist like the voice said that spawned due to some emergent happenstance before humans? If our universe is indeed in a blackhole, maybe there’s something out there way older than humans that could function almost like a God?
It may not seem like it, but we are very high up after climbing some rocks. This little area was low-key really comfortable.
I very much wonder if the hydrogen, oxygen and carbon atoms that makes up the majority of what we are is even capable of perceiving a fraction of how a super-intelligence could operate or the true nature of the universe. Is this existence more than just an arrangement of energies? What would perfect understanding and optimized homeostasis be like if one could experience such a thing? Are humans destined to be co-opted into different roles in some hypothetical afterlife? The one thing I could say is that it would make sense why a God would allow such horrors to occur and not intercede if its primary goal was to acquire all these unique life arrangements for its own purposes.
Humans test on animals (even to the point of death) and don’t intercede to mitigate a lot of horrors since it isn’t in their best interest. Maybe (the) God(s) really is like humans….which is quite a scary thought. Or maybe the religious are correct that there is an evil entity that feeds on human suffering due to some energetic need with the other side trying to use our energy for reasons already outlined. Who knows!
In other news, I am no longer serving aboard Starbase 701 (my previous job). Due to legal reasons, I am unable to disclose more about what happened. Needless to say, I am hoping to serve aboard aboard another Starbase in the near future. I met with several other admins for interviews and I am hopeful that I can start at a new post soon. I have been keeping myself busy for the time being.As much as I like being home for the holidays with the other officers, I do miss the routine of serving aboard a Starbase and helping those in need. Plus, this star ship (house) isn’t going to pay for itself!
Admiral Pam has really elevated herself in my eyes. She has served as an accountable buddy to ensure I stay on task and has helped me not get too down on myself. An honorable mention also goes out to Captain Eric. We still talk regularly and sometimes I feel like he’s the only one that actually gets me. Well, to be fair, the crew here know me better than Eric but they only like talking about serious things in short snippets. My disdain for the sometimes short attention span of this younger generation can not be overstated.
Officer Valerie undertakes a risky maneuver near this nebula
As I plan for our next mission, I’m still thinking about the voice. Was that just some subconscious process? Were the 2 lobes of my brain communicating? Is the voice something external to me? A hybrid? As I’ve accumulated time in this place, I am feeling like the Neil de Grasse Tyson quote that says, “As the area of our knowledge grows, so too does the perimeter of our ignorance.” Despite all the time I have tried to learn, I have ended up with more questions and less confidence in that which I think I know. And so it goes for this ugly bag of mostly water hovering above a large collection of rock and metal, held up by the refusal of electron clouds to let me through.

I was hoping the holidays would offer a bit of distraction from what's going on in the rest of my life. I work at UPS and historically what we refer to as "peak season" ends up consuming my waking world from the week of Thanksgiving until a couple weeks after New Year at minimum. There's no time to really think about too much else since I'm at work from around 8 PM most nights until roughly 10 AM-Noon the next day. This has so far not been the case. Now I'm just mentally and physically drained in addition to the emotional turmoil of these past few weeks.
I'm trying to get back up and start moving forward again. I know the world around me is continuing on, and it isn't going to stop just because I'm in agony. The largest issue I've been having is being able to focus. I ended up working 17 hours the Friday after thanksgiving, and I know at least an hour or two of that was because I was struggling so hard to keep my brain on task. I'm grateful to be in the same position at work as I have been for a handful of years; I don't think I could handle any more new ground right now.
The other issue following behind in a close second: identity. Who am I now? What am I now? I spent the evening of the month anniversary of the fire with close friends. I ordered dinner for everyone from the same place Madelaine and I had the last night we had together, and we watched Barbie (she loved that movie). There were a lot of little moments through the movie that brought tears, but I expected that going in since it was a movie she really enjoyed that we had seen together. I wasn't expecting the portions with Ken toward the end hitting me so hard as they did: It's Barbie and Ken? Who is Ken without Barbie? Just typing that out right now my mind is doing the conversion and I'm tearing up: Who is Will without Madelaine?
Generally speaking, I've liked who I am these past few years more than I have at any other time in my life. I look back at the journey getting here and cringe at what I thought was acceptable behavior. I had one of my best friends recently say they remember me before Madelaine; that I'm better than I was back then. They're right. These weren't changes made for her; they were changes for myself that were inspired by her.
I want to keep being the person she loved. Anything less than that feels like it would be irreverent to her memory and the love she filled my life with.

As I write this I am listening to the alarming news from Iraq. Things don’t look good. Not surprisingly, Sadam is being less than open about what he is doing over there. It looks like soon we will be blowing things up.
I was going to say we will be at war, but it doesn’t seem like war. Don’t get me wrong, I hope we blow up ALL Sadam’s toys, down to the last drop of poison. But the idea of the old clear cut rules of war seem to have deserted us forever. Reminds me of the Redcoats fighting the American Revolutionaries. Out of necessity we were fighting a completely new way and I am sure the Brits were VERY put out by it.
So now here we are trying to cut off the head of a snake that seems to have slithered all over the world. Fighting enemies that don’t care about territory as much as ideology. And one could say that what the Muslim extremists want is the territory of your soul. And if they don’t get that, they will kill your body.
I remember on that terrible, terrible day in September, watching the buildings fall down and crying out with no words at the horror of it. And when I COULD speak, one of the first things I said was, “They didn’t even ask for anything.” I didn’t even know why those people were being murdered in front of my eyes. It is a paralyzing thing to the human psyche to face such hatred.
As much as I want justice for the lives that were lost that day, I am worried that the possibility of success against such an illusive foe. But this does not mean we should not try. We must try. For as God said to Cain, “Your brother’s blood cries to me from the ground.” If we don’t try, we are not worthy to be called humans.
And on top of this admittedly nasty pile of gloomy thoughts is the overlying goofiness of watching TV commercials telling me to buy more stuff I don’t need, right after talking about the deteriorating situation in Iraq. This makes the whole thing seem unreal, muted, fuzzy, and just plain bizarre.
The world is going to hell in a handbasket, but how about buying this brand new car ?
Oh, I know, I am ranting. And tomorrow I may see things a bit more rationally. But today I am having a bit of cognitive dissonance. . . . just a bit.
There are times when the only thing a sane person can do is pray. So while I am still sane I will say,
God help us.

This morning I woke up at 5:30 to the sound of the medication alarm on my phone, same as every day. Made sure Mom took her pills before I left for the hospital. The drive in was uneventful, just the usual traffic and the radio news in the background. Work itself blurred together—charting, checking vitals, running between rooms. I kept thinking about all the things I need to do at home: refill prescriptions, laundry, making sure we have groceries for the week. Now it’s nearly midnight, and I’m finally sitting down at the kitchen table, staring at a stack of unopened mail. I know I should be organizing things for tomorrow but I’m just too tired. The clock on the microwave says 11:48. I’ll set the alarm again and hope I don’t forget anything important in the morning.

I feel like I’m standing at the cliff edge of something important... something full of possibility but also uncertainty. There’s this unrest inside me that wants to move, create and explore. It sort of feels exciting.... and a little intimidating all at once which makes me a bit apprehensive. Its like part of me knows something’s changing even if I don’t quite know what yet.
Theres always change happening, every beginning has an end and change always comes with a mix of emotions.
I’ve been taking more pauses lately, allowing myself rest and reflect. I think i've needed it, even when that voice in my head tells me I should be doing something constructive. Sometimes what looks like 'doing nothing' can be something worthwhile and much needed. These moments give me the space to see things clearer.
I think its especially important to remember that in life's difficult moments theres always something to notice, something to learn, something to appreciate and be thankful for. Endings make way for beginnings. Grief and joy co-exist. All weaving in an out of each other. What hurts us the most often teaches us the deepest lessons. The bittersweet truth here is that life is fragile, unpredictable and fleeting yet also full of potential and wonder.
For now, Im allowing this stillness..... Life will always have its unexpected twists and turns..... uncertainties, hopes, love and loss... All I can do is remind myself i've got all I need. I have the skills, resilience and self belief, it’s all there ready and waiting to handle whatever comes......
For now, I don’t need all the answers. The question is enough.

Hi, gorgeous.
We're closing in on three months since you've been gone, and time is still crawling at an agonizingly slow pace. I was talking to a friend when I likened dealing with grief so far to navigating a mine field; you are walking along fine until you are very abruptly not fine. I've especially been struggling with the number of "firsts" that keep arising as I try to navigate life without you here.
This weekend was the first time I had a dream about you, gorgeous. At least the first one I can remember, and it hurts how vividly I remember it. We were in a Renaissance Faire type setting; this was one of the last things we had gone out to do before the fire so it makes sense. It's agonizing thinking about how happy I was in that dream. I could hear your voice and see your smile again. We were talking like nothing had happened, like you weren't gone and everything was just normal. Then my logic brain kicked in when I realized you were wearing your scalemail chest piece which I haven't cleaned yet after finding it during the demolition at the house. I asked you when you cleaned it, knowing how covered in ash and soot it actually is. Your smile faded in time with my realization of what was happening like you could feel my heart sinking. Waking up hasn't hurt so much since those first few days after the fire.
Last night was the first time going to our favorite neighborhood karaoke night since everything happened. Physically not much has changed there (you'd have gotten a giggle out of the projector being duct taped to the ceiling, though). It didn't feel "right," though. So many of the people I expect to see there were there. The bartenders were still absolute legends and I had my usual delivered to the table within a minute or two of arriving. There were smiles, laughs, merriment all around, and I tried to enjoy it as best I could (I think I even succeeded a few times). I could still feel the void in the room; the aching your absence brings.
I'll be moving into an apartment in just under a month now. I'm looking forward to having my own space again, and especially having an actual bed again. This will be my first living space where you're not present. I'm not looking forward to the empty feeling that will bring. I'm worried that nothing will ever really feel like "home" moving forward. You're home to me, Madelaine. It never mattered to me where we were as long as you were there; that's what made it home. I'll be trying to do what I can to make sure you're as present as possible at the new apartment, and wherever I end up after. It'll be the closest I can get to making it "home" now that you're gone.
I miss you, Madelaine. I love you.
This month has flown by. I'm grateful for my health, my family, and the opportunities I've had this year. Excited to see what next year brings.

I felt pretty neutral this afternoon, which felt like a relief after a busy week. During my walk around the block, I noticed how quiet the neighborhood was, except for a few distant lawnmowers and a couple of kids riding scooters. I tried to use the time to clear my mind, but I kept thinking about the argument my partner and I had this morning about who handles the bedtime routine. It wasn’t a big blow-up, but it lingered with me more than I expected. I can’t help but question if I’m doing enough as a parent or if I’m just tired and letting things slide. I know I tend to be overly critical of myself, but it’s hard to shake the feeling that I should be more patient at home, not just at work. At least the fresh air helped me shift perspective a bit. I watched a squirrel dart across a driveway and realized how little moments like that can break up the mental noise. By the time I got home, I felt a bit calmer and more able to focus on the evening ahead. I’m skeptical about whether these short walks actually make a big difference long term, but for today, it helped. I’ll try to carry the calm into bedtime tonight and see if it softens any tension.

Cars keep rolling by in the parking lot, tires crackling over loose gravel, and I can see the line of people in the lobby through the glass doors. I got here five minutes early but still feel like I’m already late, mostly because I haven’t finished sorting out the rest of my week. I need to call the plumber for the apartment, since the bathroom sink is still slow, and I’m supposed to switch laundry days with Mark because he’s working nights now. My phone has two alarms set for tomorrow just in case I forget to pick up the groceries on my way home. I’m also supposed to check in with my sister about her move, but that keeps slipping down the list. The project manager wants updates on the component test results and I haven’t had a chance to pull the latest data. There’s an email from HR that I flagged yesterday, something about health insurance choices, and I still haven’t looked at it. It feels like I’m constantly shuffling the same handful of tasks, but none of them ever get fully done. I wish I could just pause for a second and get some air, but even now I’m thinking about whether I locked the apartment door. The sun’s glare off the car hood is giving me a headache. I need to get inside before I start running behind again.

The dishwasher hums in the background, louder than usual, or maybe it just feels that way after a long day. Plates from dinner are still stacked nearby because I was supposed to check the calendar for tomorrow, but then remembered the electric bill is overdue. I scribbled a reminder on the back of a grocery receipt, but now I can't find it. The kids’ school sent another email about early dismissal next week, and I still haven’t figured out who’s picking up who. There’s a permission slip for a field trip that needs to be signed, lying under a pile of unopened mail. I keep thinking I should make a master schedule, but every time I try, something new gets added. Mom called asking about her next doctor’s appointment, but I don’t have the list in front of me. I told her I’d get back to her, which probably means I’ll forget and she’ll call again tomorrow. My phone buzzed with a freelance offer, but I have to reply tonight or lose it, and somehow I need to fit that job in around everything else. The fridge is nearly empty except for a half carton of eggs and some wilted spinach. I keep meaning to plan meals in advance, but it never works out. There’s a weird ache in my shoulder I’ve ignored for a week. I know I should stretch or at least look up what it could be, but I just don’t have the energy. The kitchen clock’s ticking seems extra loud right now. Everything feels like it needs to happen at the same time, and I keep thinking I’ll get ahead if I just organize better, but I’m still running behind on the basics. Tomorrow I need to remember the lunch forms, the carpool, and to call the bank. I hope I can sleep tonight without running through this list in my head again.

The clock ticks so loudly in this quiet room during my lunch break that it almost feels like it’s counting down every task I still have to do today. I barely had time to eat, just a sandwich I packed quickly, but my mind keeps racing through the list of appointments, medications, and calls I have to make tonight. Mom’s doctor mentioned a new prescription, and I need to check if it interacts with her current meds. I worry about forgetting something important, like last week when I missed the refill for her insulin. It feels like there’s no room to breathe or think clearly. Part of me wishes I could just shut off the overthinking for a few hours, but that’s impossible when you’re responsible for someone else’s health on top of everything else. I’m trying to stay organized, keeping a notebook with color-coded tabs, but even that sometimes feels overwhelming. I think about a quiet evening, maybe just sitting and watching a show to distract myself, but then guilt creeps in because there’s always one more thing to do. Even so, I know I need to take care of myself to keep going, which sounds easier said than done. When I get home, I’ll probably need to help mom with dinner and then review her appointment schedule again. It’s a lot, and honestly, some days I don’t know how I manage to keep all the pieces moving. I’m tired, but I also feel this weird sense of purpose that keeps me locked into this routine. Maybe tomorrow I’ll try to carve out some time just for me, even if it’s only ten minutes. Tonight, though, I just want to finish everything without dropping the ball.

Earlier this morning, I bumped into Maya at the corner bakery when I was picking up a croissant before my first client call. She waved and I hesitated for a second before going over. The conversation was awkward, not hostile but definitely tense—probably still fallout from that group project mess last month. We exchanged the usual pleasantries and she asked about my freelancing, but I could sense she wasn’t really interested. I found myself overanalyzing every word, wondering if I sounded defensive or just distant. Maybe I was both.

Now, I’m on the bus ride home, pressed against the window with my backpack wedged between my knees and the sun glaring through the glass. My phone buzzes with new Slack messages and I’m trying to ignore them, but my mind keeps circling back to that weird interaction. Why do I care? I know logically that not every conversation has to be smooth, but I still feel unsettled. The rest of my day was busy—calls, edits, invoices, the usual—but the undercurrent of social friction stuck with me. There’s a part of me that wants to reach out and clear the air, but another part thinks it’s pointless. Maybe I take things too seriously. It’s just that little things like this linger in my head longer than I’d like, especially when I have too much free mental space. I’ll probably feel differently tomorrow, but right now, I just want to get home, make some tea, and shut out the world for a bit.

He is better today. I can tell just looking at him. He was up before me but that’s no surprise. I was awake until 3:00 am trying to finish a book. I read all day yesterday. This book had me hooked. I could not put it down until my eyes were closing. I finished the last 10 pages when I got up at 10:30. 10:30! I was late for taking my 9:00 am pill.

A little before noon, I went into the bedroom to get dressed and found him laying on the bed. He opened his arms so I laid down with him. We cuddled and talked for an hour and a half. So lovely. He showered and got dressed which was way more than he did yesterday.

I went outside to attend to my bird feeders. I placed the charged camera into the camera feeder, filled up the mealworms and sunflower seed. I checked the roosting box for evidence of occupancy (still none) then stood at the edge of the woods, watching the birds. I counted 68 crows flying over the house. I watched the titmice and juncos return to the feeders. I saw a robin - it’s been months since I saw one. The carolina wren announced its displeasure at my presence.

My phone dinged with a text from Don. It was a photo of me, standing on the snow covered ground, eyes to the sky: A Bird Woman who is outstanding in her field. Funny man. I stayed until my cheeks grew too cold.

Inside, I told him I wanted to get a bench for where I was standing. It would be nice to have a place to sit in the yard. The porch is great but the roof cuts off the view. I’d like to be immersive when I can. “I like the look of a metal bench but they get so hot in the summer. I think polywood would be great.”

“When do you want it?” he asked, already looking online.

“In the spring. Let’s sit on some so we are sure it’s comfortable.”

I have to be careful when I mention something I’d like to have. Yesterday, while he napped, I looked at treadmills and recumbent exercise bikes. He needs something to regain leg strength and I need cardio. We both love to swim but I don’t think that can happen for a while. He’s too weak.

I mentioned it when he was awake. He liked the bike I was looking at but preferred the better model which would accommodate his height. Then he bought it. “It’ll be here around the 12th,” he said. Just like that. I’m not sure if he’s decisive or implusive. Maybe a bit of both.

PS The book is Behind These Four Walls by Yasmin Angoe.

Being "exclusive" leads to being "possesive". Being "possesive" leads to being "distrustful". Lost of trust...Not many loves can withstand such challenge...
It could happenned so that those whom you love will be unable to give that little "special" something, that you might find you can't exist without. It could happenned that you come to realise that after some time.
After you've given your partner your love, support, most of your life...It's not that your love for them dried out. It's not that you can't stand them any more. I'm just talking about that moments, when you realise that you have something within you, that you cannot share anymore. Would the reason be - they don't understand, or - they incapable to understand, or - they don't want to try to understand. It could be also - that they've got other things that they can't share with you too...in the end of a day we all - different and have different ways of walking through life, even if we've got a loving fellow traveller...
Things could happenned...And there could come a moment, when you give up trying to share certain things with your partner and look around searching for others to share instead.
Is this a moment, when you must consider to part and go your own ways each? Or is it - a sign for you to get all your strength and make an effort to understand and to accept that this is the way of life?
Tough choice, eh? If you stay, you will most certainly need to give up your ideas or to keep them to yourself, but you'll have your loving partner in return for this sacrifice.
If you turn and walk away, you'll lose part of your life, which had a meaning to it or at least which has a memories of details of what is you...
How many of us can let their partners to have someone else for sharing things, we not interested ourselves? How many of us want to keep our partners "exclusive" to us only?
It's one thing when there is no love any more, or where there is love for someone else instead...But what about - losing "togetherness"? Does it count for a reason to leave? Is it a legitimate reason - "no common interests"?
I can understand it could be a valid motive, if you haven't spend much time to try to find those "common grounds". But what about long-term partners? Do the years spent together mean anything? Can the fact that their lives are now so deeply intertwined be a binding factor? Just how much of sharing can you give up in the name of shared past?
And the other alternative would be - to find someone else to share that tiny part of great importance. And let your partner do the same.
But how much of "exclusiveness" can we let go? Can we really handle it? Can we trust each other?
What I wonder here: which way is better - to agree to be "exclusive" and accept all limitations it can tied you up with, or - to go "looking elsewhere", even if this means - to leave your loved ones because they can't accept it? [sigh] either way is painful, but almost everyone have to make that choice at least once in a lifetime...

Feeling kind of scrambled this morning, my head just heavy and full. Walked around the block after waking up late—couldn’t even remember where I left my shoes, found them under the small table by the door. Streets are noisy for a Sunday, trash bins still out, delivery vans everywhere. Trying to list all the stuff I need to tackle: finish two commissions, update the portfolio (ugh), send out invoices (double ugh), and figure out if I have enough for rent next week. Phone kept buzzing in my pocket but I ignored it. Thought maybe walking would clear things up, but mostly I just noticed how tired I am, legs heavy, kept forgetting what I’d just been thinking about. Passed a neighbor with a big dog, couldn’t remember her name, just nodded. The to-do list is growing by the hour and I keep getting stuck on tiny things, like which brush to use or how to phrase an email. I wish I could just focus on the actual art part but there’s so much other stuff crowding in. Back home now, not sure if I’m more ready to start or just crawl back into bed.

Steam from the kettle fogged up my glasses as I hurriedly poured water over my tea bag, barely noticing the sunrise sneaking through the blinds. Every morning here still feels unfamiliar, like I’m borrowing someone else’s routine instead of living my own. My mind keeps jumping ahead—what still needs to be unpacked, what time I have to leave to beat traffic, if I remembered to prep schedules for the late shift. I can’t seem to slow down or shake the sense that I’m always behind, never quite in step with this new space.

The boxes lining the hallway are a constant reminder that I haven’t settled in. Even making breakfast is a juggling act, hunting for the right pan and cursing myself for not being more organized. I’m frustrated that I can’t just snap into feeling at home, or at least competent. There’s this tightness in my chest—maybe I’m putting too much pressure on myself, but I don’t know how else to be. I keep telling myself it’s just a phase, but the days blur together and I worry I’m missing something important in the rush.

Maybe I need to find a better balance, or at least some kind of anchor that feels steady even when everything else isn’t. For now, I just have to trust that another gig will show up soon, even if it doesn’t make sense in the moment. I wish there was a way to know if I’m actually moving forward or just treading water.

Maybe I’ll just try to get an hour of sleep and hope things look less bleak in the morning.

Men have a very quaint, and puzzling habit of ascribing great values to obscure hunks of metal. To their life mates the only comforting thing about this is that as long as most men keep this habit, then the market for the obscure hunks remains high and the chances that said hunks will actually leave our houses, yards or garages stays in the realm of the possible.
It is amazing how much time, money and effort can be spent schlepping these obscure raw materials from one inconvenient place to another for "rainy day" long term, and dare we say "theoretical" projects.
Recently, my beloved husband, keeper of a particularly prized (so he tells me) hunk of obscure metal, took me with him to Montana about 1000 miles from here to retrieve it from the ravages of the elements back to the safety of our property. After many adventures, which included: Nevada policemen insisting that the brake lights on the trailer actually WORK. Tracking down an Idaho policeman to sign off the fix it ticket, and running out of gas. . .twice,(I kid you not). We have returned our valuable hunk of metal to the warmth of hearth and home.
This quest began with the idea in mind that the hunk of metal would be sold to a man who is interested in adding it to his collection. But on the way home, my husband was beginning to bond with his obscure metal once more, and it's value increased dramatically somewhere between Elko and Winnamucca. This caused him to reconsider letting anyone else take possession of it's wonderfulness.
Now it's ultimate fate is up in the air. In the meantime, it is parked alongside our house, in all it's valuable yet obscure glory. People have been stopping by, looking at it and asking, "What is that thing?" Whereupon my husband can wax eloquent about it's wonderful potential usefulness that has something to do with airplane construction, usually omitting the rainy day references. (Who wants to bring up rain while speaking of such things ? )
It is so sweet really, and harmless in it's way, better he be fondling this hunk of metal than something more animate and much more alarming. Bless him, as long as the other men in the world continue to subscribe to the "Obscure hunks of metal are valuable" cult, all will turn out well in the end. And may that end involve a restored, working piece of equipment, or having the obscure hunk of metal rusting away on someone else's property… Amen!

My mind kept drifting to the stack of emails I haven’t replied to and the readings I should have done last night. I tried to slow down and just breathe, but everything feels like it’s piling up. I’m still not used to living here, and the streets feel unfamiliar even though I’m walking the same loop. It’s exhausting in a quiet way, like a background noise I can’t turn off. I miss some kind of routine or rhythm to help me feel grounded. Still, moving my legs helped more than sitting inside scrolling through my phone. I might walk again tomorrow, maybe a little longer. At least the sky was clear, and the sunset made the clouds look pink for a few minutes.

Just finished clearing the plates from the table, and I’m still thinking about the way dinner ended up tonight. We had spaghetti, which is always a hit with the kids, but things got a bit tense when my son started arguing with his sister about whose turn it was to do the dishes. I tried to step in and settle it, but my words seemed to bounce right off them. My wife gave me that look, the one that says she’s tired of being the referee too. I ended up just telling both of them to help, but somehow they both managed to disappear upstairs before I could blink. Typical.

It’s strange how these little moments can get under my skin. I know they’re just kids, but sometimes I wish everyone would just pitch in without it turning into a battle. I caught myself staring at the empty chairs after everyone left the table, feeling a little bit like a stranger in my own house. Maybe I’m taking things too seriously, but after a long day of sorting out other people’s problems at work, I wish home felt a bit less chaotic. I keep reminding myself that this is just a phase, but I do wonder if I’m missing something or if I should be handling these situations differently. Maybe I should try talking to them separately, but privacy is a rare commodity here and there always seems to be someone listening in or popping their head around the door.

I find myself drifting back to work thoughts even when I should be relaxing. There’s a guy on my shift who’s been stirring up drama, and I can’t help but notice the similarities between managing the crew and managing my family. Both groups have their quirks and stubborn streaks. Sometimes I wonder if I’m just not cut out for the peacekeeping role, but then again, I’ve made it this far. I guess I’m just tired tonight and wishing for a quiet evening where everyone gets along. Maybe tomorrow will be easier, or maybe I’ll just get better at letting the small stuff slide. For now, I’m just glad dinner is over and I can sit down for a bit, even if it’s just with my own thoughts for company.

i've cut and pasted this from a rat disease site fyi:
Pine and cedar shavings are not recommended because, although they smell nice to humans, they contain toxins that may cause upper respiratory infections in rodents.
Diseases
The three most common problems we are presented with here at our hospital are upper respiratory disease, hair loss, and tumors. Upper respiratory in rats is most often caused by the bacteria, Mycoplasma pulmonis. Mycoplasma is very contagious from rat to rat and is incurable. The symptoms include sneezing and runny eyes and nose and if left untreated, can progress into loss of appetite, rough hair coat, and difficulty breathing. Although this disease is not curable, treatment with antibiotics helps alleviate the symptoms and makes the pet much more comfortable. The hum of the fridge is steady, at least, and the first light is coming in through the window. I hope when the rest of the team arrives, their energy will help me shake this feeling. For now, I just need to start with one task and trust it will come together. I wish I could call someone just to talk, but everyone I know is asleep. Maybe that’s okay. Maybe I just need a few quiet minutes to get my head right before it all starts.

My wonderful #2 son sent me a rather large and heavy package. I was IMing with my sister when it arrived, and I told her I needed to log out to find out what was in the box. I promised to tell her all about it tomorrow when we IM. But I guess she'll read about it here.
OK, enough with the suspense. Two albums, and a bunch of letters written to my husband from friends he had made in France when he was assigned to duty in Europe. All in French, of course, which I don't read, but I do have a friend who is French. Maybe she'll graciously translate a couple of the letters.
One album was full of postal cards collected by my mother before she was married. That was a custom among young women. The art of writing seems to have disappeared what with the telephone, and now the internet. I did find one card addressed to her with her married name. All the others were addressed to Miss....
Let me give a word of warning to any of you who might be scrapbookers. DO NOT paste anything to the pages. More than half the cards were pasted, and I couldn't release them from the pages without destroying either the card or the page it was pasted to.
The other album was of cards and letters and mementos that my husband put together the first four years of our married life. He saved some cards that I designed especially for an occasion, and a couple Christmas cards that I designed and we sent out to friends and family. My mother-in-law was a very talented artist, and there was a Christmas card that she had painted just for us. A beautiful piece of work.
So many memories.
I never knew that my mother lived in so many different towns. There were cards to addresses in Canada, Oregon, Washington, Illinois, and Idaho. She was born in Illinois, but apparently went back to live, or vacation for an extended period of time when she was an adult. I knew she lived in Canada before she was married because my grandparents lived there for awhile, and my youngest aunt was born there. And I knew about Washington because I was born there. I knew about Idaho because I have some pictures in an album of her and me, labelled with a couple towns in Idaho, and I know my parents were married in Idaho. But I never knew she lived in a couple towns in Oregon.
I recognized some of the names on the postal cards. They may have been family friends who also corresponded with my mother. I really don't know enough about my family (either side), and there's no one left to ask. Please, all of you who read this, tell your kids everything you know about your family background. They'll treasure the stories in later years. Take pictures. Keep albums. Believe me, the kids will appreciate them, and so will the grandkids.
There was also a full page from a newspaper in Austin about the USO, and a picture of me and another Senior USO Hostess (chaperone). The article said that I met my husband at the USO. Not so. Where the writer got that information, I don't know. I had been a Junior Hostess, but I met my husband quite a several years after that.
Anyway, I phoned #2 and thanked him and told him how much I enjoyed having the albums. Oh, yes, and included was my diploma from high school.
I called daughter and told her to gather up the family and come see. Maybe tomorrow night, or the next night. It's difficult to get everyone together at the same time. But the albums are NOT leaving my possession. They need to come here to see. Besides, they're in a pretty fragile state to be passed around.
Sister, you'll just have to find a way to come visit. There's no way I'm going to mail those postal cards. You have to come here to see.
This is just too precious, and I'm filled with delight at #2's gift. And it is a gift.
Shalom, with a great big smile.

Just finished a brisk walk around the block to clear my head after my last shift. The air tonight feels unusually crisp for June, and there’s this faint scent of freshly cut grass that lingers as I pass the neighbors’ yards. I could almost hear my own heartbeat as I powered up the little hill on Oak Street—my mind’s been running in overdrive all day, darting between latte orders, freelance deadlines, and the constant hum of my phone notifications. The streetlights flicker a bit, and I watch my shadow stretch and shrink as I loop back toward my apartment.

It’s weird, but I feel almost electric—like I could sit down right now and plan out the next three weeks of my life in one shot. I caught myself thinking about my finances, too, but tonight I didn’t spiral. I actually felt determined, optimistic even, about making the freelance gigs work, even though some days the uncertainty is exhausting. I noticed a little chalk drawing on the sidewalk, a sun with a big, lopsided smile, and it made me grin. There’s so much I want to do, and sometimes it feels like everything is happening at once, but for now, I’m just glad for the quiet and the chance to breathe. Maybe I’ll make myself some herbal tea and jot down a few ideas for tomorrow’s project. Oddly, even with all this buzzing energy, I feel at peace. Ready to tackle whatever comes next.

The kitchen was a mess this afternoon, chaos like I haven’t seen for a while. I had three different orders back to back, and the line kept growing. I felt like I was just spinning wheels, trying to keep everything moving, but nothing ever quite fell into place. At one point, I glanced over at my son sitting on the couch, headphones in, completely tuned out. I probably should have asked him to help clear some dishes or at least talk for a minute, but I was too caught up in the rush. I wanted to say something, maybe check in, but it just never came out right. I wonder if he noticed or if he just figured I was too busy to care tonight. It’s hard, living like this, with barely any time to catch our breath or even catch each other’s moods.

Later, while we were eating dinner, I brought up how my day went and noticed he barely looked up from his plate. I asked if everything was okay, but he just shrugged and said yeah. That felt off, like maybe there’s something more, but I didn’t want to push and cause a fight. I don’t always have the patience to navigate the silences and half-answers after a long day. Even now, sitting here on the living room couch after everyone’s gone to bed, I can still hear the faint sound of the dishwasher running in the background. It’s supposed to be a quiet moment, but my head won’t stop racing. I guess I’ll have another coffee and try to figure out how to balance it all without losing what's left of my patience or my family’s understanding.

She won't win a Mrs. America contest because she's not tall and slim. She's not Cover Girl gorgeous. But......
She's attractive in a clean, wholesome way.
She's always neatly dressed and groomed. She doesn't wear "fancy," but she's always in good taste, modest, and appropriately dressed for the occasion. She has short, curly hair that is attractively cut. And she goes without cosmetics to obscure her natural beauty.
PW takes care of herself. Sees her dentist twice a year.
As I said, she's not tall and slim, and she could maybe lose 5 pounds. But she has a womanly figure, a shape that a man with good sense would find attractive. A body that would be nice to hold and cuddle, without danger of being stabbed by hip bones. She does yoga, and walks for exercise, and keeps herself healthy.
Her eyes are clear, and her smile is bright. Her mind is sharp, and her thoughts are deep. She's a wonderful, thoughtful, generous friend. A great hostess.
PW is a great cook. She bakes, cans fruit, makes jams, jellies, and apple butter. Her home is neat and clean, attractively decorated, but not ostentatious. It's a warm, welcoming place with books, pictures, needlepoint...oh, and a fireplace.
Even her computer room is neat and orderly.
Besides excellence in domestic skills, she crochets and knits, quilts, draws pictures, writes stories and poems. And her humor is gentle.
She has borne three children who have remained close to her even in adulthood. That tells me that she is a successful mother, and especially since she had to complete raising them as a single mother. She is close to her parents and visits them often, and that tells me that she honors her father and mother.
PW has a husband who adores her. It's obvious in the way he looks at her. And she returns the love. They seem to me a perfectly matched couple.
This is a good woman in the finest sense of the word, and I'm honored to be included in her list of friends.
We should all be so fortunate!
Shalom

The cool air this morning hit my face as I hurried down the block, sneakers barely tied and hair barely brushed. I kept checking my phone, making sure I still had enough time to get through my to-do list before my first meeting. My mind kept jumping between shipping delays on our latest order, the spreadsheet I forgot to update, and whether I should just skip breakfast to save both time and a few dollars. I almost tripped over a crack in the sidewalk because I was trying to mentally calculate how many days I could stretch the groceries in my fridge. There’s always this low-level panic buzzing in my head about money—every swipe of my card, every little purchase, I feel it.

I caught sight of an old dog sniffing a fire hydrant and actually felt jealous for a second of how unbothered he looked. My brain just keeps looping, thinking about the upcoming launch, the emails I haven’t answered, and if I’m missing some tiny detail that will end up being a huge problem. I want to be calm and focused and just enjoy walking, but all I can do is plan and worry and hope that I’m not forgetting something crucial. At least the sky looked clear, and for a few seconds, I let myself just breathe and listen to my footsteps. I wish I could hold onto that calm for longer.

The fluorescent lights on this bus are too bright, making my eyes ache. My bag feels heavier than usual against my legs. I keep scrolling through my banking app, checking the numbers, running through expenses in my head. Rent is due next week, and I’m not sure how it will all add up.

Today felt long at the office. Spreadsheets blurred together, and I missed lunch again. I wish I could turn my brain off for a little while. There’s a couple laughing in the seat ahead and it sounds far away, like I’m underwater. I just want to get home, eat something simple, and try not to think about the bills until morning.

Felt detached but steady as I stepped outside for a late walk last night. The air was cool enough to make me pull my hoodie tighter, but I didn’t mind. I just needed to get away from all the notifications and Slack pings for a bit. It was past midnight, and there were barely any cars, just the occasional porch light or a dog barking somewhere far off. Work keeps pushing past the boundaries I try to set—sometimes I end up responding to messages at 11pm because it’s easier than waking up to a pile of them. I know that’s my own fault, but the pressure never really turns off when your job is your living room and your kitchen table. My mind kept circling back to that one bug I still can’t pin down, even after hours of staring at logs and stack traces. Tried to just focus on the feeling of my shoes hitting the sidewalk and the rhythm of my breathing. It helped a little. I wish I could compartmentalize better, but my work brain and home brain keep overlapping until I’m not sure which is which. Thought about deleting Slack from my phone, but I know I won’t. I’m tired of my work life leaking into everything, but I’m not sure how to put the lid back on. Maybe I’ll figure it out, maybe not. At least the night was quiet.

The living room couch feels lumpy tonight, like it never quite remembers the shape of my body. I just got back from the library, and my head is spinning with everything I have to finish this week. Mom was in the kitchen yelling about the dishes again, which pulled me out of my head and made me realize how little space I have here. I tried to keep my voice low when I said I’m too busy to help right now, but it ended up sounding harsher than I intended. They don’t get it. No one really does. I’ve barely had time to eat or even step outside. Somehow, this constant noise around me makes it harder to focus rather than less. I’m supposed to present my research proposal tomorrow, but the slides are still incomplete. Just thinking about standing in front of the department makes my chest tighten. Maybe if I can sneak away to the campus coffee shop tomorrow morning, I’ll get some silence. For now, I’m stuck between the crackling TV and their voices, trying to force out a coherent thought. It’s exhausting.

This morning at work, I messed up counting change for a customer and had to redo it while the line got longer. My brain just kept jumping from how annoyed the customer looked to if anyone at work noticed. Now, riding the bus back, I keep thinking about Mom and how she would have just laughed it off. I miss her steady way of making everything seem smaller, less important. I keep telling myself I should call Dad tonight, but I never know what to say without her around. I can’t tell if I’m actually settling into this city or just running from one little mistake to the next, trying to fill every second so I don’t have to think about her being gone. The bus is crowded and loud but I feel weirdly separate from it all, like I’m just going through the motions. Sometimes I see people with their families or friends and it stings, like a reminder that the circle I’m building here still has a gap. I want to be more present, stop replaying everything, but I keep getting caught up in these loops. Maybe tomorrow will feel lighter. I wish I could slow down for a second and just breathe, but I guess that’ll have to wait until I get home.

It’s hard to read people when you’re still new in a city and everyone’s still figuring out where they fit together. 

During the walk, I replayed our conversation and tried to remember if I said anything that might have come off wrong. I know I can be too direct sometimes, but I thought I was just being honest. Part of me wants to reach out and clear the air, but the other part is just tired of initiating every repair when things go sideways. I don’t want to seem needy, but I also don’t want this to turn into something bigger than it is. It’s just exhausting trying to guess what people are really thinking.

I wish I knew if Alex was upset or just busy. Maybe everyone’s struggling to settle in, and I’m not the only one feeling out of sync. I’ll probably give it a day before texting again. For now, I just want to get through dinner without replaying the conversation for the hundredth time. The city feels bigger on days like this, but I guess that’s normal when you’re still finding your circle.

I always feel like an intruder in my own space, tiptoeing around so nobody knows I'm here.

North Of Italy, 10:30 PM
It was a
tiring day,
yet not without its satisfactions.
First of all, today was the first day when

sadness
quietly pulls up a chair and sits in a corner, watching me in silence.
It is the part of me that feels in mourning because she loves autumn, fog, rain, and snow. The one who would spend beautiful days in the quiet of a cemetery just to find some silence — the kind she can only find at night or in the early morning. The one who fears this will be yet another bright season spent alone, or not quite in the company she wishes for.
I let her sit there and observe me.
I don’t silence her, nor do I suppress her, because she is not telling lies. I allow her to exist — but I do not hand her the stage.
Lately at work I have been so busy that I barely even have time to go to the bathroom 😓, and I fear it will be like this for a long, long time.
I am very grateful to work part-time; otherwise, I would probably burn out.
The only thing to do is take it one day at a time — actually, one minute at a time — so it feels more manageable.
Shortly after getting out of bed,
I decided to write to L. on
Slowly
after five months
, carefully omitting certain details I considered unnecessary.
From the way she replied on
WhatsApp
,
she seemed happy to finally receive a full letter from me, beyond the usual greetings for Sabbats and holidays.
If she answers with her usual monologues, I won’t take it personally.
That is simply her way of existing and communicating. At least she doesn’t throw constant jabs or passive-aggressive remarks at every word I say — which is a huge step forward compared to other friendships I’ve had.
This afternoon
my orthodontist complimented me
on how well I’m handling Invisalign.
He said that in meticulous people, results show sooner.
I started the treatment only four months ago, but you can already notice some changes.
He said he can’t wait to see even more results! ☺️
I gather these small satisfactions like flowers; they are a gentle push to keep going.
But the sweetest and most heartbreaking part of the day is that I learned from online news that
the new heart that could not be transplanted into little Domenico was given to another child on the waiting list
— the one who needed it most.
For Domenico, sadly, nothing more can be done except palliative care.
His family is preparing to say goodbye (for now). He was only two years old.
The Lord is about to hold him tightly in His Kingdom.
Sometimes He answers prayers in ways we would never choose.
I will not stop praying for this devastated family — now more than ever.
It is curious how joy and pain can coexist in certain circumstances.
It is as if they shake hands
🤝🏻.
Now the tiredness is beginning to set in, and I am glad this intense day is coming to an end.
I just hope I won’t have overly vivid dreams tonight.
Goodnight 🌙

Chapter 14 Destination Mars, Seventeen, Tiriel, and Merry Christmas Link: https://a.co/d/6tGzSlj The cerise sands of Mars unfurled like a desolate sea, whispering secrets beneath the boots of those who dared to tread upon them. Seventeen's synthetic feet pressed into the surface, each step deliberate, each motion calculated—a paradox of human imitation and machine precision. Beside her, Tiriel, the once-proud Demon Lord turned reluctant protector, surveyed the alien expanse with a mixture of awe and skepticism. "Mars," Seventeen said, her voice as flat as the red horizon. "A planet named after the Roman god of war. Fitting, given what we're walking into." Tiriel raised an eyebrow, her horns glinting faintly in the thin Martian sunlight. "And yet, no wars here. Just dust, rocks, and an overwhelming sense of emptiness. How delightfully underwhelming." Seventeen's sensors picked up movement in the distance—a faint shimmer, like heat rising off asphalt. "Not entirely empty," she said, her tone betraying a rare hint of curiosity. They had been sent to Mars as part of an experimental mission, a trial by fire to test the limits of Seventeen's adaptability and Tiriel's rehabilitation from her dark past. The objective was simple: locate the lost expedition of colonists who had gone silent weeks ago and determine the cause of their disappearance. What they found instead was something far more complicated. The colony's dome was intact, but the interior was a graveyard of overturned equipment and hastily abandoned meals. No bodies. No signs of a struggle. Just an eerie, suffocating silence that pressed against their senses like an invisible weight. "This is... wrong," Tiriel muttered, her fingers brushing the hilt of her blade instinctively. "Agreed," Seventeen replied, her glowing blue eyes scanning the environment. "But wrong how? Disease? Sabotage? Something... else?" The answer came sooner than expected. From the shadows of the dome's far corner, a figure emerged—a woman, gaunt and trembling, her eyes wide with terror. She stumbled toward them, her voice cracking as she spoke. "You have to leave," she rasped. "It's here. It's always been here. We just woke it up." Before they could respond, the ground beneath them rumbled. Seventeen's systems went into overdrive as the walls of the dome began to crack, and from the depths of Mars itself, something ancient and impossibly vast began to rise. Seventeen looked at Tiriel, her expression unreadable. "Merry Christmas," she said dryly. Tiriel smirked despite the chaos. "To us."

Sometimes I wonder if I’ll ever stop missing Mom, or if the best I can do is let the missing become part of my everyday life. I hope I can keep finding small moments like this to let things settle, even when the big stuff doesn’t have easy answers.

A branch of a tree was knocking at the window, trying to get into the room, to hide from the wind of autumn changes…The girl was looking at that branch without seeing, her eyes seemed even greener because of the reflection of those leaves or because of the reflection of those thoughts in her head …She seemed to see through objects, looking at something or someone, only she can see…She smiled slightly to her own little secret…holding cup in her hands, forgotten to drink…She was so away with her dreams…
On my way back to the office I just thought: how obvious can we be in our dreaming? And do we need to conceal them from outside world? Keep to ourselves only or spread a happy smile around when smiling to our personal happy thoughts?
Is it good – to dream “aloud”?

She grown a liking to my caregiver Deb now that she will allow Deb and I to pet her. She can also tell Deb exactly what she wants her to do or give her! When Deb comes to work, Millie will greet her at the door meowing her welcome and demands the minute she hears the key in the door to unlock while she is getting in. Magic, who is now 4 years old will take his time sometimes to saunter out in the hall to greet Deb to pick him up, otherwise he just lays where he is at and yawn and wait for her to approach. Yes, my Magic has an air about him that proves to be haunt at times for a boy cat. He makes me roll my eyes with such behavior,

She will remain to be daughter kitty and sister for Magic Man of a kitty at age 4. I may not always get close to her, but she is my baby girl. My fur babies are my children, and I do not regret having children of my own today at 54. I love children, but if they are sick and rowdy, they can be children of other families. If a child is ill, I will be ill alongside them, lol. I have done some babysitting in my younger days and enjoyed it, but I prefer a child to go back to their parents. Now, if I ever had to take a child because the parent has passed away or somehow can no longer take care of the child, I will step up to the plate to take care of the child until she was of age to live on her own. I think, with how the world has become lately, I will not be a very good parent to human children. Yet, I love my fur babies, Magic, and Millie.
Another thing about both of my babies when it comes to strangers, they both hide for a while before Magic makes his presence known, and Millie Girl comes out and watch in the safety of where she feels safe yet is being semi-social—if that even exists. It does in this family!

The kitchen clock glowed dimly as I sat alone at the table, the dishes from dinner pushed to one side. Dad was quieter than usual tonight, and I could feel the tension lingering in the room even after he went to bed. I tried to explain why I couldn't stay late at work tomorrow, but my words felt tangled and half-made. He looked away, and I wondered if he thought I wasn’t doing enough for him. It’s exhausting, balancing his needs and my own deadlines.

I keep thinking about that small crack in his voice when he talked about missing mom. It’s like every time he brings her up, I’m reminded that time is slipping through my fingers fast. I want to be patient and present, but sometimes the weight settles so heavily on my chest that I just want to run away somewhere quiet. I told myself I’d call the nurse tomorrow just to check in, though it feels like a drop in the ocean.

I’m hopeful this too shall pass, that we’ll find a new rhythm. But for now, the quiet in the house is too loud, and my thoughts race every which way. Somewhere between caring and exhaustion, I need to find space to breathe. Maybe tomorrow will be a little easier. 🌙

Hi, gorgeous.
I'm sorry I haven't written for a while. There's been a lot going on over the last couple months, but I promise I haven't stopped thinking about you this whole time. I miss you.
There have been a lot of memories arising these last few weeks. New traditions starting. A new place to live and a worry that nowhere is ever really going to feel like home again now that you're gone. My first birthday without you celebrating with me making me feel like maybe it is worth celebrating.
I was looking through the pictures of/related to you on my phone and was reminded of a Valentine's Day date we had a couple years ago. It was a fairly normal date night for us: favorite hibachi/sushi place, taking you to the book store and following you around carrying the books you wanted, but the movie that night seemed perfect for us: Lisa Frankenstein. It's been two years, and I had forgotten just how much it felt like that movie was made for you. It was the type of dark romance we always appreciated together, and the final scene was like something we would have written as the ending of one of our love stories. I'll be watching this every Valentine's Day from now on thinking about you, and how so many of our own stories had those similar themes.
I'm back living on my own again. I found a fairly nice apartment, but I didn't get to tour it before moving in so there's a big issue I know you would've hated: way too many mirrors around in the dark; you would have hated that. There is a nice in-wall shelf as you walk in which I've filled with pictures and smaller mementos of you. I was given some flowers on Valentine's Day (I went over to our friends' house so we could all watch the movie together, and I think they agree about it basically being made for you,) but they're on their last legs at this point. It did give me the idea of getting some silk flowers for the shelf, though, with a focus on the Victorian flower language you had made art around.
I'm happy to be in a bed again, and being back on my own seems like the more "me" thing to do in the vein of Ken figuring out life without Barbie. I know its only been about a month, but it doesn't feel like home. These past few years "home" was where you were; home was you. I'm by myself so everything is fairly neat and orderly. Things are in their place. All I want is our bedroom and bathroom with your piles of clothes everywhere. I want to look around and see those reminders that we live together, that this is home, that you're there.
My pictures made sure to remind me of my birthday from two years ago; you got us tickets to Distant Worlds. The pictures of the trip to and from are still some of my favorite with you and Tobias, and it's still one of my favorite birthday gifts I've ever gotten. The Final Fantasy series has been a fairly constant presence through my life, and getting to hear so much of the music played by a live orchestra was pretty amazing. You had a knack for making me feel seen and appreciated. My birthday this year was mostly spent in bed. There were offers to do something, but I just didn't have it in me.
I miss you, Madelaine. I love you. I wish you were still here, or that this was one of our stories where I was the death knight with his lich queen, together for eternity. Or Taika and the Blade together in a dark forest, the nearby villages speaking in hushed tones about the Blood Witch and her red-furred werewolf protector. I wish I was still teasing you with the Josh Strife Hayes video where he facetiously comments on girls only being able to play healers in MMOs (and then always playing Sage in Final Fantasy 14, healing so you could play the tank).

The parking lot lights are buzzing, those weird yellow halos, and I keep hearing the clank of carts getting dumped back in their stacks. Feels like the whole world is exhaling after a long day, but my head is just full of static. My phone keeps vibrating with unread messages from him, and I can’t decide if I want to read them or just toss my phone out the window. I’m so tired of this cycle—arguing, apologizing, promising things will change, and then we’re right back here like nothing moves forward. Maybe it’s partly my fault for overthinking every word and reading into silences, but tonight it felt like he was a million miles away, even when he was right next to me in the car.

I should be thinking about job applications, or at least about what I can make for dinner with the last $16 in my account, but my brain is foggy and all I can do is replay our conversation. Did I sound needy? Was I too harsh? I want closeness but I also want peace—I don’t know how to have both. It’s almost 7:30 and I’m just sitting here, watching people walk by with takeout bags, wishing I could just turn off my feelings for a night. The steering wheel is cold under my hands. I wish I could call Mom but I don’t want to burden her with this. Why is it so hard to just talk without it turning into some weird competition about who cares more or who’s more hurt? I keep checking the rearview mirror like I’m expecting someone else to show up and tell me what to do. Maybe I’ll just drive around a bit before heading home. Maybe he’ll text something different. Or maybe I’ll just ignore my phone for a while and try to remember what it felt like to breathe easy.

Trying to figure out the best time to call Mom today, since the last few days have been a mess with her appointments and my work stuff. I ended up walking around the block this afternoon just to clear my head and maybe mentally go through the schedule again. I keep thinking I should make a shared calendar for everyone, but then I remember I’m the only one who actually checks those things. My brother texted again about helping him get to his follow-up appointment next week, which means I’ll need to shuffle two client calls and possibly reschedule that grocery delivery. It’s not that I mind, but lately it feels like every time I think I’ve got a handle on things, something else pops up, and I start worrying I’ll forget something important.

I’m still not really settled in this new place, and I keep misplacing things like my phone charger or the notebook where I jot down reminders. I caught myself making a to-do list in my head about halfway through the walk, and then realized I’d left the actual list on the kitchen table, which is just textbook me. There’s always this nagging feeling that I’m about to drop the ball on something, and I wish I could just pause everything for a day to catch up. Maybe tonight I’ll try blocking off time to actually finish some of these little tasks, but I’m already tired just thinking about it.

Saw a sticky note stuck to my lunch bag this morning, the one I forgot to clear off yesterday—it just said "remember," in my own handwriting, which, honestly, is useless unless I specify what I’m supposed to be remembering. I laughed at myself and then forgot about it until now, when I’m finally getting a breath during this lunch break. There’s the hum of the fridge and the ticking clock in the break room, and my brain feels like it’s running on low battery, just kind of idling. I’m supposed to be using this quiet time to catch up on some emails, but instead I keep replaying last night, which ended with me on the couch, half-watching a documentary, and half-texting Sam—if that’s even what we’re doing, I’m not sure. There’s this weird limbo where I want to ask, “So are we doing this or not?” but I don’t want to seem impatient or, worse, desperate. I don’t think he knows what to say either. It’s been a long time since I’ve had to navigate this sort of thing, and I keep forgetting the rules, if there are any. We were supposed to meet up for dinner but he had to reschedule, and I get that work can be chaotic, but I can’t help but wonder if I’m reading too much into it. Feels like managing a project with shifting deadlines and no project plan, which, as an engineer, is both ironic and a little maddening. My coworkers kept popping in and out of my office all morning, needing things urgently, and I’m starting to feel like everyone wants a piece of me but no one is actually interested in how I’m doing. I keep telling myself to be patient, but I’m tired—more tired than I want to admit. The microwave is beeping now, someone’s heating up soup, and I wish I could just pause everything and have five minutes where no one needs anything from me, including myself. Maybe tonight I’ll just turn off my phone and read, but then again, what if he texts? Ridiculous how much I let that influence my mood. Anyway, lunch is almost over, and I’m still not sure what I was supposed to remember, but I guess I’ll find out eventually, or not.

Steam curls up from my mug, and the hum of the espresso machine is almost loud enough to drown out my phone’s constant buzzing. The table here is sticky, and I keep losing focus, jerking back to the laptop screen whenever a new message pops up from work. It’s barely 9:30 and I already feel like I’m running behind, but everyone on the team wants answers instantly. I said yes to covering someone else’s shift out of habit, even though my own list is a mess. I wish I was better at saying no, or at least not so reactive when someone asks for help. The barista called my name wrong again, but I just smiled, too tired to correct him. I can’t decide if it’s better to hide in public like this or just stay home where the boundaries blur even more. Maybe I’ll order another croissant before the lunch rush starts, just to buy myself a few more minutes away from the screen.

These past few days have been filled with
intense prayer.
🙏🏻
It wipes away any kind of temptation that might creep in, but even more than that, it helps me forget my sense of
loneliness
and the white lies I sometimes tell at work to avoid admitting — especially to myself — that I hardly have any friends, and to avoid being looked at with pity.
In particular,
I’m discovering the power of the
Liturgy of the Hours.
For now I’m listening to it on the
CEI app
, but in two or three weeks the printed version for the
Lenten
season
💜 and
Easter
time 🤍 should arrive.
Today my
Daily Missal
— for Sundays and weekdays — also
arrived.
It’s definitely bulkier, but it fits in my bag, and at least I won’t have to buy the little missal every two months anymore.
I might keep that one in digital form.
It’s actually quite easy to find your way through it — I thought it would be worse.
At work today
, despite everything I had to do and considering that I work part-time,
I managed not to leave anything unfinished.
It was wonderful to see my desk completely clear (I know very well it won’t stay that way for long)!
I’m proud of myself
and
grateful
— every now and then it feels good to say it. 😎
Later I learned that
my aunt L’s father-in-law passed away.
💀
She announced it in the family
WhatsApp
group.
None of us knew this person, and
my parents sent their condolences rather reluctantly
, because they felt it was a bit forced, and in their opinion it was unnecessary to inform us in the first place.
Their coldness and sharpness saddened me a little
, to be honest. 🍋
I believe that
everyone deserves kind words at moments like these.
After all, in a larger sense we are all brothers and sisters, and supporting each other matters.
I briefly mentioned my point of view to my mother, but I immediately sensed from her tone of voice and body language that she was becoming defensive, so I didn’t insist.
I’m simply glad that I haven’t hardened to that extent.
Before ending this page, the
two adorable dachshunds
I met this morning along the avenue on my way to work definitely deserve a mention 🐕.
Their human companion was giving them treats and speaking to them with such sweetness 🥰💕.
From time to time they come back to my mind, and it feels like adding sugar to a bitter cup of coffee ☕.
I don’t know their official names, but in my mind I’d call them
Potty
and
Witty
!
How would you call them?
I'm very curious to know!

Stepped outside this morning before the kids woke up, just to breathe and move. The air was cool but not cold, and the sidewalk still held a bit of last night’s drizzle. I tried to focus on my steps, on the sound of my shoes against the concrete, instead of the list running through my head. Interview next week, need to check if the calendar matches with the kids’ schedule—already feeling anxious about juggling both. My phone buzzed with a reminder about a parent-teacher call, and I almost turned around, but I kept walking, hands deep in my jacket pockets.

It feels like I’m always double-checking, making sure I don’t miss anything important for them or for me. I wonder sometimes if I’m doing enough, being enough. The uncertainty about work is heavy. Still, I keep telling myself things will shift eventually, that I’ll find something stable. The gentleness I try to show the kids is something I want for myself, too, but it’s hard. Today, at least for a few blocks, I could breathe a little easier.

Earlier today I was shuffling through my calendar, trying to make sense of whether I actually confirmed that noon slot with the new client or just thought about confirming it. I remember looking at my email drafts and seeing three half-written replies, none sent. Typical. Now I’m on this bus, head pressed against the window, running through the day’s sessions in my mind, and I can’t help but catalog what I forgot or failed to finish. I still haven’t sent that invoice for last week, and the insurance paperwork is probably overdue again. I told myself I’d update my availability on the website tonight but the idea of opening my laptop again makes me tired. Clients keep rescheduling on short notice, which leaves these awkward gaps in the afternoon and then I scramble to fill them, or I just end up wasting time reading articles I don’t need to read.

My notes from today are all over the place, sticky notes on my phone, some scribbles in the margins of my planner. It’s hard to keep the threads straight, especially when one session just bleeds into the next in my head. I keep thinking I should build a better system, maybe color-code things, but then I get distracted or decide it doesn’t matter. The rent is coming up and with the income so up and down, I’m worried I’ll forget something important (again). Tonight I need to sort out the paperwork, answer two emails, and check if I actually have a session tomorrow morning or if I imagined that too. My mind feels calm right now but I know as soon as I get home and see the pile of stuff on my desk, it’s going to be a different story.

The seat on this bus is scratchy, and my bag keeps threatening to topple into the aisle every time we jolt. My mind is still tangled in the back-and-forth from work, replaying the conversation with that parent who seemed both grateful and frustrated by the new routines. I tried to listen, but I kept thinking about the forms I forgot to send and whether my own notes are in the wrong folder again. The move has thrown me off in so many little ways. I keep checking my phone for reminders about the plumber, the delivery that’s late, and the neighborhood meeting I think I already missed.

I know I’m supposed to be setting up the new office space at home, but the boxes are still half-unpacked and the printer is buried somewhere under winter coats. I keep telling myself tomorrow I’ll catch up, but new things keep sneaking onto the calendar. It’s hard to focus on any one thing. Even now, I’m on this crowded bus, feeling both relieved to be alone and uneasy that I haven’t called my sister back, or figured out what to do for dinner. There’s a list in my head that keeps looping. I wish I could just land somewhere for a while, but every day has more pieces that don’t quite fit together. Maybe after I get home and sit down, I’ll be able to sort through at least one pile.
