The streetlights flickered as I walked around the block tonight. The usual distant hum of cars was oddly comforting, though I couldn’t quite shake the tight feeling in my chest. It’s hard to find a quiet moment at home with everyone around, so this walk was necessary, even if it didn’t bring much relief. I noticed a couple of neighbors out on their porches, which made me realize how little I actually see anyone these days beyond brief hellos at work and the rushed goodnight from the kids.

Work was the same as usual, fielding complaints and trying to keep my patience when customers get frustrated. It wears me down, but it’s predictable, which is a small mercy. I did forget to return one call today, and that’s been bothering me. It’s a small thing, but it sticks with me, like a reminder that I’m juggling too much and not keeping up as well as I want to. Back home, everyone was arguing about something trivial, and there was no space to tune out or process the day properly. The noise made my head ache.

I’m going to try to get to bed earlier, though the idea feels like a distant luxury. Maybe tomorrow will be better. For now, I’ll have to be content with these minutes outside where I don’t have to pretend everything’s fine. The air was cool and a little damp, which helped clear my thoughts somewhat. It’s strange how a simple walk can highlight how much I miss a real break from all the noise, even if it’s just for twenty minutes. 🌙

This morning when I was putting on my shoes, I remembered how my mom used to always tell me to double knot the laces so I wouldn’t trip. That popped in my head out of nowhere. I walked around the block before work, mostly just to clear my head. The air felt weirdly heavy, maybe just humidity or maybe I’m just tired. Saw a neighbor walking their dog and waved. I realized I still haven’t called my sister back about Dad’s appointment. I know I should, but I keep putting it off and then I feel guilty. Thinking about it, I don’t really know where things are going with Jake. He texted late last night but I didn’t answer. I can’t tell if I just need space or if I’m avoiding something. There’s so much uncertainty right now and I don’t feel like myself, but I also don’t know what ‘myself’ even is most days. I guess I’ll try to check in with Dad later. Work is waiting and I have to focus, but it feels impossible today.

This morning, when I handed Mom her pill organizer, she looked at me like she wanted to say something but then just smiled. It was still dark out, and the kitchen light made everything seem even more tired. I can’t get that look out of my head. Now I’m in the parking lot with the engine off, just trying to breathe. I barely slept last night, kept thinking about the bills and wondering how much longer I can stretch things. I hate how guilty I feel for even thinking about work stuff when Mom needs me, but I can’t ignore it either. All the job apps blur together at this point. The dashboard clock says 8:11 and I’m stalling, scrolling through emails but not really reading them.

I’m tired of feeling like I’m letting everyone down. I snapped at my sister on the phone last night, which I regret, but she doesn’t really get how heavy this all is. My hands are shaking a little and I keep checking my phone for a message that isn’t coming. I’m not sure if I want to cry or scream or just hide. I guess I’ll just go inside and put on my game face again. Maybe today something will shift. Or at least I’ll get through it without falling apart.

The bus rattles over a rough patch of pavement, and I catch myself staring at the cracked plastic of the seat back in front of me. Trying to keep track of the kids’ schedules feels like juggling flaming objects—soccer practice on Tuesday, violin lessons moved from Wednesday to Thursday, and oh yeah, dentist appointment next Friday that someone has to drive them to. I thought sharing custody meant splitting time, not doubling the calendar chaos. I barely managed to update the shared app because every time I try, I get distracted by emails from the school, texts about who picks up where, and reminders about which forms need signing. At some point today, I realized I haven't even started on the code review inbox that’s piling up while I’m drowning in coordinating. These little tasks build up until they’re a wall, not a to-do list. I’m dry enough to joke that my life is basically a series of status updates and who’s watching whom when, but underneath I’m just tired. Being nonbinary sometimes feels like another layer of “explaining” that I don’t have the bandwidth for, especially when all the energy is funneled into logistics and keeping everyone on the same page. I imagine a week where I don’t have to say no to myself because I’m too busy saying yes to everything else. Instead, I’m counting stops as the bus rolls on, trying to map out what I can finish while still pretending things are under control. At least the air conditioning is working, and I’ve got a lukewarm coffee in hand, so not all’s lost.

Feeling pretty wiped out today, just can’t seem to get my head clear. Lunch break finally, some quiet in the prep room with my sandwich and tea. The kitchen’s still echoing in my ears though, even with the door closed. Phone keeps buzzing but I don’t want to check it—probably another client changing dates or canceling.

Mom’s health stuff is hanging over everything, even when I’m trying to focus on slicing or plating. I keep thinking about how I used to call her after shifts, tell her about the weird orders or just complain. Sometimes I wonder if I’m doing enough or if I’m just running around in circles with all this freelance stuff, never sure if there’ll be enough gigs to keep things afloat. Feels like I’m drifting, just reacting instead of steering anything.

Wish I could just turn off for an hour. I almost forgot to eat, again. Maybe I’ll call my brother tonight, check in, see how he’s holding up. Feels like there should be some answer or sign, but I just keep chopping onions and hoping tomorrow’s less heavy.

The literature review deadline was moved up again, which means another weekend overshadowed by looming work. I tried to read through the stack of articles after dinner, but the words started blurring together around 11pm. The lamp on this couch is too harsh, and the cushions are lumpy—nothing feels like it fits, including me. I keep getting distracted by the boxes still stacked in the corner; I haven't bothered to unpack half my books, and now I can’t find the one I need for tomorrow’s meeting. I thought moving would shake things up in a good way, but mostly I just feel adrift. My supervisor sent another cryptic email about "tightening up methodology" and I’m not sure whether to laugh or panic. Maybe if I just get through this week I’ll be able to focus, but I don’t really believe that anymore. Sleep would help, but my brain won’t turn off, even though I’m exhausted. At this point, I’m not sure if I’m restless because of the move or the work, or if I just can’t sit still regardless of context.

I barely got through the morning classes today. During lunch, I sat in the staff room and just stared at my sandwich, not really hungry. I kept thinking about how I rushed through that last lesson, stumbling over my words while the students looked half asleep. It bothers me that I can’t seem to capture their attention, no matter how much I prepare. I know I’m tired, but I keep replaying that moment when one student asked a question and I snapped at them. I felt guilty immediately. I wish I had more patience and energy, but most days it feels like I’m running on empty. There’s nowhere to really decompress at home, with everyone always around and no space to just be quiet. I want to do better, but right now, I mostly just feel drained. Maybe tomorrow will be different, but I’m not sure how to change anything.

This morning I caught a glimpse of my dad's worn-out baseball cap tossed on the back of the chair. It hit me harder than I expected, how small things like that carry so much weight after he's gone. The bus is mostly quiet tonight, but my head won’t stop racing through all the little interactions I had with Mom today. I told her I was fine, but that felt like such a lie—she’s hurting too, and I’m trying to hold it together for both of us. Work never really stops, even from home, and the blurred line between office hours and family time is suffocating. I keep wondering if I’m doing enough, if I’m just going through the motions without truly processing everything. There was a call from the insurance company this afternoon about Dad’s medical bills; I didn’t expect to feel so exhausted by paperwork. I was overwhelmed, trying to be practical while I really just wanted to scream or cry. Yet here I sit, staring out the window at the dim streetlights, trying to find some pause in this relentless noise inside my head. Sometimes I think I should write him a letter, the things I never said, but then I worry about dredging up too much. Maybe I’m just scared of how raw it still feels, even months later. This bus ride feels like the only space where I can allow myself to be messy and unsure without explanation. Tomorrow feels like a mountain and I’m still stuck at the base, looking up, wishing for a sign that it’ll get easier. For now, I’ll try to breathe through the heaviness and remind myself it’s okay not to have all the answers.

Earlier today Mom called just as I was closing out a client spreadsheet, and I pretended my headphones were acting up so I could cut the conversation short. I felt bad about it the second I hung up, but the exhaustion just kind of wrapped around me and I couldn’t deal with another round of her telling me to take better care of myself or asking if I’m eating enough. Now it’s late, and the bus is almost empty except for a couple arguing quietly a few seats behind me, their voices blending with the dull hum of the engine and the streetlights flashing by the windows.

I keep thinking about Dad lately, and it makes the ache in my chest heavier on nights like this. Maybe that’s why I’ve been short with Mom, or why I haven’t called my brother back in over a week. I know I’m withdrawing a bit, but I’m just so tired—work is up and down, and when the gigs are thin, the stress feels like it’s pressing right on my forehead. I keep telling myself things will turn up, that I’ll land a few more steady clients or at least get a good night’s sleep. But the quiet on this bus just makes everything echo a little louder. I wish I could tell someone all this without feeling like I’m being a burden. Maybe tomorrow I’ll try to call Mom back and just let her talk, even if I don’t know what to say.

It’s weird how even looking at those listings makes my heart race a little, or maybe that’s just the third cup of lukewarm tea kicking in. Every description sounds like a trap, honestly, with their 'fast-paced environment' and 'must be a self-starter' lines. I can almost hear them laughing as they write it. 

My partner texted to check in, which I appreciate, but it’s hard not to feel snippy when I’m this tired and on edge. We keep talking about communicating better, but some days it feels like we’re just sending smoke signals through a hurricane. Tonight, we’re supposed to have a real conversation about our plans—whatever that means. Part of me wants to just order takeout, put on a dumb show, and ignore the looming pile of adult decisions. 

I know I need to keep pushing, but today it all feels heavier than usual. Maybe I’ll just finish this bland sandwich and go for a quick walk before the next round of applications. At least outside, I can pretend I’m just someone taking a stroll, not someone desperately trying to get her life together.

Do you not know I am a woman? When I think, I must speak.
(~William Shakespeare, “ As You Like It)”
I am a woman, a thinking woman, so I guess, it’s time to speak. I feel that I’ve been neglecting my DD past few days…It was not because I haven’t been thinking and therefore didn’t have anything to write, but rather opposite – I’ve been having all sort of thoughts: smart thoughts, crap thoughts, second thoughts and stupid thoughts, you name it…But the main thought was – were they worth to be thought of…[hmmmmm…that doesn’t sound right, right? ~shakes her head]
Well, actually, we’ve got an issue here: How to define worthiness of something? Or – even – someone?
I am guilty of depreciation of the worthiness of self. I intend to see myself to be the last one in line. I intend to think of me in grey colours. I intend to get rather sad every time, when this little quirk of mine gets in a way of me pursuing something really worth pursuing…
I can permit others much more of everything, then I can let myself. I've set up too high standards for self, but never measure others with them. I'm more kind to others then to self [ “me, me, me” - that’s “some” confession, eh?]
Well, for what it worth (?!) this is what was on my mind these days…And it didn’t make me feel good, which in turn upsets me even further…a circle of self-detraction…
But sometimes a simple words, understanding, but not imposing, seamlessly taking thoughts to flow in different direction can make the difference…And I hope, that I’m just a tiny little bit, but closer to that person I always want to be: Confident in Self. [~don’t we feel blessed, when a friend set aside their important things and let us have their time and shoulder and sympathy?!.]

This morning I remembered standing in the kitchen, halfway through making toast, when I realized the milk was expired and the recycling still hadn’t gone out. I left both half-finished, thinking I’d circle back, but I didn’t. Now I’m circling the block, walking fast, almost like I’m trying to catch up with all the stuff I’ve let dangle throughout the day. The list of things I need to do is ridiculous: send the edits back to Dr. F, invoice for the last dataset, figure out if I can afford groceries before Friday, and double-check if I missed a meeting invite buried somewhere in my inbox. The phone keeps buzzing, mostly with reminders I set for myself, which is both helpful and completely annoying. 

I’m trying to keep organized, but it’s like every time I finish one task, two more appear. I had a brief moment of clarity about what I actually want from this freelance patchwork, but it vanished as soon as I started thinking about rent and deadlines. I keep thinking I should make a master list, but then I get distracted by the next thing that pops up, so the list is just scattered notes on my phone and scraps of paper in my bag. My head is full of project outlines and half-finished grocery lists. Walking helps, a little. I can’t really tell if I’m moving toward anything or just staying busy, but at least I’m moving. Maybe tonight I’ll actually finish something. Or at least remember to buy more milk.

This morning, I was trying to remember if it was my turn to drop off Mia at her dad’s or if he was picking her up. I ended up scrolling frantically through our shared calendar, and of course, there was a double booking for her ballet class and my work meeting. I felt like I was already behind before the day even started, which seems to be the usual lately.

Now I’m at my desk in my room, laptop open, staring at the long to-do list for work. I keep replaying my conversation with Mia last night about missing her grandma (my mom), and it’s like I can’t find the right words to help her or myself. I wish I could just shut off the anxious thoughts for a minute, but they keep looping, especially about whether I’m doing enough as a parent. I know I should be proud for keeping things moving, but I keep focusing on where I’ve messed up or forgot something.

My body is the best weather forecaster, bar none. I don't need to read the weather page in the paper, or check the weather on the 'net. Nope.
And I'm here to tell you that we're in for another storm.
I'm beginning to hurt again.

However....
When I went out at 7:00pm, the sky was clear, and I could see the color in the eastern sky that presages moonrise. When I left to come back home shortly after 8:00pm, the sky was completely overcast again. And if this evening is any indication, I'm going to have to buy a winter coat.
I have a light-weight London Fog raincoat, and another warmer raincoat with a liner, neither of which is going to be adequate if winter is going to be as cold as I think it will be.
I'll be glad when spring comes around again.
Next July I'll be complaining of the heat.
Shalom

The coffee is still warm in my mug, but I’m barely tasting it this morning. I woke up thinking about the text from my ex last night—something about switching weekend plans because he has a work thing now. I’m trying not to let it throw me off, but the calendar juggling feels like too much already. I want to be flexible, of course, but I also worry about how these last-minute shifts affect the kids. They ask questions I don't always have answers for, and I hate feeling like I’m the only one keeping everything organized. We had a brief call after I replied, and it felt like we were both dancing around frustration without naming it. I’m not sure if he understands how anxious this makes me, or if I’m just making it worse by overthinking. Maybe I’m reading too much into a text that was meant to be simple. But it’s hard not to spiral when it feels like I’m always the one holding the schedule together. I remind myself that we both want what’s best for them, even if our communication is off sometimes. I should write down a clearer plan for the week today, to take some pressure off. Still, I wonder if I’m making too many assumptions about his intentions. Maybe I need to breathe more and trust the process, whatever that looks like. The sunlight is catching the steam from my cup now, and I want to hold onto that quiet moment before the craziness starts. Every small thing feels like so much, but I’m trying to keep hope alive that we’ll figure this out together, somehow.

The streetlights flicker above me while I walk, hands deep in my jacket pockets. It’s pretty quiet except for my footsteps and the distant hum of a car radio. The air feels damp tonight, like it might rain, and I keep hearing the sound of my own breathing louder than usual.

Mom’s been on my mind most of the day. Can’t shake the feeling that I should be doing more for her, even though I know there’s not much left I can fix. Being a mechanic makes me think I can repair anything, but I know I can’t fix this. Sometimes I wish I could just work on engines and not think, but tonight everything follows me.

Money’s tight again. Got three jobs lined up for next week, but nothing guaranteed. I worry about bills, then feel guilty for thinking about money when someone I love is hurting worse. I keep telling myself things will even out, but it’s hard to believe that tonight. I hope a better mood finds me in the morning.

My empty plate is still in front of me, cold broccoli pushed to one side because I got distracted thinking about tomorrow’s appointments and whether I sent the right forms to the insurance lady. I keep glancing at the calendar pinned crookedly above the microwave, rows of scribbled notes for doctor visits, therapy sessions, and Leo’s rescheduled parent-teacher meeting. I feel like I’m always a step behind, chasing after paperwork or remembering who needs to be where at what time. Mom’s follow-up is at noon, but I agreed to proofread a client’s draft by 2 pm, and I have class readings I haven’t even started yet. I meant to call my brother back tonight about Dad’s estate paperwork, but it slipped my mind again. If I don’t write these things down immediately, they get lost, but the lists themselves are becoming overwhelming.

Lisa tried to talk to me about splitting up the weekend errands, but I snapped that I’d handle them myself. She didn’t push back, just cleared the dishes and turned on the TV. I hate that I’m making things tense, but sometimes it feels easier to just take everything on rather than ask for help and risk a fight about who forgot what. I need to find a better way to keep track of everything without feeling like I’m drowning. Maybe a shared online calendar, but even that feels like just another thing to manage. My mind’s still ticking through who needs rides tomorrow, whether we have enough groceries, and if I remembered to refill Mom’s prescription. I should get up and start prepping for tomorrow, but I just want to sit here a minute longer.

This afternoon I recalled a brief exchange I had with my wife over text. She asked if I’d remembered to lock the back door before leaving for work. I said yes, but now I’m not sure if I actually checked or just assumed I did. It’s a small thing, but it’s stuck with me because I keep going over the conversation in my head, wondering if I brushed her off too quickly or if I sounded distracted. Maybe she felt ignored or that I wasn’t really present. 

Right now, I’m sitting in the parking lot, waiting to clock in, feeling the usual mix of tiredness and that nagging sense that I’m falling behind on everything. The lines between work and home have gotten so blurry with remote study and jobs. I want to be better at listening, at showing her I care, even when I’m overwhelmed. I hope tomorrow will bring a chance to clear this up. Sometimes I worry I make things harder than they need to be by holding back instead of just saying what’s really on my mind.

There was a secret santa at my work, but I didn't take part.

Three reasons:

1) I don't want to get an anonymous 'joke' present (or get a lame one and be paranoid that it was) and be sad about it

2) If someone gets me something nice, I want to know A) who got it, B) that they meant it, not felt forced to get me something.

3) I already bought presents during Black Friday, I didn't want to go back to worrying what the heck to get someone I barely know

Plus, one of our colleagues isn't the best person. Would you want a present from him? Would you want to spend money giving him a present?

I told these reasons to my supervisor Xandra who was arranging it. I said I didn't want it to be like peer pressure and feeling like you "should" do it. To prove my point, rather than just saying "ok, it's optional", she replied saying "but" this and "but" that, explaining the concept etc.

And I replied "see?"

She suddenly handed in her notice after that... not because of that, but because she got outright handed a job with kids, and she always wanted that. She really didn't want to leave and she feels bad. Especially with how it screws up my holiday hopes.

All the above might be why she gave me a big Christmas bag of presents - macaroons, gingerbread, tree decorations.

(And also cake from her birthday.)

Zipped my jacket up as I stepped onto the bus, fumbling with my headphones and nearly dropping my phone yet again. Just finished clearing the dishes and honestly I kind of zoned out halfway through, thinking about that talk with my mom over dinner. She asked me if I was eating enough lately, and I know she’s worried because I look tired, but I just got irritated instead of saying anything helpful. I snapped a little, not even realizing how much her concern is probably about grandma being sick. I feel like I should have been more patient, but lately it’s like my brain is just skipping around all over the place. The new apartment still feels empty, and sometimes I almost expect to hear voices from the old house. I keep forgetting where I put things, like the salt, or my sketchbook, and then I get frustrated and it all spills out at the wrong moment. I wish I could explain that I’m not trying to be difficult, but the words kind of get stuck. Maybe I’ll try again tomorrow, but for now I just want to sit here and not think about anything in particular. This isn’t really what I thought moving out would feel like, and I’m not sure if I’m handling it well or not.

My fork is still on the plate even though I finished eating a while ago, just sort of staring at my empty water glass and thinking about how much I spent on groceries today. The receipt is still in my pocket, crumpled up, but I keep going over each line in my head—milk, bread, rice, the cheapest apples they had. I didn’t get chips or anything extra, but somehow it all adds up faster than I expect. I told myself I’d figure out a better system for tracking expenses, but the spreadsheet is already making me want to nap. I tried using an app, but it kept crashing or asking for money, which is pretty ironic. My phone screen has a tiny crack now, so when I was checking my bank balance this afternoon, the numbers looked even worse through the little spiderweb line. I guess it’s not the end of the world, but it feels like every little thing is a new task to deal with. I still haven’t finished the online forms for job applications and the tabs are multiplying. The kitchen light keeps flickering and it’s annoying, but I keep forgetting to tell the landlord because I’m too busy thinking about the next thing I have to do. I meant to call my mom and ask about her trick for getting stains out, but the time just sort of disappeared. Thinking about laundry now, and how I need to make sure I have enough quarters for the machines downstairs. Not sure if I’ll get to it tonight or if I’ll just stare at the basket and pretend I did. I keep telling myself I’ll get everything under control, but it’s like juggling and I’ve never been good at that. The table still has crumbs on it and I should wipe it down before I forget. Maybe I’ll just leave it for a bit and watch a video to clear my head, but then I’ll probably feel guilty for wasting time. Ugh. I hope tomorrow feels a little less crowded with dumb little things.

Zipped up my coat just as the bus pulled up, and now I’m finally heading home after a long shift. The city lights look smeared through the dirty window, and my legs are heavy from standing most of the day. I keep thinking about that customer who asked for help with the blenders and ended up telling me her whole life story—funny how people just open up. My mind always goes in a million directions at night, but right now I’m surprisingly calm, just watching traffic crawl. I almost missed the bus because I stopped to help a coworker close out her register, but I’m glad I did. It’s nice to feel useful, even if it means getting home later than I wanted. My phone buzzed twice, probably the family group chat about what to eat tomorrow, but I haven’t checked yet. Privacy is a joke at our place, but the noise is comforting in its own way. I’m already planning tomorrow in my head even though I know it never works out the way I picture it. Sometimes I wish I could just shut off the overthinking and be in the moment. I guess riding the bus at night is as close as I get—nobody expects anything from me here. I’m tired but not unhappy, which feels like a win. The bus just turned onto our street, so I’ll have to put my game face back on soon. For now, I’ll enjoy these last few quiet minutes before the chaos starts up again.

Cell phones have provided us with the opportunity to carry on some truly bizarre conversations. In the old days the telephone was firmly anchored to the wall and only the telephone repairman fooled around with it. Then they came up with the little clip on phone lines and we started buying our own phones and plugging them in every room in the house. Then the portable phone came along and we took it all over the place with us. Who would have ever thought we would hear the question, “Where’s the phone?” but we ask it all the time these days. Because we are always laying it down someplace in the garage instead of back in the cradle where it belongs. And then the cell phone arrived.
Now practically everyone I know is carrying around a cell phone, these tiny, plastic packet like things that for some strange reason remind me of travel kleenex packages. They sing, vibrate, tweet and play classic tunes. (Beethoven would be embarrassed ) . Anyway, we have people making phone calls from entirely new places and thus having phone conversations never heard before.
As an example, I give you a conversation I had with my oldest son E. the other day. He was in Los Angeles, I in Sacramento.
Me: Hello.
E. : Hey mom, what’s up ?
Me: Not much, I’m getting ready to go out and work in the garden before it
gets too hot.
E. : (muffled noise) Mom, hold on a minute… (barely audible) Ah, could I
Have a double order of Chicken Tenders, fries and a large Coke ?
Yeah, large Coke……no, I don’t want a Whopper, Chicken Tenders.
Right.
Me : Where are you ?
E. : Burger King
Me : This is weird listening to you order food.
E. : So mom, did you hear the press conference by Rumsfeld this morning?
Me : Yep, he was great ! I love to hear his one word answers. The reporters
never know what to say when answers with a simple yes, or no.
E. : Yeah, he was so cool…. What ? … oh could I have barbecue sauce,
Thanks.
(Silence)
Me. : Are you there ?
E. : Mom.
Me : What ?
E. : Never order a large Coke at Burger King.
Me : Why not ?
E. : This thing is HUGE ! This is a VAT of Coke ! It looks like the
barrel that a St. Bernard rescue dog would carry to revive people.
Geeze, how am I going to drink all this ?
Me : (Laughing hysterically)
E. : Just a minute, (barely audible) Okay thanks… (to the checkout guy)
Okay mom, where were we? (exiting the drive through)
Me : Rumsfeld.
E. : (Paper bag rattling in the background)
Silence…..
Me : What is it ? Don’t tell me…..
E. : They gave me a Whopper.
Me : Laughing even more hysterically…. Are you going back ?
E. : No, I can’t I have to go to a meeting. Geeze, a Whopper…
Me : (Cracking up)
E. : Well, I just wanted to find out if you had heard Rumsfeld.
Me : Yes I did. (wiping tears from my eyes)
E. : I have to get on the freeway now, I have to hang up.
Me : Okay, have a good day !

I just finished a quiet lunch alone, trying to focus on the book I brought, but my mind kept drifting back to Mom. It’s strange how her absence feels heavier some days, like this afternoon when I saw a woman at the park who reminded me of her laugh. Balancing school and work is exhausting enough, but grief adds this extra weight I can’t shake off. I caught myself staring out the window more than reading, watching people pass by without a care. Sometimes I wonder if I’m holding on too tightly to memories, or if letting go would feel like losing a part of myself. I didn’t call Dad today, though I meant to. There’s this hesitation, maybe guilt, or just not wanting to start a conversation I can’t finish. I’m tired, but the restless feeling won’t let me rest, so I’m jotting this down before heading back to the library.

Tonight, the paperwork from the clinic felt like a small mountain, and I found myself wishing I could split into two people just to get everything done. My mother’s prescriptions needed sorting, and between fielding her questions and answering work emails, I barely remembered to eat dinner. The most striking moment happened around 7, when she asked if I’d sit with her to watch an old sitcom. I almost said no out of habit, but something in her voice made me pause. We ended up laughing at the ridiculous punchlines, and I noticed how much she still enjoys these small rituals. It was a rare pause for both of us in the middle of a day that felt like triage. Even as my mind kept drifting to the next task, I could see how much these shared minutes matter to her, and maybe to me too, though I don’t often admit it. The weight of responsibility doesn’t get lighter, but sometimes it shifts just enough to let in a bit of relief. I’m restless tonight, thinking about how long I can keep juggling everything, but at least I didn’t miss that moment with her. I suppose that counts for something, even on days where everything feels a little too much to handle.

I have lived surrounded by men all my life.
I have one brother, I married men who only had brothers and gave birth to three sons. What can I say? I have been swimming in the seas of testosterone as long as I can remember. Funny that I have stayed feminine at all !
I have had conversations with all these masculine life mates of mine that I think are probably illegal. Women are not supposed to know some of the things that I know about men, but I am here to share one of these hard won secrets with you.
Here is the secret. When a masculine type person wants to ask you a really profound question about life and or his manhood, he waits until you are both somewhere near the toothpaste aisle in Wal-Mart.
One day, before I knew I should be on my toes for this phenomenon, my 15 year old son asked me, (as I was looking for shampoo in a blissful state of ignorance) "Mom, how do you know when you are old enough to have sex?" After the first shock wave hit me, no not the one of realization that we were having a sex talk, but ...My God, is this conversation REALLY going to happen with a bottle of Pantene in my hand ? He was standing there saying to me, "Well?" I told him as smoothly as I could muster, "Give me a minute, will ya ? that is a very BIG question." stalling for time. But then it hit me like a flash, I felt like Einstein ! I told him, "When you think you are ready to become a father." No more, no less, that is all I said. Needless to say he was impressed. Whoa, he was thinking, I was just talking about SEX ya know, not like uh. . . fatherhood. But that’s exactly what IS missing in an immature view of the subject. Ah, sometimes I even amaze myself.
I can report to you the secret of these conversations now, because I had the second one to confirm that the first was not just a fluke. This time I was ready.
The question came just as we were turning the corner by the hair dye. He was wondering about the size of his private parts and just how important was that anyway. . . from a woman’s point of view? Without so much as a gasp, I dove right in. This time though, I did get an admonition to stop making gestures with my hands (fish stories come immediately to mind) "Mom, do you want to embarrass me ?"
(Like asking this question in Wal-Mart is perfectly normal ??!!)
So I gave him my opinion on the subject. Didn't even blink an eye.
He seemed satisfied with my answer, and then we picked out a new kind of toothpaste together.
Ah, the joys of motherhood and womanhood in Testosterone land. Never a dull moment, not even in Wal-Mart. I wouldn't trade this job for any other on the planet.
(No, I am not going to share with you what I told him about private parts. We would have to go to Wal-Mart. It’s the way these things are done don’t you know!)

Pushed my plate away and sat there for a minute, just kind of zoning out after dinner. Dad asked me if I’d figured out how to handle my rent this month, and I got snappy, which I regret. It’s not like he’s wrong to ask, but I hate talking about money in front of everyone, especially when Mom tries to jump in and suggest I pick up extra shifts or sell stuff I don’t even want to get rid of. I know I’m supposed to be grateful for advice, but it feels like they’re questioning whether I’m even trying. Maybe I overreacted. I can’t tell if I’m annoyed at them or just stressed about never having enough to cover everything. I keep thinking about what my life’s supposed to look like right now. Is everyone else just faking it or actually on top of things? Felt stupid for raising my voice, but sometimes I wish they’d trust me to figure it out. I want to ask for help, but I also want to prove I can handle things alone. Sitting at the table felt like being on display. I tried to change the subject, but the tension just sat there. It’s weird to not know if I should apologize or just try to act normal tomorrow. I keep thinking maybe they’re just worried, but anxiety makes me think I let them down. I don’t know if I’m overthinking or not thinking enough. I’ll probably just go to bed early and hope tomorrow’s easier.

Just got off the phone with Jamie, trying to sync up schedules for next week. It’s always this weird mix of polite and tense, like neither of us wants to say the wrong thing but we’re both tired of trying to keep things smooth. I suggested Tuesday and Thursday for drop-offs, but she didn’t sound thrilled. Not sure if something’s going on or she’s just annoyed I couldn’t do Wednesday. I keep replaying what I said, wondering if I sounded too blunt or not clear enough. 

It’s kind of draining, honestly. I want us to work together for our kid, but it sometimes feels like we’re just trying not to piss each other off. Maybe I’m overthinking it. I know we both have other things going on, and it’s not always about me. Still, I catch myself getting defensive before anything even happens. I wish I knew if I’m handling this the right way. I keep telling myself to just keep it simple, focus on the calendar, don’t get into feelings, but that’s hard when things feel awkward. Maybe it’ll get easier over time. Or maybe I just need to stop worrying about being perfect at this.

I spent most of dinner thinking about the spreadsheet I couldn’t finish at work. It’s ridiculous how a few missing numbers can make me feel like I’m losing control, but I keep replaying the conversation with my supervisor in my head. She asked if the report would be ready tomorrow, and I said yes even though I’m not sure it will be. I probably should have just told her the truth instead of trying to sound more confident than I am.

After we finished eating, my sister called. She wanted to talk about Mom’s old house again. I think she’s hoping I’ll have some kind of strong opinion about what to do with it, but I just don’t. I don’t know if that’s because I’m still not used to being here in this new city or if I’m avoiding the subject on purpose. She sounded frustrated when I said I’d have to think about it some more, but I really don’t know what to tell her. It’s hard to focus on family things when work feels so overwhelming.

The kitchen’s still a mess, and I keep glancing at my phone, half expecting someone to text but knowing they won’t. I miss having someone to just vent to about all these little things. Maybe I should try joining that walking group I saw on the community board, but I don’t know if I’d fit in. Everything feels a bit up in the air right now, and my mind is jumping from one thing to the next. I wish I could just let it rest for a bit.

I spent most of today trying to coordinate schedules between my work tasks and the tentative plans with him. It feels like every time I settle into one thing, another pops up demanding immediate attention. After dinner, when we sat at the table talking, I noticed how much my mind wandered even while he was sharing something personal. There’s a part of me wanting to be fully present, but the relentless to-do list in the back of my head keeps pulling focus.

He mentioned something about meeting again soon, but didn’t specify when. That uncertainty nags at me because I’m not sure where this relationship is headed. I want clarity but also don’t want to rush or push. It’s a delicate balance, and I’m not sure I’m managing it well.

The night feels both full and empty, like I’m waiting for something to settle or reveal itself. Maybe it’s just the restless energy I can’t shake. Either way, I need a better way to juggle all this without losing sight of what matters.

Had to restock the greeting cards this afternoon, which sounds simple but those racks are always a disaster. I wasted a good part of my lunch break digging through piles of "Happy Birthday" and "Get Well Soon" cards that looked like they’d survived a tornado. My sandwich kept getting squished in my bag, so I ended up eating half-mashed turkey and lettuce while crouched behind the loading door, trying not to get mustard on my shirt. The radio in the staff room was playing some upbeat pop song, which felt oddly out of place with how tired everyone looked. 

Even though it’s busy today, I feel a little lighter than usual. Maybe it’s just having a routine that helps. I caught myself making dumb jokes with the other associates while we organized the clearance shelf. No one really laughed, but at least no one looked annoyed either, which I’ll count as a win. My manager asked me to cover a shift tomorrow, and I said yes without really thinking it through. I guess I don’t mind the extra hours, but my head feels all over the place lately. Still, it’s nice to have things to do. After work I’ll probably just microwave some leftovers and watch something mindless before bed. Living alone has its perks, like not having to share the remote, but it also means I’m the only one who cleans up the mess. Not that I’ve been keeping up with that very well lately. I’ll try to get to the dishes tomorrow if I remember.

The refrigerator hums quietly in the background while sunlight glints off the edge of my lunch plate. I keep catching myself staring at the same leftover pasta, fork poised but unmoving, as thoughts spiral around the question of who I really am under all these layers of deadlines and research topics. Being a grad student is supposed to be about learning and growing, but lately it feels more like standing on shifting sand—each new idea makes me question the last one, and nothing feels solid. My mind jumps from worries about my thesis to random doubts about whether this path even makes sense for me, and I can’t help but wonder if I’m just impersonating someone who has it together. There’s an ache in my chest that I can’t quite name, some mix of fear and longing for purpose. Lunch breaks are supposed to be restful, but I end up using the quiet to pick apart my own motivations. Maybe everyone feels like this sometimes, but it’s hard not to feel alone in it. The clock on the microwave blinks 12:43, and I realize I’ve barely eaten a thing.

The desk lamp hums quietly, one of the only sounds in the house right now. I just finished sorting through a pile of appointment reminders, insurance paperwork, and school forms—my own, my clients’, my kids’, all jumbled together. My back aches from hunching over for what must have been an hour, but I can’t seem to get ahead, not really. I keep thinking about what I’m missing, like there’s always another urgent email I forgot to reply to or some forgotten permission slip that will pop up at the worst moment.

I try to remind myself that it’s fine, everyone has these days, and yet my mind just keeps spinning with lists. The family is just on the other side of the bedroom door, and I can hear muffled voices, laughter, the TV, which makes the feeling of being needed in two places at once even stronger. I wish I could just shut it all out for a few minutes, but privacy in this house is like a rare bird—you catch a glimpse, and then it’s gone.

Maybe tomorrow I’ll get ahead, maybe I’ll wake up early and make a plan that actually works. I want to stay optimistic, but right now I just feel like I’m underwater, paddling hard to keep from swallowing too much. I hope nobody notices how scattered I am lately. For now, I’ll just breathe and let this be enough for the night.

This morning, when I was making oatmeal for Mom, she asked me what day it was and then forgot again before I could answer. I had to repeat it three times, and each time the word "Thursday" felt thinner, like I was stretching it out too far. I keep replaying that moment while I sit here in the car, watching the sun come up over the medical building's ugly sign. My hands smell faintly of lavender from the lotion I used on her legs before I left, which is comforting and also a little sad.

I have clients starting in 20 minutes, so I should be reviewing notes, but all I can think about is whether I locked the door, if the soup will be enough for Mom's lunch, and how I'll manage to get her to her doctor’s appointment between sessions. My brain is ping-ponging between work and home, but somehow it all feels connected—every story I hear from clients echoes in my own life lately. I’m grateful for the quiet of this parking lot, even though it smells like hot asphalt and old fast food wrappers. I wish I could call my brother and ask for help, but I know he’s just as overwhelmed. Maybe after my last appointment today, I’ll buy a little plant for Mom’s windowsill—just something green to add a bit of hope. I’m tired but alert, running on a strange kind of energy that isn’t quite adrenaline. Sometimes I wonder how long I can keep doing this, but for now, I just need to go inside and be present for someone else.

Mrs Claus is so underrated...
Women are the magic behind all things Christmas. The big guy in the jolly red suit can kiss my arse. He may get all the credit but we women, plan, organise, prep, cook, make never-ending lists so we don't forget one person or one element; all to make the season great for others.
As I'm writing this, I'm sitting here on Christmas Eve listing all the ways my husband (I do love him truly) has done not a damn thing this year, again. He hasn't put up one single decoration for Christmas this year, hasn't made a list or organised what presents to get for others. 80% of the gifts we buy go towards his side of the family, yet I'm the one doing it all. Is this fair?
Every year I get the same old tired replies:
"I'm just not that good at wrapping, you're amazing at it!"
"I have no idea what to get him/her, let's just go with your idea."
"Leave that, I'll get to it." Said item or task is still sitting there on Christmas Eve not handled and I have to end up doing it myself.
We've been together going 19 years now, do you know he's only cooked Christmas dinner himself once? And he thought he was doing me a favour by giving me a break. I still ended up in the kitchen for an hour handling the food, just with a gigantic mess on top of it as he never cleans as he goes. Some break.
Sometimes being married is exhausting in itself, it's supposed to be a partnership but at this time of year it's ever more evident how untrue that really is. And you're also more aware of the lack of effort when it comes to the gift giving. 80% of my gifts end up being sweets or chocolates which isn't helpful when he's fully aware I have a sugar condition that limits how much I should be eating. It just feels lazy, last minute and like there isn't any thought put in to it. All year long I make a list of things he does and doesn't like, and I use this to make sure his gifts are that bit more special for him. Is it too much to ask that he puts a bit of that effort aside for me? I just feel taken for granted and it's killing the romance for me.
I feel so selfish even writing this post but there's a part of my brain that's also like "Why are you feeling guilty? It's all true. You have the right to have the same effort put into you, as you give to others!". I'm emotionally exhausted from this year and I'm just grateful I've made it through. Whatever pile of confectionary waits for me tomorrow, I'll simply smile, show I'm thankful and pour myself a nice big glass of Baliey's to numb some of the pain. The 26th to the 30th of December are my actual holiday days, where I can float around the house in my PJ's and just ignore everyone for some me time. I get 4 whole days in the year where I can focus just on myself without a shred of guilt.
I wonder what it feels like to be a man, uncaring and floating through such moments in life carefree, knowing it's all being handled for you. I imagine it's what winning the lottery would feel like. Maybe I should start playing it every week...
Merry Christmas everyone, I hope you get some time for yourselves you unsung hero's of the female variety!

I felt a little unsettled after our Zoom call this afternoon. I thought I had conveyed my concerns clearly, but there was this moment when the tone shifted, and I wasn’t sure if it was frustration or just tiredness on their end. It’s hard working remotely when you miss those subtle cues, like body language or the kind of sighs you don’t hear over a headset. Instead, I found myself replaying what I said and wondering if something came off wrong or if I misunderstood their reaction entirely. I keep going back to the part where I suggested a small change in the data collection process. Maybe it seemed like I was questioning their approach too much? I really wanted to be collaborative but also helpful. I guess I didn’t get the chance to explain why I thought it could improve things, so it might have sounded more like a critique. I’m hesitant to bring it up again soon because I don’t want to seem pushy or defensive. Maybe I’m overthinking, but that kind of uncertainty lingers and makes me anxious. On the other hand, the rest of the day was productive, and I managed to finish most of the paperwork I’ve been avoiding. Trying to focus on that helps keep the anxiety at bay. Still, I wish I knew how to read these virtual conversations better and be more certain about where I stand. I’m hoping tomorrow’s meeting will be smoother or at least clearer. For now, I’m just going to make some tea and try to let go of these swirling thoughts before dinner.

So this morning, I took my walk in the crisp morning air. I greeted my Hmong community with an especially loving good morning as they walked to school, and they returned the greeting in kind. I listened to The Serviceberry to ground myself as I walked. I noticed the frost on the trees over the pond and green stains from the buckthorn berries in the snow. The flock of robins passing through in search of these berries. And as I walked along the main thoroughfare, I walked with a smile on my face so that each commuter could start their day with a smile. A few waved.
Today, I am thankful to have siblings who share in my horror, even though they do not live here.
I am thankful to Robin Wall Kimmerer for sharing her Potawatomi wisdom in her books.
I am thankful for the peacemakers.

Feeling kind of jittery tonight, sitting at the table after dinner with my head full of lists. Today was another one of those days where it felt like my schedule was just an endless loop of trying to keep things from falling through the cracks. I kept reminding myself to send a message to that client about moving pallets next week, but I never got around to it. There’s a weird comfort in the routine of sorting boxes and scanning labels at the warehouse, but when I’m home, it’s like all the unfinished stuff just crowds in. I’m trying to track all the shifts I’ve picked up this month, which invoices are still out, and if there’s any hope of landing that bigger contract. My phone keeps buzzing with reminder alerts, and half of them are just so I don’t forget to buy groceries or call about the water bill. Sometimes I wish I could just clock in and out, let someone else handle the paperwork and the scheduling headaches. I’ve got this folder on my laptop full of spreadsheets and budgets, but I still feel like I’m missing something every day. I know I’m organized, but lately it’s like the more I try to line things up, the more things slip out of place. Tomorrow I need to check in with the temp agency again, and I should probably follow up on those emails from last week. I keep hoping something steadier will turn up, but for now it’s just juggling jobs and hoping I don’t drop the important stuff. At least I managed to cook tonight, even if it was just pasta with whatever was left in the fridge. I guess that’s something. I’ll try to write a better plan in the morning, but right now, it’s hard to focus on anything except how much I still need to get done.

The early morning light filtering through the curtains is softer than usual, which is nice because it makes my cluttered desk look less chaotic. I spent the first hour trying to prioritize the dozens of small tasks piling up, from client revisions to invoicing and follow-ups. It feels good to have so much work, but the surface calm hides a tight schedule and a sense that I’m always a bit behind. I keep reminding myself that I can’t do everything at once, especially since the line between work and home blurs more each day. Midway through, a text from my partner popped up. It wasn’t sharp, but I could tell there’s tension lingering between us over how we divide household responsibilities. I want to give more, but I’m stretched thin, and that’s hard to explain without sounding like I’m making excuses. I’m hopeful today that we can find a way to talk openly without frustration getting in the way. There are half-packed boxes on the floor, reminders of things I still haven’t sorted from the move weeks ago. Somehow, everything feels like it needs to get done yesterday, but I’m trying to stay patient and keep a clear plan. Coffee is cooling next to my laptop, and I’m tempted to just step away for a bit, though I know I’ll lose momentum if I do. Instead, I’m setting a timer for 25 minutes to keep myself focused. The balance between staying optimistic and managing this anxious buzz is tricky, but I’m holding on to the thought that a better rhythm is just around the corner. For now, it’s about organizing the chaos one small step at a time.

Today at lunch I caught myself zoning out while my partner was telling me about their day. It’s like my mind kept jumping to that call with the client that went sideways again. Trying to hold it together while multitasking isn’t really my strong suit, especially when I’m supposed to be fully present. Late last night, I got stuck thinking about that phone call with my mom. I wish I could just dial down the guilt of not calling more often. She sounded tired, and it weighed on me more than I expected. I’m aware that my tendency to rush through conversations doesn’t exactly help the situation, but slowing down feels like a luxury I can’t afford right now. Balancing work projects, keeping up with communication in my relationship, and dealing with family stuff is wearing me thin. I keep telling myself I’m doing enough, but the self-critical voice is loudest when I’m alone in moments like this. It’s frustrating because I value being spontaneous, but sometimes it just looks like I’m scatterbrained and distracted. I wonder if my dry humor is a way to mask how overwhelmed I feel inside. All these little frictions pile up, making simple interactions more strained than they probably should be. I want to improve how I listen, not just hear, but it’s hard to find the mental space when I’m always rushing. Maybe I need to schedule forced downtime, even if it’s just 15 minutes with no screens or multitasking. For now, I’ll go back to my coffee, clear my head, and try to come back to these conversations with more patience. It’s a start. ☕

I spent most of yesterday evening adjusting the lighting in my studio area yet again, as the shadows on the new canvas just weren’t cooperating. By the time I finally called it quits, it was past midnight and I ended up sprawled on the living room couch, half-watching the city lights flicker through the window. I can’t help but feel the weight of the upcoming gallery submission deadline pressing in on me—there’s a constant internal debate between pushing for technical perfection and just letting the work breathe as it wants to. The unfamiliarity of this city is still gnawing at me; I miss having someone to bounce ideas off of, or even just a familiar face to decompress with after a long session. My hands smelled faintly of oil paint and turpentine, and I noticed a streak of blue on my wrist I must have missed. The silence here is both comforting and unsettling; it gives me space to focus, but sometimes I catch myself wishing for the ambient noise of my old neighborhood. I forgot to pick up the groceries after work again. Too many things on my mind at the end of the shift, and honestly, I just wanted to get home and collapse. The living room was dark except for the TV's blue light, but I didn't even turn it on, just dropped my keys on the side table and sank into the couch. My partner was already there, quiet, scrolling on their phone. I tried asking about their day, but it felt forced.

We both know things have been tense. I keep thinking if I say the right thing, it’ll help, but mostly it comes out awkward or too blunt. I caught myself staring at the ceiling, counting the small cracks in the paint, while they answered with half sentences. The silence between us is heavier lately. I want to fix it, but my mind feels dull by the time I get home, and I worry I’ll make it worse if I push too much.

Sometimes I imagine just blurting out everything I’m worried about, but I can’t find the words when it matters. I wish I had more energy at night, or more patience, or both. Maybe tomorrow will be different. For now, I just folded the blanket over my lap and tried to be present, even if all I could do was sit next to them in the quiet.

For now, I’ll just watch the city lights out the window for a bit and hope sleep comes fast.

I had a busy (and expensive) weekend. Saturday I purchased a digital camera for my upcoming Oregon trip. It's a Cannon G1, several steps up from Cannon's digital Elph that I got the Professor for Christmas. I was hoping that if I stuck with Cannon I'd be able to use the same software packages with it, and by and large that is the case, but I needed a different driver for downloading images from the camera, and I got a nicer package than the Professor got to edit the pictures. I've taken several dozen pictures of the Kitten with it, in an effort to get more comfortable with using it. It has a movie setting too, that I'll have to play with later. That eats a lot of space on the memory though, so I doubt I'll be using it on the trip.
Saturday night I spent taking tickets at a special event at the Philadelphia Zoo for kids with leukemia. It was sobering to see these young kids with no hair on their heads or in wheelchairs or wearing surgical masks to protect them while they were immunicompromised from chemotherapy. If you could get past appearances, they were in every way normal kids. They wanted to see the tigers and giraffes, and for some reason the monkies were especially popular. They wanted hot dogs and candy. They watched the keepers who were there to talk about their charges, and had awe in their eyes as they listened. I saw all this, and realized how little I was really doing to help, and wondered at how small my problems are in contrast. I think I need to do things like this more often.

This morning, I watched my roommate pacing around the kitchen, almost tripping over the recycling bin while talking on the phone, and it just struck me how much we’re both running in circles these days. Now I’m sitting in the car, engine off, just letting myself breathe before I go inside and face the stack of things waiting for me in the office. I keep thinking about that moment, the way he kind of laughed at himself and then went right back to checking the time, and it made me realize how much I do the same thing. I feel like I’m always trying to squeeze more out of every hour, like if I can just be a little more efficient or organized, things will finally settle down. But here I am, tired already, staring at the dashboard, and I know I haven’t figured it out yet. The company’s growing, which is good, but it means I have to keep up this pace, balancing everything, and I’m worried I’m missing the point sometimes. I keep telling myself I’ll take a real break soon, maybe actually shut off my phone for a night, but then I look at the calendar and it all gets away from me again. Tonight I want to at least try to leave work at a reasonable hour, eat something real for dinner, and maybe talk to my roommate about something other than schedules or bills. I want to feel like I’m actually living in my own life, not just running from one task to the next. It’s weird how even small moments, like watching someone else rush around, can make you stop and think about whether you’re being honest with yourself about what matters. I guess I’m hoping I can hold onto that thought long enough to actually do something about it.

I woke up this morning already thinking about the staff schedule for the next two weeks. There’s a lot going on at work right now with people requesting days off and trying to swap shifts, so my first instinct was to pull up the spreadsheet and start sorting things out before breakfast. I noticed that Alan left me a message asking if he could leave early tomorrow to be at his daughter’s recital. A couple years ago I probably would’ve just said no since we’re already stretched thin, but I found myself wanting to help him make it work. Maybe because lately I’ve been feeling how isolating it can get, just going through the motions day after day, and I know these moments matter for people. I approved his request and started reassigning some tasks to cover the gap. It made me think about how much responsibility comes with being the one who decides these things. On some level it feels good to be able to help, even if it means more juggling for me. I’m tired, but there’s a kind of satisfaction in knowing I can make someone else’s life a little easier, even in small ways. The rest of the morning was spent checking inventory and fielding calls, but that early decision with Alan stayed on my mind. It reminded me that even in a job that sometimes feels like it runs on autopilot, there are real moments where I can choose to be decent. That counts for something, I think.

The clatter of dishes still echoes faintly as I sit here, the leftovers barely cleared from the table and the fading light casting soft shadows across the room. We had dinner later than usual, thanks to the chaos of today’s schedule, and it’s like the small cracks in our conversation widened without either of us fully saying why. I could see the frustration flicker in her eyes as I made some dry joke about the laundry pile. Not my finest moment, but honestly, when you’re juggling a toddler’s tantrums and a work email meltdown at the same time, the humor feels like a lifeline, even if it’s a bit sharp-edged. I’d hoped we’d laugh together, instead I got silence and a quick glance away. I guess the weariness is sinking in deeper than I admit. I want to reach across the space, the part of me that’s still gentle and optimistic whispering that we’ll find our way through this. But right now, it’s just hard to even get the words out without tripping over the exhaustion and the guilt. Tomorrow’s another day, they say, but it’s hard not to feel like we’re walking a tightrope stretched a little too thin. I need to remember that these moments don’t define us, even when they feel like they do. Maybe a better joke, or just a longer hug. Somehow, someway. ☕

The glow from my laptop is the only light in the room right now, and my eyes are starting to sting. I keep replaying the last conversation I had with Sam—if it even counts as a conversation when half of it was just awkward silences and me staring at my chipped nail polish. I guess I thought things would settle into some kind of rhythm by now, but everything feels off, like I’m walking around with one shoe untied. I tried to bring up where we’re headed, but it came out all wrong, like a bad punchline to a joke no one wanted to hear. My brain’s too foggy to make sense of what I actually want, except I know I don’t want to waste time on something going nowhere. There’s this underlying tension, and I can’t tell if it’s coming from Sam or if it’s just me projecting my usual skepticism about relationships. The walls feel closer somehow, or maybe that’s just the result of too many hours holed up with research articles and not enough sleep. I just wish I could get a straight answer out of myself—or out of Sam. Instead, I’m scrolling through old texts, trying to read between the lines, which is exactly as pointless as I imagine it sounds. Maybe I’ll sleep on it and things will make more sense in the morning, but honestly, I doubt it.

The plates from dinner are still on the table, and I can smell the leftover garlic from the chicken I cooked. Tonight felt more tense than usual. Mark hardly spoke, just scrolled through his phone, and I kept glancing at him, waiting for some sort of conversation to start. I tried asking about his day, but he just grunted and said he was tired. I know remote work has blurred the lines for both of us, but it’s like we’re living side by side rather than together lately. I keep wondering if it’s me, or if this is just what midlife looks like when the kids are grown and work seeps into every quiet moment. I’m restless, distracted by thoughts I can’t quite pin down. After dinner, I cleared the dishes and wiped the counters, but that didn’t help settle anything in my mind. I noticed how quiet the house was, just the ticking clock and the hum from my laptop in the other room. I keep thinking about whether nursing is still the right fit for me now that everything’s gone remote. I miss the hospital noise, the face-to-face moments with patients and coworkers. Sometimes I feel invisible here, like the work is endless and the boundaries don’t really exist. I wish I could talk to Mark about this, but every time I try to bring it up, he seems closed off. Maybe tomorrow will be different. For now, I’m just tired and hoping for some clarity or at least a better night’s sleep.

I'm tired but not in the sense that I can just crash. This morning in the kitchen felt like a battlefield with all the stuff I have to juggle. My laptop, phone, bills, random notes, all piled near the coffee maker while I was trying to make breakfast. I kept thinking, how am I supposed to keep track of everything when my income is all over the place? Freelance gigs don't come on a schedule, and the retail job is a grind that barely leaves me enough time to breathe. I know I should plan better but honestly, I don't have the patience or the time to create perfect systems right now. It added to this constant pressure that I’m not doing enough, which is stupid because I’m doing what I can. Still, I can’t shake this feeling that I’m scrambling instead of moving forward. I kept checking my phone to see if any work emails popped up, which just made me more anxious. There was one moment when I accidentally knocked over a container of sugar trying to type with one hand and hold a mug with the other. It was a mess—white crystals everywhere. I just stared at it, frustrated with myself for being so clumsy but also kind of laughing at how ridiculous the whole morning felt. It’s like I’m running on fumes and still expected to keep everything balanced perfectly. I hate that my skepticism keeps me from trusting the process sometimes, but maybe I need to be more patient. Anyway, the coffee finally kicked in, and I guess I have to get through today like this, rushing but steady enough not to fall apart. Hopefully, tomorrow feels less scattered.

There is something about a fall afternoon that makes me think I can see the future. Especially when there is the smell of a storm in the air. Did you know that in the Jewish calendar autumn is the beginning of the new year ? I think I have always sensed this even though I was not raised with this knowledge. I was taught it later in life.
I remember several autumn afternoons in my life when I felt this amazing pull. Almost as if one could pass into another dimension if one knew just where to stand, or just the proper words to utter. These moments have framed my perception of the world. They have convinced me that just beyond the clamor of modern life, there is an entire paradigm that is full of the magic that we lack. A world that is more open to possibilities than we allow ourselves, even in our age of technology. A reality that is not safe. Where one might be forever changed by watching water flowing over a stone or be propelled into enlightenment by a thunderstorm.
Oh, how we have kidnapped Wonder, and placed her in a tower surrounded by thorns like the Sleeping Beauty she is.
By our cynical and jaded views, we hold her captive in a cruel exile. We should be ashamed, but we boast about our sophistication and call ourselves immune to the gullible tales of the simple minded. But those very moments when we let go the reins of rationality are the gates to most excellent Joy. How foolish we have become. We trade real happiness for ersatz titillation and think ourselves wise. It makes me weep.
But I will not weep forever. Because in time, our world WILL be transformed, and all the doors will be flung open. Yes, at the expense of some of our most prized monuments, and stalwart modern doctrines. Let them fall I say, and let Wonder loose again in the world. Free to wreak havoc with the cynic in all of us, until we are weak with laughter at our former folly and our unbelief is washed away. May that time come speedily in our days. Amen

Suicide has always been a big thing in my life from a young age. I see people trying to commit everywhere on here, and I don't know what to do. I comment, I lead to resources, but it still feels like I'm not doing enough. It's crushing me that I feel like I'm not reaching people with my efforts. I wish I could just hug some of these people, and I don't even like physical contact. I wish I could let these people know they're not alone, that there are so many people who care about them, but it feels impossible with this platform. The worst part is that I see myself in a lot of them. I see the anxiety, the feeling like you're never enough, that no one actually loves you. I've never been suicidal, and I don't think I ever will be because I've seen what it does to people, to families, to friends. I would never do that to somebody I loved, even if they didn't love me. Even if I'm right and there is no one there, I know that I will always have God, and even if none of these people actually care about me, I know he does more than any person can dream of, and that keeps me from being suicidal. I see my boyfriend, and I couldn't bear to choose to do that to him, so that keeps me non suicidal, but what about the people who don't have that? What about the people who don't have a person to live for, or God to believe in, even in the tough times? What do you do for them other than give them reassurance, support, and love? How do I show them that life is worth living? How do I show them that nothing good comes from suicide?
I don't know, that's just something that has been weighing on me a lot today, I just had to get that off my chest and into the open. Ok, I'm going to end this, Bye.

Earlier this afternoon, I was standing in the hallway, calendar in hand, trying to figure out which parent pickup was mine and which was Jamie’s. I remember looking at all the sticky notes on the fridge (yellow ones are mine, blue ones are Jamie’s, the kids have their own colors too) and just feeling this weird sense of calm even though everything looked like chaos. I sat down at my bedroom desk to try to sort out the mess, laptop open to three tabs: school portal, work email, and a grocery list. The funny part is, I actually felt okay about it all. Maybe I’ve gotten used to the juggling. There was a moment when the phone rang and it was my son, asking if I could come to his rehearsal instead of Jamie, and I just wanted to say yes right away. But I had a meeting I couldn’t move, and he sounded disappointed but tried to hide it. That moment stuck with me for the rest of the day, just echoing in the background as I sent emails and booked appointments. I think what hit me was how much I want to be everywhere for everyone, but the logistics just won’t let me. Even coordinating with Jamie feels like running a small company sometimes. We managed, though. Later, when I checked the calendar one more time before dinner, everything was in its place. It’s not perfect, but it works most of the time. Sitting here now, the house is finally quiet, and I’m realizing that even though my days are packed and sometimes feel out of control, it’s the small moments like that phone call that make me stop and feel something real. I guess I’m grateful I noticed it instead of just pushing through. Maybe that’s the optimistic part of me. Tomorrow is another day of schedules and reminders, but for now, I’m just letting the quiet settle in.

Hi Diary,
Well Im feeling a lil sad at the moment. Just sad about this whole Dear Diary thing and how its changed.
And I guess I just have a lot of thoughts about it going thru my head, since I have opened up and shared with a few about having a online diary and my H finding it.
A few people I told had asked me why I would put something on without making it private or password protected. Granted they dont understand this whole website deal.
I used to write just for me. Nobody else ever saw. I never shared it. It was MINE. I have about 4 different journals, nobody that im aware of has read my real pen and ink ones.
And my early teenage year ones I dont think I would care.
I think back to high school and my creative writing class. We had a journal. Started out each class with the teacher giving us a word on the board, and we were not allowed to stop writing whatever came to our mind until she told us to stop.
THEN she would call a few of us randomly up to the front of the class to read it.
It wasnt like a full on diary type thing, but she wanted to write what came to our minds, and some were embarrassed at times reading.
It was really cool, the class wasnt a large one, it was an elective, so people that wanted to write were in there. But you had a mixture of a few popular guys, a few of the "nerds" the goth chicks, and a jock or so. It was really interesting because we all became close, Hearing one anothers writing, it was more intimate.
The teacher made a book at the end of the year combining pieces of our writings for all of us to keep. It was really special.
Why did I start sharing my diary. Well actually I think back, and it was during counseling with the H. I was also talking to another guy online at the time I had a internet crush on. He was in recovery groups and we were talking about feelings and sharing things, about speaking in a group,writing out our thoughts.
Then the counselor had the H and I make a list of things. Nice things to do for one another. I was working on it and Ink would pop online. We always just said Hello, kinda "How you doing" chit chat and then would just trail off into our own thing. So Im not sure why we both started sharing our writing and at what point he did also. I didnt tell him it was from a internet diary or anything. I just cut and pasted some things via email to him.
When I was at his place one day he showed me his real journals, and read some things to me. I was really touched and felt that he trusted me to do such a thing. Wow he was reading this to me???
So we started this exchange.
I didnt tell him about my diary right away. That came a little later.
Is it healthy to share you diary with others?
I guess this is what is in my mind now. Cause i find that I miss writing and people being able to read it. It became my new sort of therapy. It was still journaling, but now I had feedback, feedback from anonymous people, and feedback from the one man i trusted to read my thoughts. Who I knew was just as open and vulnerable to me as I was him. So I didnt worry with him.
I dunno, just letting some thoughts flow out here, gonna quit for now

Anyway, the air smells nice, and I'm not sneezing now.
