Friday was a grocery shop day. I got a few things done at home, and then Wendy came over in the evening for a visit, which was nice.

Saturday was taking my mom to the grocery store, and then I finally managed to put my new office chair together after three days of it mocking me (and a week of sitting on a broken chair). It wasn’t actually that hard . . . it took about half an hour including the unboxing. So now I have a new chair. Right now, I’m just very conscious of the fact that it’s not my old chair. It’s a bit different ergonomically. The arm rests are maybe an inch lower, which doesn’t sound like a lot, but I feel the difference when I’m using the mouse (I typically have to rest my forearm when I use the mouse otherwise I get elbow issues because my body is stupid). We’ll see what happens, but I might put the armrests from the old chair on the new chair (the attachment holes look like they’re spaced the same), or you can get pads for armrests (which would raise the resting surface up a bit). I tried another chair with adjustable armrests (which would have eliminated this issue), but I didn’t like that chair (and it was more expensive). I’m also having a hard time getting used to the back rest, which is one of the mesh ones (it seems that almost all the reasonably-priced chairs have those mesh backs), so it isn’t solid like my old one and it’s upholstered back rest. So my back feels kind of stiff (or maybe the muscles are just tired from holding a different position) after I’ve been sitting for a while. The new one has more seat padding than the old one, so that’s good. Hopefully I’ll get used to it in the next week or so. It is returnable for up to 30 days, but I didn’t really find anything else in my price range that I thought would be better, so it kind of feels like I either get used to this one or I’m screwed. Hmph.

Funnily, I was sitting on the old chair on Friday when I heard something hit the floor. I thought that what snapped on the chair (inside the piece that attaches the back to the seat) was plastic. But I found half a bolt on the ground that had clearly snapped off the other half (the other half was still attached inside somewhere). So that’s kind of wild. It’s just too bad those bolts that snapped aren’t accessible because replacing the bolts would have been easy. Oh well.

This whole “having a different chair” thing (especially when I’m not sure if my body will get used to it) just makes me feel stressed out. I’m not a fan of change. I sit in a lot of different office chairs at work, and some definitely leave me stiff by the end of the day. And sometimes I find myself thinking “thank goodness I get a different chair tomorrow). Well, with this new chair, it’s here to stay. And if I end up not liking it, I don’t know what I’m going to do. Perhaps I need to train myself to sit up straight without really using the back rest. I used to do that when I was younger because my physiotherapist told me strengthening my back so I could sit without leaning on the back rest would help with my jaw issues. So I used to be really good with sitting up straight. Perhaps this chair will force me back into that. 

The weekend’s other big chore has been taking everything out of my utility room and piling it up in my living room. I dislike the visual chaos of all that stuff in a place it shouldn’t be. It’s why unpacking after I moved here was so stressful - I just wanted all the Stuff put away so it wasn’t Everywhere. At least this is less stuff for a shorter amount of time. Next week, a technician is coming to clean all the dryer vents in the building, so we have to give them as much room as possible to work (our utility rooms are pretty tight). Most of my stuff is in storage containers, but I do have a small shelving unit in there as well, so that took a bit longer. 

But the biggest issue was something else. One of the previous owners built a makeshift cabinet that created a shelf above where the dryer hose connects to the building’s vent system - a fairly solid wooden box (with openings cut to slide around the dryer hose) which was cobbled together with various bits of cabinetry, panelling and scrap wood. It allowed more things to be stacked in there because the dryer hose does snake along a few feet of floor (which the shelf let you pile stuff above). I had to remove the box (that connection between the hose and the outlet would have been completely inaccessible otherwise), and it partially broke in the process. Additionally, inside and behind the box was so filthy with dust, dryer lint and assorted dinge that I just about gagged. Like that thing was either a health hazard, a fire hazard, or both. And that’s not even taking into account the random nail heads that were sticking out of it. I’ve never really been happy with having my stuff piled on top of this platform (which puts some restrictions on where you can put things). So I decided that this was a sign from the universe to finally deal with getting a proper storage solution for that corner. It’s money I don’t want to spend right now, but I was so disgusted by how much filth had accumulated, plus the box was partially broken in a way that reassembling it would have been difficult (and possibly leaving the box not as structurally sound). So today, I went scorched earth and completely demolished the thing. And that was quite a chore. I took almost 30 screws out of it, pulled out a whole bunch of nails of different sizes, and still had to go at it with a hammer and body weight to break it apart because it was also glued to high heaven. At one point, I was standing on one foot inside the box and using the other foot to push on the side to break the two pieces apart. The front appeared to be a cabinet door (that was still attached to another part with hinges. I made a huge mess in my kitchen (which was the best place to take it apart) and had to do a big clean-up operation afterward. 

I now have a box full of these panels and strips of wood that I have to take downstairs in a few shifts. We don’t have direct access to the dumpster, so I just have to leave pieces outside the utility room where the dumpster is. And I don’t want to leave the whole pile at once because the condo board might come after me for not disposing of my own “building materials” (there is a list of things we’re supposed to remove from the premises to dispose of due to size, and building materials is one of them). But if I just put a piece or two down there every few days, hopefully our caretaker just shrugs and tosses them in the dumpster.

Anyway, now I have to buy a utility shelf. I can assemble it such that the dryer hose threads through it so that I can use that vertical space that I don’t have on the floor. But because I have two very large storage totes that won’t fit (and there’s nowhere else to put something that size, in the utility room or otherwise), I’ll have to get some new storage totes as well and reorganize the stuff in the big totes (those big totes are started to get some cracks, so they would have been replaced soon-ish anyway). More surprise expense. Life loves throwing me surprise expenses around the holidays. GRUMBLE. 

Also, I need to leave a note on my dryer saying something to the effect of “Hello, if you have to move the laundry appliances, please make sure that when you put them back, both appliance doors are able to fully open without hitting the furnace.” Because there’s literally a centimetre of clearance right now, and if those machines aren’t put back properly, I’m certainly not capable of moving them myself.

So now let’s take that storage stress (and expense) and add it to the chair stress (and expense), and this is why I don’t want to go back to work yet.

The microwave hums behind me as I poke at a plastic salad container, not really hungry but needing a break from the constant parade of emails and texts. My phone buzzes with yet another reminder for a meeting I don’t remember agreeing to, and I have three sticky notes in my pocket with errands for after work—laundry, groceries, call the plumber. Lately it feels like my days are just a series of checklists stapled together, and I’m the guy with the red pen who never quite catches up. I can hear my partner’s voice in my head, asking if I remembered to book the appointment for her, and I know I’ll forget to mention something else when we talk tonight. It’s amazing how two people can be together for years and still misfire on so many small things. Maybe that’s just what happens when life starts to stack up—everyone gets drowned out by their own to-do lists. I’m supposed to be working on communication, but half the time I don’t even know what I’m trying to say, just that I’m tired of repeating myself or getting the details wrong. There’s a meeting in fifteen minutes, and I can’t even remember what it’s about. Maybe I’ll just fake it and hope nobody notices. The salad tastes like plastic, but at least it’s quiet in here for now.

The quiet hum of the air conditioner is oddly soothing during this rare moment alone at home. Late last night I was wrestling with ideas for my next piece, but my thoughts jumped all over the place, probably because I kept trying to juggle family stuff and deadlines at once. I really want to capture something meaningful, but every time I sit down to write, there’s a barrage of little tasks that pull me away—like reminding my brother about his appointment or sorting out dinner plans. It’s frustrating but also a bit familiar, this constant back-and-forth. I hope I’m patient enough to let the words come naturally rather than forcing them. Maybe when I get a moment of true privacy, the scattered ideas will settle into something clearer. I keep telling myself there’s optimism in the chaos, even if it feels overwhelming now. Hopefully, this break is enough to recharge so I can face the afternoon with less noise in my head. At least the light through the window is soft and calm, reminding me to breathe and not rush everything all at once.

Now I’m trying to focus on the rest of the week, but I keep drifting back to that call. I can’t quite shake the feeling that I’m not getting this coparenting thing right, even after all this time. The bus is packed and loud, which isn’t helping my restlessness. I just want to get home and turn off my brain for a bit.

Ok. That hat feels too tight for me. Although I am grateful for all congratulations. Is it something like being an Oscar Thing receiver – do we suppose to give a speech? Hope – not, as I’m not going to. And it wasn’t even my best entry. Oh, well…[sigh].
Anyway. This whole event made me think of a “Complimenting”.
Can you take compliments? How you respond to the compliments? And do you like to receive compliments more then to give them or opposite?
As long as I can remember myself, I never liked to receive a presents. The anticipation of having to say something when being given a present could make whole birthday a “notanticipated” event at all… I am not sure why it was that hard to say “thank you” and feel good. Maybe it was a question of being in a spotlight – it’s hard not to be for a birthday girl, isn’t it?
With age accepting becomes easier. I would “blame” it partly on hypocrisy that comes with age – we learn to live to socially acceptable norms, even if it means - learn to say commonly accepted things in commonly accepted situations. Anyway. Even if I still do feel a little uncomfortable with the gifts, more pain bring compliments. I’ve been told once that maybe I don’t like being complimented, because I “agree with the compliments, but feel rude for accepting them as fact”…Hmmm…no, I don’t think, that is the reason. But I don’t know the real reasons anyway.
Perhaps, the fact that compliments we get, often – about things, we not aware about us. What is the compliment, anyway?

Just got back from a slow walk around the block, jacket zipped up tight because the air’s still got that damp chill even though it’s supposed to be June. Every time I walk at night I end up thinking too much—tonight it was about who I’m even trying to be right now, and how I feel so all over the place but still oddly sure things will work out. The streetlights were flickering in that annoying way, and I kept dodging puddles while running numbers in my head again, groceries and rent and whether I can actually squeeze in that new set of pens for work. I can’t help but glance into other people’s windows, see little flashes of their lives, and wonder how together everyone really is behind those curtains. It’s weird how I can feel so focused on what’s next while also second-guessing if I’m even cut out for this version of adulthood I’ve landed in.

I texted Mark before I left, hoping he’d reply, but nada so far. The tension between us is like a pebble in my shoe—small but impossible to ignore, and I keep replaying last night’s conversation in my head, wishing I’d said something smarter or at least not sounded so defensive. Still, I’m stubbornly hopeful that we’ll sort things out, and maybe tomorrow will just be easier. My keys felt cold in my hand when I came back inside, and the hallway light was too bright, like it didn’t get the memo that I just needed a soft landing tonight. I wish I could just turn my brain off for a while, or at least slow it down enough to hear what I actually want amidst all this noise.

Early morning sunlight is coming in at a low angle, making the crumbs on the kitchen table look like a miniature landscape. I started writing out a list for the day on the back of a grocery receipt because I couldn’t find my sketchbook, which is probably buried under those reference photos from last night. There’s a weird tension in my chest, partly from thinking about everything I need to coordinate for the new installation, partly from that half-finished conversation with my partner about schedules. We’re still not great at this communication thing, even after all these years. I keep replaying our talk in my head, wondering if I was too abrupt or if I should have let things breathe a little more. 

It’s hard to juggle logistics when my brain wants to skip straight to the creative part. This afternoon is already overbooked: studio time, supply run, then trying to squeeze in a call with the gallery manager. There’s also the ongoing background noise of laundry, meal planning, and trying to not let dishes pile up. I know I need to check in with my partner before the evening, but finding the right moment feels like another task to schedule. Sometimes it feels like managing a relationship is just another project, except with fewer clear deliverables. I’ll try to be more present later, but for now my head is spinning with timelines. The toast is cold and my tea is getting that weird skin on top, but at least I got the list started.

There’s a sharp brightness in the parking lot this morning, sun glaring off the hoods of cars while I sit here before my shift. I can hear the distant beeping of trucks and people slamming their doors. It’s weird how normal everything looks even when my head is spinning with so much. I barely slept last night, thinking about how Mom’s appointment went and what the doctor said about her needing more tests. It’s hard to focus on debugging code or tracking my assignments for class when I’m so worried about her health. I keep checking my phone just in case there’s an update from Dad, but nothing yet. My mind keeps drifting between my to-do list for work and the possibility that things might get worse at home. I know I’m supposed to compartmentalize, but it feels impossible some days. There’s so much pressure to keep up with school deadlines and show up to work ready to problem-solve, but my thoughts feel scattered. I keep replaying conversations with my family in my head, trying to remember if I said the right things or if I missed something important. I want to be helpful and optimistic for everyone, but I don’t always know how. Even simple things like remembering to eat breakfast or pack my laptop charger seem like huge tasks when I’m anxious. I’ve promised myself I’ll go for a walk after work to clear my head, though I’m not sure if I’ll actually do it. For now, I just need to get through this shift and try not to let my mind wander too much. There’s a part of me that hopes things will settle down soon, but right now it’s just about making it through the day.

I know I should be reviewing notes or maybe going to bed, but I’m just sitting here at the table, staring at the mess and half-planning what I’ll do tomorrow. There’s a list in my head a mile long: work, classes, laundry, call Mom, pick up more pens since I keep losing them. Sometimes it feels like I’m juggling so many things I can’t even remember what’s in the air. But right now, I actually feel sort of calm, just letting things slow down for a second. Maybe I’ll just wash this plate and call it a night.

The house is quiet except for the faint hum of the refrigerator and the occasional creak from settling wood. Earlier today, I tried to talk with mom about her medications, but the conversation felt off. She said she understood, yet her eyes told me otherwise, maybe confused or just tired. I’m not sure if I explained things clearly or if she’s just overwhelmed, which makes me question whether I’m really helping or just adding to her stress.

I’m stretched thin as it is, managing classes and research while keeping an eye on her, and these moments weigh on me more than I like to admit. It’s frustrating because I want straightforward answers but keep running into vague responses. I guess all I can do is keep trying and hope that clarity comes with time. For now, all of us just need to get through one day at a time.

Earlier today, I was in the kitchen trying to update my resume between making lunch and dodging questions from my uncle about job interviews. Now it’s almost midnight, everyone’s asleep except for the TV humming in the living room (why do they always leave it on?). I’ve got my laptop balanced on my knees in bed, half my stuff scattered everywhere—notes, job descriptions, my old planner from last year. Every time I try to focus, someone knocks on my door or asks if I’ve eaten or if I can help with something small. I keep writing and erasing lines in my cover letter. It feels like everything takes three times as long in this house, especially at night when I want quiet but can still hear footsteps and the pipes clanking. Did I remember to finish that online application? Not sure. My to-do list keeps growing, and I’m starting to forget what I actually finished today. I wish I had a small desk just for myself, but there’s no space. It’s like my brain is just as crowded as this room. Maybe I’ll try again in the morning when everyone’s gone out, but for now I just want to close the laptop and breathe for a minute.

Channuka, Hannukah, Hannuka, Channukah. Which spelling is correct ?
All of them ! If you understand this, you understand something of Judaism. The point is not how to spell the word but to get on with the lighting of the candles already !
Just do it , was the slogan of the Jews long before Nike decided to use it .
Our menorah sits on a table in the kitchen by our front window so it can be seen from the street. Lighting it is such a quiet ritual, gentle and simple.
But it’s message is very profound. . A little light dispels much darkness.
What are we saying when we light our menorah at home ? That we believe in freedom of religion. And also the right to practice that religion in a semi-public way, from our kitchen window.
We went downtown last night to the capitol building and had a menorah lighting ceremony there. In front of the steps near where we stood, was a very large and beautiful Christmas tree. When I saw it, I was happy. I want people to be able to display the symbols of their faith. They have theirs, we have ours, and amen ! I don’t feel threatened by seeing a Christmas tree.
What I find truly puzzling is the fear that so many people seem to have that if any religious symbol is displayed in a public place that this means we are “violating” the separation of church and state. ( a phrase not found in the constitution by the way ) Let us be honest. What is SAYS is that the government shall not ESTABLISH a religion. And last I heard, the governor hasn’t made any resolutions declaring that all people in our state need to become Christians if they want to get a government job ! It’s PREPOSTEROUS to conclude that ANY display of religious ritual in public amounts to establishing that religion. We are only walking openly in the very freedom that America was founded upon. We are the most religiously diverse country on the face of the earth !
Let us celebrate this wonderful gift. Let us not try to drive the religious people among us into the closet. I THOUGHT our society had come to the conclusion that is was admirable to come out of there. . . .
Oy Hannukah, oy Hannukah, come light the menorah !

Another day of playing with my siblings—though this time, I tapped out earlier than I usually do. The past few days, we've been playing Apex for what… five to eight hours? That's basically a full work shift. I can already hear my sister teasing, "Rookie numbers." And yeah, in a way, it is. I used to play far longer than that, until I could feel my body completely crash out on me. But I'm well into my 30s now. I just… cannot.
And as much as I love playing with them, it's kind of hard to truly enjoy the game when I suck ass at it. I really appreciate that my siblings still intentionally invite me despite how little I contribute. Bots on hard mode? No problem. Human players? Completely different story. I'm constantly dying, and they're constantly reviving me. And being the emotional, impatient player that I am, I feel crestfallen whenever we lose.
I know—it's a pity party.
It's not like they blame me. They're actually very reassuring. "Okay lang 'yan." "That's fine, that's fine—next game ulit." And my brother—the best gamer I know—always throws in encouragement: "Nice revive!" "Nice ult!" "Nice kill!" It makes me embarrassingly giddy when he says those things, because I really do see him as that good. Still, I can barely feel a sense of victory in this game, and it's slowly driving me insane. Lol.
Like I said, I'm grateful they always include me. But if I don't enjoy something, I find it much harder to improve at it. So I'm gradually tapping out of game nights. Maybe. We'll see. There are small improvements between the first time I played and the nth time I'm playing now. It's not as fun as my single‑player games, but I still enjoy it—just a little.
I also want to write about this small, stupid, funny moment with my sister. She's usually the one who invites us to game nights. Earlier, my brother told her to turn on her AC before we headed to her room so it would already be comfortably cold by the time we started playing.
She squinted at him and said, "I'm starting to get the sense that you guys only go to my room for the AC, and not really to play."
My brother gave her a suspicious smile and laughed.
"I thought this was supposed to be genuine sibling bonding," she said. "You guys are just here for the AC."
I laughed too—especially because whenever she invites me over, I usually spend a good fifteen to thirty minutes just writing. She'll keep asking me to join the game, and I'll say, "Give me five minutes," which inevitably stretches into half an hour.
To be fair… she does have the best AC in the house.
Anyway—on to writing.
I've been wanting to write more because of a daydream prompt from Luisito. It made me think, What if I expand on this? I finished writing something, and I was genuinely happy with it, even if I know it's a little cliché. He appreciated it, and now he's expanding on it too—giving me more ideas. It's making me want to dive deeper into the story. My mind feels like it's overflowing with ideas, and I'm trying to catch them all before they disappear into the folds of forgetfulness.
I tapped out early from game night today because I wanted to keep writing. Writing has always been cathartic for me. And after losing over and over in Apex, I wanted a win.
Writing gave me that.
I haven't done anything monumental yet. I've mostly just fleshed out the three main characters—but oh my god, I was giddy doing it. I can hear that annoying voice in my head saying, "This is so cliché. This is obviously written by a wannabe writer." Shush. We're doing this. This is what makes my heart flutter. Don't ruin it.
The character sheets? Chef's kiss. Reading through what I made drowned out that stupid disappointment and that stupid voice telling me I'm a noob at my siblings' games.
I have a basic template for writing a book, and I'm going to follow it—just to give myself some structure. This probably won't be an active pursuit. More like a passive hobby. But who knows? Either way, I need organization. My mind is chaotic and cacophonous; it needs some rails.
I also finally responded to Luisito today. I appreciate him sharing his everyday daydreams with me—it gives me something to write about. I appreciate how engaging he always is. I know I sent him a story instead of replying to all his mini‑letters and a 2.5‑hour voice note after going quiet for two weeks—but still, he's just as talkative and engaged as ever. It still surprises me how easily he talks about anything, how he invites my thoughts in, how he doesn't just talk at me but actually responds and builds on what I say.
Anyway, I'm looking forward to his thoughts on the story. And I might—or might not—continue writing this on my own too.
I mean… I do want some alone time with my fictional black centaur of a stud. Lol.

This afternoon, I caught a glimpse of the new delivery schedule posted on the break room wall. It looked more complicated than last month’s, and I already know it’ll be a headache to manage with the team spread thin. Running numbers in my head, I can barely afford to mess up the hours because every overtime minute is under the microscope. On the bus home now, the usual noise feels heavier, like it’s pressing down on my thoughts. Tonight’s shift was brutal — three no-shows and two machines acting up meant I was scrambling the entire time. I kept thinking how much easier it would be if things simply worked as planned, but that’s never the case here.

I’m still sorting through bills in my head, trying to figure how to stretch the grocery run until next payday. No extra cash to throw at unexpected expenses. The whole week feels like a balancing act, juggling deliveries, team temperaments, and my own patience. It’s hard not to replay every decision and wonder if I missed something obvious. I told myself to stay optimistic, but it’s tough when the weight of reality keeps pulling me down. Tomorrow’s another long day, and I have to face the chaos again with a clear head or at least pretend I do. I just want to get home, lie down, and shut off the noise for a while. The city lights flicker past the window, and I’m counting the stops until my street. Hopefully, a little sleep will reset the brain clutter and I’ll find a way through this mess.

I just finished clearing my plate from dinner, and I keep replaying what happened this afternoon at work. There was this moment during break when a few of the guys were joking around, and I tried to join in, but the conversation just sort of shut down. No one was openly rude, but I could tell my comment didn’t land. It always seems like there’s some inside track I haven’t figured out yet. Maybe I’m overanalyzing, but it’s hard not to when I feel like an outsider. Moving to this new city, I knew building connections would be tough, but I didn’t expect to feel this tense every time I talk to someone. I wonder if it’s because I hold back or if I come off as standoffish. Sometimes I catch myself scanning for signs that people are annoyed or bored, which probably just makes me more awkward. I keep telling myself to relax, but it’s like my brain wants to catalog every possible misstep. I know I need to give it time, but it’s hard not to feel impatient or frustrated when everyone else seems at ease. Maybe I just need to find one person I click with instead of trying to fit into the whole group. I’m still glad I made this move, but days like today make me question whether I’ll ever actually feel settled here.

Feeling unsettled tonight. Dinner just finished and everyone scattered quickly, leaving plates, stray napkins, and a half-empty salad bowl on the table. The clatter of forks and the hum of conversation faded too soon, replaced by the muffled sounds of TV from the living room. I lingered at the table longer than usual, hoping for a quieter moment with my partner, but she seemed preoccupied, tapping away at her phone and barely looking up. It’s been tense between us this week, small misunderstandings piling up into something heavier. I wish I knew how to break through the awkwardness, but every attempt feels forced and awkward, so I hold back more than I should.

I sometimes wonder if I’m drifting away from the person I thought I was—someone open and spontaneous, eager to connect. Lately, I don’t recognize myself; I second-guess what to say, how to make things better without creating more distance. Maybe this is what happens when privacy is so hard to come by and everyone’s schedules keep colliding instead of syncing. I have the urge to just pack up my notebook and write somewhere else, but I know that’s escaping, not solving. For now, I’ll settle for jotting these thoughts down here, hoping tomorrow brings a lighter mood.

All issues since 1997 can be found at its official site https://www.economist.com/weeklyedition/archive. When it comes to writing, it comes easy for me to write my feelings, experiences, and get my thoughts of the day written. Yes, the World Wide Web (WWW) is not safe, I have come across
DD
in 2001. Finding DD was a godsend and a great joy when I ran across it looking for diaries. The creation of DD has become my home away from home in 2001 and 25 years later Dear Diary has come back to its (practically) former glory earlier this year or late 2024, I have not found other online diaries that satisfied my pallet of writing. Now I know I have many diaries or journals at Dear Diary (DD) and I write a lot, I have to admit that I will write a lot during the week, but my diaries and journals are my works of words going across the screens of monitors, windows, and whatever we call some things these days. More than one word can mean the same or similar word or thing.
So, sitting here, in my living room, waiting for my caregiver Jackie to get get with lunch from Taco Bell, after her appointment, I am watching and listening to the tv program titled The UnXplained (as the title is) with William Shatner, I am finding it the right time to get my thoughts in order and write away my life of the day the best I can while at home enjoying the peace and quiet of my space as the only sounds of the tv is the only loud noises of the apartment. Now, when it comes to having my space with nothing else in it may be nice at times like this, I do find having time for myself after my caregivers gone for the day a wonderful thing in my way of thinking.

I know I have mentioned before so please don’t hold it against me that I repeat myself all the time. I don’t mean to be a broken and scratched record on its turntable, okay? Please bear with me and be patient. Sometimes it takes me a while to say what I want or need to say. Thank you for understanding. That is one reason I am so glad to know that Dear Diary has pretty much saved my life’s sanity at some point in my world — a world that sometimes spins a lot faster than our earth does through its days, months, years, and 5 decades of my own life.
I love using the MacOs or iOS program called Pages. At one time I have found this program plain and boring. Today, after ending my $6.99 subscription a month using MS365 online in January or February when my debit card had to be changed due to fraudulent activity, I have been careful where my debit card is used. If I can, from now on, where I can, I will use my bank account numbers instead of my debut card to get rid of headaches that creep up every now and then I cannot explain where my money goes. Pages is free on your iPhone, iPad, and MacOS whereas you have to pay $6.99 to$9.99 a month to $80-$120 a year for MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook. Pages, Numbers, and Keynote, Notes are free to use with your Apple products which are iPhones, iPads, Apple watch. I think at one time Apple watches were called iWatch but I can be wrong. Don’t take what I said about Apple watches and set it in stone as what they may have been called so long ago.
Pages is go to word processor these days! I love how it lays out when using the program today than several years ago. The creators of Pages, Numbers, and Keynote have created a fine usable system to write my diary entries at before copying and pasting them to my diary pages at Dear Diary. Although it is my opinion, I do want to say, if you prefer android and Microsoft Windows over Apple products, you have that right to like it over Apple products. Everyone has their preference. I know my preferences even though I use both at times during the week. Today I prefer my Apple products over android and Microsoft Windows versions. I have knowledge of both from having some type of computer in the home since I was 17 years old. My first computer system was a Commodore C64—a Christmas gift from my mom and stepdad Lonnie in 1987. It was my first gaming and writing system for a few years. There was a program called WordPerfect I enjoyed using when I used Windows OS, and for the life of me, MS365 has become its best program for Windows. WordPerfect doesn’t exist anymore… Or does it? Now I am curious.
Changes
Since writing has become my life on a daily to regular basis, I do have to admit that changes is always happening in my days of writing. Some days I have very little to say that makes sense to I have a lot that doesn’t make sense. At least that is how I see it at times. My life isn’t burning, per se, but it is definitely not ordinary. Changes? Something I find hard to accept in areas of my life — true enough — but something to be done once in a while. Practically every day I find myself dealing with some kind of change I am not always ready to accept but later finds done for the beat along the way in life sooner than later. Maybe?! Acceptable, I guess.
More Later
I have a lot more to say, but I will wait for a while.

Have you ever seen a pantomime on the streets: mime would do that funny moves, as if he is behind a glass wall and can’t get through it? He would be pawing over the invisible barrier, making anxious faces and it would look like that wall is there for real…
Barriers set up by us. Boundaries. Artificial or natural, it is us, who define them.
From time to time we stumble upon them, when walking new paths. Some boundaries are – our own creations, others – those of others. Which one you’d prefer? Certainly it’s better when what stops you – your own limits. Physical, or moral or religious, anything really…Everyone has got different limits and that’s natural – everyone is different.
Does it hurt when you hit someone else’s barrier? Sure it does. Is there an alternative? A way to avoid collision? Doubt that there is…The very point of a boundary is – you hit it, because you don’t see it! But isn’t it the way to learn – to run against the walls and take upon the bruises from the clash?
“The more we live, the more we learn, the more we know…”
Killing has its boundary. The amount of hate or frustration one has defines how far one can go. I’ve witnessed how such boundaries gets moved out of proportion under certain circumstances.
It happened when I graduated from school; there was that war in Afghanistan. Due to compulsory military service my male classmates had to go through that rigorous soldier's duty…Few never returned. Those who came back, changed. We talked. They described how terrifying it was – to do your first killing. After the first one next has been easier and so was every next shot. The barrier of killer’s brute appeared to get broaden and there were no more moral stopper to kill a human. Most of them ended up as bouncers, or body guards for the mafia’s big men. Only few choose civil professions. Once stretched, boundaries almost impossible to narrow back down.
Animals kill without hesitation – their boundaries lies very wide, limited only by the fear of starvation – natural boundary.
If somebody will ask me “…could I kill someone for real?”
My answer would probably be – it depends on what limits that person has. I would like to hope that theirs boundaries would not be natural like those of animals, but more of – moral, set up by human, about human, for human. Killers simply unable to comprehend and control their instincts – how then they different from animals?...
Love has its boundary too. Despite of millions of famous quotes about “unlimited love”, still – I believe that you can only love that much – as much as you are able to give. When you've got nothing left to give, a glass wall of sympathy will be built.
And the mime will never get through.
There are so many boundaries in our lives. It would be good to know them, although no one does and I think - no one ever will. You can try in order to learn or you can just learn it from the others, who already have experience in crossing. Either way - it is - your responsibility and it will be you to stand in front of the judge when you violate your boundaries.
Your desire for an illusion is like a wing.
This wing will take you to Reality ...
Preserve the wing; do not feed the desire
this wing of desire will take you to Paradise.
People think they are enjoying themselves:
in reality they are tearing their wings apart for the sake of an imaginary form…
[Rumi]

This morning I forgot to send that email to the client before leaving the apartment. It’s annoying how one small slip can set off a chain reaction in my day. Now I’m at this corner table in the coffee shop, laptop open, but my mind keeps jumping between job applications, chasing down invoices, and figuring out if I even want to keep freelancing. I’ve made a rough schedule on my phone, but it feels useless when every task comes with its own set of follow-ups and possibilities of rejection. 

I’m tired of juggling a hundred little things that don’t add up to anything solid yet. Some days I think about giving up and getting a regular job, but that feels like admitting I failed at finding a real path. That uncertainty eats at me more than I expected. The coffee helps a bit, but it won’t fix the backlog of incomplete tasks or the restless feeling that I’m stuck in this no-man’s land between survival and actual progress.

The lamp on my desk hums softly as I sit here, rubbing my temples and staring at my half-finished assignment. I can still hear the echoes of the argument with my sister earlier this evening. She said I was being distant again, always busy, always too tired to really talk. I tried to explain how stretched thin I feel with school and taking care of Mom, but I could tell she thought I was just making excuses. It stung more than I expected. 

I know she means well and wants to help, but sometimes her comments just make me feel more alone. There’s this constant sense that I’m not doing enough for everyone, and it gets heavier when I sense resentment from her. I replayed her words over and over while making dinner, and even now, her tone lingers in my mind. I wish she could see how much I’m juggling, but I also wonder if I’m shutting her out without realizing it. It’s hard to be open when I’m anxious about barely keeping it together myself.

Now, the house is quiet except for the ticking clock and my own restless thoughts. I keep thinking about whether I should text her an apology, or maybe just let things cool down. It’s hard to know what the right move is. I want to be there for my family, but some days it feels impossible to meet everyone’s needs. Maybe when I wake up tomorrow, things will look clearer, but right now I just feel tired and a little lost.

I feel better.

The hum of the fridge is louder than usual in this tiny kitchen, and the sunlight sneaks in through a crack in the blinds, spotlighting the crumbs I forgot to wipe up. Last night was a weird mix of relief and nerves—I finished my readings for tomorrow early, but my mind wouldn’t stop spinning. I keep wondering if the people I met at orientation last week will actually text me or if it was all just polite small talk. I’m honestly tired of playing the friendly stranger. It’s exhausting to keep introducing myself and pretending I’m not sizing everyone up, trying to decide who seems real and who’s just here for the ride. I caught myself scrolling through old photos of friends back home around midnight, which didn’t help. I always say I’m optimistic, and I mostly am, but there’s this undercurrent of doubt every time I try something new. The city is still a jumble of unfamiliar streets and faces, but it’s starting to feel less alien. I walked to the campus library after dinner, just to see what it looked like at night, and the quiet there was weirdly calming. Ate a granola bar at 11 p.m. because I was too anxious to sleep and too lazy to make anything else. I know I’ll probably find my people eventually, but right now it feels like I’m in this holding pattern—busy, yes, but not really connected yet. I made a to-do list for today during lunch, even though I know I’ll end up crossing off maybe half of it, if I’m lucky. Still, it feels good to have some structure, even if it’s just a bunch of sticky notes and reminders on my phone. I guess I’m just hoping the next week feels a little less like drifting and a little more like building something real.

I started the morning by double-checking the family calendar on my phone, only to realize I’d missed an early email about a school event for Jamie next week. That set the tone for the day—constantly feeling like I’m one step behind, even when everything is technically under control. Work was a blur of meetings, mostly remote, and I kept one eye on my Slack notifications while coordinating pick-up with Alex. I still worry that we’re not communicating enough about the kids, but every time I bring it up, it feels like I’m overanalyzing. The living room is finally quiet now, just the faint hum from the fridge and some traffic outside. I noticed, while folding laundry this evening, that my patience was better than usual—maybe because I reminded myself to take a few deep breaths between tasks. Sometimes I wonder if I’m too hard on myself about the little things, like forgetting to sign a permission slip. It’s hard to know where the line is between responsible and obsessive. I keep all of this to myself because I doubt anyone else is interested in my constant internal audit. Still, writing it down makes me feel a little lighter.

My hands were still sticky from slicing tomatoes when I got home tonight, and all I could think about was the mess in the kitchen sink. I ended up calling Mom this morning before my shift because she left me a message saying she needed help with something at the house, but I was running late and didn’t really listen to the whole voicemail. She sounded tired on the phone, way more than usual, and I kept thinking she was about to ask for money or something I couldn’t give. I tried to keep the conversation short, but she kept circling back to Dad and how she misses him, which I never know how to handle. I wanted to say something comforting, but I was distracted, half-watching the clock and thinking about my prep list for the day. She asked if I was eating enough, which kind of pissed me off even though I know she means well. I snapped at her without meaning to, told her I had to go, and hung up. Now I keep replaying that in my head. Was I too harsh? I wish I could just be more patient, but lately, everything feels like it’s pressing in on me. Money, work, missing Dad, and trying to keep it all together. I want to call her back and apologize, but it’s late and I don’t really know what I’d say without making it weird. Maybe tomorrow I’ll feel clearer. Or maybe I’ll just keep putting it off.
Haven't written in a few days. Been busy with end of year stuff. Nothing major to report, just the usual chaos of the holidays. Ready for things to calm down a bit.

I felt unsettled tonight sitting on the couch, the house quiet except for the hum of the fridge in the other room. My mind kept replaying that interaction with Marco at work, the way he cut me off in front of the new line cook, made me feel small in my own kitchen. I know I’m supposed to be the one setting the tone, but lately I feel like a guest in my own space, watching people talk over me and questioning if I’ve lost my edge. I came home and looked at the receipts again, tallying up the week’s groceries and supplies, double-checking the numbers, feeling my heart race with every total. It’s exhausting to work so hard and still feel like I’m barely treading water, both at work and at home. I want to believe I can turn things around, but some days that hope is just a whisper, hard to catch. Maybe I’m too intense, too quick to react, but it’s how I’ve always gotten by. Tonight, after the lights were off and the kitchen was finally quiet, I found myself wondering if I’ve become too much for people, or maybe not enough. I keep thinking about how much I used to love the chaos of the dinner rush, the way everyone relied on me to pull things together. Now I’m anxious before every shift, worried someone’s going to challenge me or that I’ll miss a bill at home. I wish I could talk to someone about all this, but I don’t want to sound like I’m complaining. So I sat here, staring at the ceiling, telling myself tomorrow I’ll handle it better, but not really believing it. I just want to feel like myself again.

Feeling kind of frustrated and a little lost after last night and then waking up early today, still with everything swirling. Desk is a mess—last night’s crumpled notes, half a banana peel, my work laptop open but not actually doing anything. I keep replaying that conversation with her, can’t seem to let it go. We both kept interrupting each other, and I know I got defensive about the timing of my classes and group projects. Wish I’d just said, yeah, it’s a mess right now and I get it, but instead I started laying out my calendar and talking in circles. She got quiet, which is always worse than her being mad. I could tell she was hurt but I barely managed to say anything helpful. Then I stayed up late reading articles for class that I barely absorbed, kept checking my phone out of habit, nothing useful there. Eyes feel gritty this morning, everything feels slightly off-balance.

Supposed to be working on a project plan for work but all I can think about is whether I should text her or just wait. Can’t focus on the Gantt chart, keep looking at the sticky notes stuck to my monitor—half of them are reminders for stuff I haven’t done. My mind jumps from deadlines to the look she gave me when I brushed her off, to whether I’ll even keep up in class this week, back to work again. I know I need to apologize but I don’t want to sound like I’m making excuses. Wish I could just stop overthinking and actually fix something. Light outside is kind of gray, which matches my mood, I guess. Might try to write her a note. Or maybe I should just clean up this desk first, see if that helps.

I realized halfway through my shift that I'd forgotten to pack a snack again. It’s strange how tiny routines like that start slipping when everything else feels unsettled. The bus is humming, almost empty, and I keep tapping my fingers against the seat, trying to remember the last time I felt truly rooted somewhere. The city is still unfamiliar—every street looks similar, but none of them hold any memories for me yet.

I keep wondering what it means to feel at home. Is it just about time, or is there something else I should be doing to settle in? The regulars at the café have started to recognize me, but I’m not sure I’ve recognized myself lately. My mind drifts back to earlier, weighing whether I’m just going through the motions or actively shaping something here. Maybe I’m overthinking it, but the uncertainty feels persistent.

The sun is starting to set, casting those long shadows through the dirty bus windows. The driver’s radio is playing some old pop song, muffled and tinny, almost comforting in its predictability. I’m calm, but there’s this undercurrent of restlessness. The move was supposed to be a fresh start, but so far it’s just made me more aware of the gaps in my day and the way I fill them.

I know I’m patient, or at least people tell me I am, but I don’t know how that helps when it comes to figuring out who I am in a new place. Maybe I’ll try a new route home tomorrow, or stop by the park before work. Small steps, I guess. For now, I’ll just watch the city pass by and hope that these small choices add up to something that feels like belonging eventually.

This morning, while pulling espresso shots during the early rush, I noticed how the steam swirled oddly in the air, catching the light from the window just right. It was a small moment, but it made me pause, even if only briefly. Now on my lunch break, the café feels like a refuge, quiet compared to the chaos earlier. I’m sitting by the back corner, sipping on a black coffee, trying to map out my thoughts without much luck. Work has been nonstop, and it’s hard not to feel drained by the constant flow of customers and the pressure to keep everything running smoothly.

Lately, I’ve been thinking a lot about this new relationship, wondering where it’s headed. There’s that sweet, gentle warmth when we talk, but I can’t ignore the little anxious whispers asking if we’re on the same page. I don’t want to overthink it too much, but my mind jumps ahead, imagining all these what-ifs. Balancing this with work feels overwhelming at times. I wish I could just fast forward and see if this is something stable or if it’s destined to be just another fleeting chapter. For now, I guess I’ll hold onto these moments and try not to let the uncertainty overshadow the good ones.

Well. I survived the visit from middle child. He arrived around 1pm yesterday and left at 6am this morning and we did A LOT of talking in between. A LOT. Because there was a lot that needed unpacking. We tackled a lot of material, from his job losses and current job, to his wife/divorce, the tumor, his childhood. I was honest. I felt vulnerable at times, fearful that he would use what I said against me sometime in the future. I think he left with a better understanding and with a sense of feeling loved. He seemed happier this morning. I did emphasize several times throughout the day that this issue or that issue is where a therapist could really help him find the tools to deal with it. I think the visit can be summarized as:
He was TRAUMATIZED during the one year spent in Liberia with the Peace Corps. The very fact that he is brought to literal tears talking even briefly about it 8 years later tells me that there is a lot still unresolved and I do believe the experience now affects how he approaches the world.
He does not want a relationship with his siblings. He views them as cruel and says they pick on him all the time when they are together. I was present at several instances he mentioned and there was no cruelty and i don't understand where he is coming from. But he says even if it isn't true, that it is his feeling and the way he feels is not right or wrong. It makes me sad and uncomfortable, forced to have "two" families.
Is he on the autism spectrum? Possibly. Is he extremely sensitive? Yes. Is he socially awkward? Most definitely. But instead of seeking help (therapy) to adress some of these issues, he has resigned himself to being alone and friendless for the rest of his life. At the age of 31.
He continues to bring up suicide. I struggle because I know if that is what he is intent on doing, there is nothing I can do to dissuade him. I am leaving my heart and my door open so he knows I am there for him always. That I am a safe place for him. I am gently trying to get him to therapy without making him feel he is broken. But he is so dead set against taking a pill, even though I explain not all solutions and tools are pills.
(Happy that I
finally
found the button to get out of the numbered bullet points.)
So, like I said, I survived. I did the best I could. I gave him insights. And sent him on his way. And he said he would like to visit again sometime.
I am emotionally spent.
Wish I had someone to unpack all I now carry as a result of this visit.
Otherwise....
Christmas Eve was nice. Honey and I had babyback ribs and mac n cheese and potato salad, with gingerbread cake for dessert. After dinner, we exchanged gifts--he gave me a set of screwdrivers which was really thoughtful because two of mine disappeared as we renovated this house. We started on the jigsaw puzzle (finishing it xmas morning) and watched A Carol For Christmas, a 1964 Rod Serling-directed take an A Christmas Carol. Interestingly, the main character's thinking/attitude was so similar to our current POTUS that I turned to honey during the movie and said to honey that the demented one must have seen the movie as a young man and used the character a role model on which to base his current attitude.
Today, I recover from the emotional and physical toll the visit took on me. The only thing I have planned is to wash the bedding. Open Diary has been down again for two days, so I can't work saving pictures as I had planned.

My nervous system was already shot when C texted the group on Tuesday morning to ask if he could stop by the Center to see us. That brought everything to a screeching halt. J and I got the text at the same time and had the same reaction: “WHAT??”

I asked C, “are you here?”

He didn’t respond for another 20 minutes or so. This had J and I reeling. C is our colleague from the DR. Nobody had mentioned that he was coming to visit and his boss had made it clear that she didn’t feel comfortable sending her Latino team members to the US this year… and for very good reasons. (cough La Migra cough) Was C just teasing us?

He wasn’t teasing us. He was, in fact, in town… and he showed up at work about an hour later.

The weather has been terrible. We had high wind on Tuesday - 38 mph gusts! - and heavy rain on Wednesday. Still, we bent over backwards to accommodate him. He took very good care of me in DR last year and is getting ready to do it again next month. I wanted to make sure he had a good time with us.

I ended up throwing together a night out on Wednesday so we could all just hang out and socialize. M was out of town, but R and J agreed to join in. We also invited S and J, both from different departments. We ended up going out to dinner. We ate Mexican, which was best for everyone’s dietary restrictions and preferences, though J gave us some light shit about it. (“Oh I see how it is. Mexican for the Mexican, huh?”) Then we drove out to see the lights at the Plaza and get some ice cream at a great GF ice cream joint.

I brought C home from work with me on Wednesday night while we were staging to get ready to drive out and meet up. We stopped by the grocery store and picked up some candy for him to take back to the rest of the crew in DR and then I introduced him to my family, the dogs, and Inti. Inti was afraid of him at first but quickly warmed up to flying to him. It was a little awkward for about 45 minutes while we waited for R. Chad later confessed that he had a difficult time understanding what C was saying because of his thick accent. But it was okay.

We talked shit about our bosses over dinner. We probably shouldn’t have, but we all work on different teams and it was refreshing to see that we all endure similar organizational frustrations at work. I laughed so hard I couldn’t breathe and tears were just rolling down my face when J recounted the story of last week’s fire drill.

It was a much-needed distraction from the looming euthanasia we had scheduled for Thursday morning. That whole process has been so heavy and stressful for so many reasons. I’m so glad I have a good therapist to help me process it…

… and I was grateful for the distraction that C brought. I felt a little manic and out of control. I think I was just unmasked more than I usually am. A necessity for survival for times like these.

C is leaving just before the party on Sunday. That kind of sucks. I won’t see him again until next month when I visit DR. But I feel like I did the best I could to make him feel welcome. The weather just didn’t cooperate to get to show him some good bird flights. I strongly encouraged him to give us a better heads up next time so we can plan for him. It wasn’t entirely his fault; he found out he was being sent to the states just days before he left and didn’t know he’d end up here until the day before he booked the ticket.

Woke up early again, 5:40 or something like that. I heard the neighbor’s dog barking through the thin kitchen window while I was just trying to toast some bread, and I thought about how I don’t know any of the people here yet. I still can’t remember where I packed the butter knives—using a steak knife for my toast feels ridiculous, but whatever, it works.

Now I’m standing here waiting for the kettle, scrolling through my phone and feeling that tightness in my chest again, thinking about yesterday’s awkward conversation at work. Tried to laugh along with the new team, but I could see some of them glancing at each other when I brought up the last project. Did I come off like I was criticizing? I always worry I’m too blunt, or maybe just not fitting in at all.

I keep telling myself it’s just a phase, all this moving and starting over, but the practical side of me wants to just fix everything already. Make some friends, find a routine, stop feeling so restless in this house that still smells like paint. But then I end up fussing over stupid details, like the way the mugs don’t line up in the cupboard.

Guess I should get ready for the day. Calendar’s packed. I’ll try not to overthink every small thing, but that’s just what I do. Maybe things will settle down eventually.

I kept thinking this afternoon about that phone call with Mom, when she told me about Aunt Maria’s test results. The way her voice shook made my stomach twist. I was in the middle of editing a client’s project but everything just blurred after that, and I ended up staring at my laptop for half an hour, not really seeing anything. Now it’s after dinner and I’m just sitting at the table, picking at the edge of a placemat and replaying the conversation in my mind, wondering if I should have asked more questions or said something different. My partner sat across from me, quietly scrolling through their phone, and I could feel this thick silence between us even though we’re both trying to be careful around each other lately.

I wanted to talk about what’s going on with my aunt, but I hesitated, like I always do, because I’m not sure if I’ll sound dramatic or just make things heavier than they already are. Maybe I’m overthinking, but I keep second-guessing myself about everything I say and do, especially around family stuff. My chest feels tight—maybe from anxiety, maybe from just holding it all in. I know I should reach out again, maybe see if Mom needs anything, but every time I pick up my phone I freeze. It’s weird how just a few words from someone you love can mess with your whole day. I wish I could just relax and talk about it, but it feels like every sentence will come out wrong. I keep telling myself to just try, but it’s like I’m stuck in a loop.

Phone buzzing in my lap, keys still in the ignition, and I’ve managed to spill protein bar crumbs all over the passenger seat again. 7:42 pm, edge of the lot, sun just dipping behind the ugly brick building across the street, and I’m early for once. The windows are fogging a little from my breath—guess I’m more anxious about tonight’s intake session than I thought. New client, new issues, and I’m already running through a dozen scenario trees in my head. I keep thinking about how I don’t actually know anyone well enough here to just call and decompress after work. Funny, I tell people to build support networks all day. Maybe I should write myself a prescription for my own advice.

It’s loud in my head—lots of shoulds and maybes. I keep checking my watch, as if that’ll speed things up. Noticed a weird buzzing sound from the dashboard but can’t decide if it’s something mechanical or just my brain making up problems to fix. I left my lunch tupperware under the seat again; smells like old broccoli. I’m trying to focus on the positives: work is steady, I’m learning the city inch by inch, and the grocery store clerk finally recognized me tonight. Tiny victories, I guess. I’ll go in soon, smile, listen, and maybe by the end of the night I’ll feel like I belong a little more here. For now, just me and the crumbs, waiting for the next thing to happen.

The break room lights flicker a little, and the hum from the soda fridge is the loudest thing in here right now. I finally got to sit down and eat my sandwich, and it feels like I’ve been running nonstop all morning. Customers were already lined up before I even clocked in, and I swear some people come in just to complain. I try to keep my patience, but it wears thin when I know I’ve got to leave on time to check on Mom. She called once already asking if I’d picked up her prescription. I haven’t yet. I’ll have to swing by the pharmacy after work, and I’m not looking forward to the traffic. Sometimes I wonder if things will ever slow down. I keep telling myself it’s temporary, but every week feels the same. The manager’s been on my case about restocking shelves faster, but I’m just trying to make sure I don’t mess up and forget anything important. My lunch is half gone and I barely tasted it. I need to remind myself to eat slower, but there’s always something else to think about. I’m hopeful that maybe next week I can ask for a day off, though I’m not counting on it. For now, I just have to get through the next few hours, then get Mom settled, then maybe I’ll have five minutes to myself.

I didn’t want to start something, so I just sat there, scrolling on my phone, not really paying attention to anything. The room felt crowded and tense even though it was just the two of us. I kept thinking about how we used to get along better, but maybe it’s just the stress of everyone being crammed into one house.

Eventually I gave up and went to bed, still kind of frustrated. Woke up feeling foggy, like I didn’t really sleep. I want to fix things but I’m not sure how to start. Wish I had more space to just breathe for a bit.

I’m sitting on the couch, my knee bouncing a little while I scroll through old texts from last night. There’s a weird aftertaste from the cereal I just ate, and I keep replaying the argument with Jamie in my head. It started so small: she asked if I could chip in for groceries this week, and I kind of snapped without meaning to. I know money’s tight for both of us, but I felt like she was blaming me for not pulling my weight, which sucks even if it’s not what she meant. I probably sounded defensive, talking too loud and cutting her off. She just got quiet and said she’d figure it out herself, then disappeared into her room. The silence afterward felt huge. I hate when things get like this, but my brain was all over the place, thinking about bills and the store schedule and whether I could even pick up an extra shift. Now I’m stuck here, wishing I’d handled it differently but also annoyed that I have to keep proving I’m trying. Am I overreacting, or is she just not getting how stressed I am? I keep thinking about apologizing but don’t know what words won’t come out wrong. Maybe I should just leave a note before I go to work, something simple. I don’t want this hanging over us all day, but I also feel like I’m always the one who has to fix things. Still, I miss how easy things felt between us before all this money stuff started creeping in. I wish it was just about groceries and not everything else piling up. My head feels too full to sort any of it out right now, but I know I need to do something before it gets worse.

Sitting in front of a blank screen. Feeling a little “arty”. A screen is a canvas, where I am about to paint my picture. I am looking out for some colours and a brush…And I am thinking…Of what I’d like to paint. My life, perhaps? Or just a tiny bit of my mind? Either way – it’s a thoughts being caught and pinned with the words. It’s not the real 3D-dimensional illusion, just unsophisticated flat painting…So not really the real thing, isn’t it? But at least – it will be mine…
I would put a foundation into that picture. A Love and a Kindness. I might be one of those incorrigible dreamers, but I still believe in those. I try to remember to love and to be kind, even when there is urge to hate. I can’t manage it sometimes…Nobody’s perfect…
I’ll add few colourful strokes of hope and faith. Not too much, coz I don’t want the picture to appear too mixed up.
In the middle of that picture will be – I. I look at my photo – I don’t like how I look on photographs…Even often I can’t believe that it is me on there. I used to see myself differently. Guess, we all do. But that’s the way human’s sensors work – eyes will see what’s on outside, hearts - inside.
I wonder if this is true, that in afterlife all souls will be free and then we will see each other “naked”. Sometimes in a moment of despair I wish that we could make this happened in our realm. But maybe then we would be scared away with what we saw…
I will paint myself the way I see me. The way I like me and the way I am – me. (hmmmm..might turn out to be not such a pretty picture after all…lol) nah – of course it’ll be Perfect!
Being there, in the middle of a picture, actually means, that despite of any thing I still have some good thoughts about myself, which is good, right? Maybe – a little selfish, but hey – you’ve got to love someone, what’s wrong if that someone is – you?!
Now – got to be careful here, as its time to smudge a bit that bubble of illusions of mine, make it paler and lighter. Don’t need too much of these anymore. Getting older brings advantage…
Well, not much left to add now – only few brush waves here and there of seriousness, flippancy, impatience, reasoning, naivety, wit and invariable fairness. A few drops of tears, perhaps and a little cute smile in the corner…Its amazes me that when it comes to say few words about yourself, suddenly all the words have gone into hiding…Am I that unfamiliar with me or just refuse to recognise certain things?
Anyway – the picture is almost ready, as it’s up to imagination of the viewer to fill in missing details. Frame this into the borders of responsibilities and – there you go – a Perfect Picture.
[hammeres in a big thick Nail and hangs the Picture. Steps back and admires for a second. Then takes it down and into recycling bin]

The soup on the stove is barely simmering, and the clock says 1:13 pm. I keep looking at my phone, expecting a message from her, but nothing. Lunch break should feel like a pause, but my mind keeps going back over the argument from last night. She said I don’t listen, and maybe she’s right. Hard to tell when everything feels like it blurs together—work, calls, family stuff, all at home. I keep second-guessing if I should apologize again or just wait. My mom’s voice in my head is no help, just a mix of worry and guilt about how we’re all doing since Dad got sick. 

I nibble on a leftover roll and wonder if everyone else feels this pressure, or if I’m just not cut out for this. Remote work sounded easier, but it’s not. The walls feel closer on days like this. I want to believe things will get better but I’m not sure what the next step is. For now, just watching the soup, waiting for a sign, and thinking too much.

"An Abuser's New Partner as His Leading Ally"
Paul had divorced his wife and was now seeing Laura. Laura felt terrible for Paul because he was such a sweet man and his ex wife was accusing him of having abused her. Laura was determined to "Be there" for Paul, and even hoping to help him win custody because his ex wife was "out of control". Dozens of ex partners of my clients have described how the abusive mans new partner takes on a role similar to Laura's: "His girlfriend is worse than he is. She talks to me like I'm dirt and she spreads bad things about me. Id almost rather deal with him. I think she outs him up to some of the stuff he does. Shes a itch."
Perhaps his new partner really is a mean, hostile woman, but there is a equally good chance that she isnt. Look through her eyes for a moment. The abuser is re creating the same dynamic he set up with you, beginning with loving, attentive treatment in the early months of the of dating. He speaks to her with downcast eyes that well up with tears as he recounts how mean and unreasonable you were and how you called him abusive whenever he refused to boy to your control. If you have children with him, his girlfriends heart is bleeding because he cries in front of her about how much he misses them and says that you are keeping them away from him out of pure vindictiveness or out of a desire to turn them over to another man to be their dad. I currently have a case, for example, where the abusive father decided not to see his son for 6 mos, he even put his decision in writing, in a document that I read, and then complained publicly that he was being denied visits. Paul has probably misled Laura in some similar ways. His girlfriend sees a kind, loving parent whose desire to maintain a relationship with his children is being thwarted, how could she not hate you?
He may remain on good behavior with his new girlfriend even longer than he did with you because he is motivated by his campaign AGAINST YOU. Of course, his other side will slip out sooner or later, but by that time he can blame it all on how badly you have hurt him. His girlfriend thus gets sucked into breaking her back trying to prove that shes a good woman, UNLIKE YOU. She hopes that if she demonstrates her loyalty to him, hell become loving and available to her once again, as he was at the beginning. So she wants to show him she is really there for him by JOINING WITH OR EVEN OUTDOING his hostility and blaming of you.
By the time his selfish and abusive side finally gets so bad that his new girlfriend cant rationalize it away any more, shes in pretty deep. She may even have married him by that time. For her to accept that he is an abuser, she would have to face what a terrible wrong she did to you, and that would be quite a bitter pill to swallow. So what tends to happen instead is that the new partner BECOMES ANGRIER AND ANGRIER AT YOU FOR THE WAY SHE IS BEING TREATED BY HIM, BELIEVING THAT YOU "MADE HIM THIS WAY" BY HURTING HIM SO BADLY.
A couple of years ago I worked with a woman who said to me "I really hated his ex, but now I'm realizing he must have done the same stuff to her hes doing to me" Her guilt weighed heavily upon her. Women need a long time before they can accept having been used in this way.
In the story of Paul and Laura we never meet Paul's ex wife, but I have talked to 2 dozen or more women in her position among the partners of my clients. It is difficult to capture the pain I hear in the voices of women who's abusive ex partners are attempting to take their children away from them through the legal system, and the fact that they have a female ally helping them carry out that nefarious plan is almost too much to bear. The mothers ask me "Does she realize what she is doing? Has she bothered to think about what its like for a mother to be threatened with losing her children? What if he turns around years from now and does the same thing to her?"
At the same time, I believe it is important not to judge the new partner too harshly. I sometimes say to women, "You know manipulative he can be, and he is sure to be feeding her carefully crafted distortions. I'm not saying you should excuse her actions, I'm just reminding you that the one behind it all is HIM, not her. If you pour your energy into HATING HER, you are INADVERTENTLY SERVING HIS INTEREST." We do, however, need to create a social ethic that makes it clear that anyone who chooses to go to bat for a man accused o abuse has a responsibility to get ALL the facts and not just the view that he promotes. The abuse of women is simply to rampant for anyone to assume that an allegation is false or exaggerated without checking it out, very carefully.
From "Why Does He Do That?" By Lundy Bancroft

The hum from the street outside blends with the faint ticking of the clock on my desk, even though it’s barely 7am and the sun hasn’t really gotten past the buildings yet. My mind is already running through the day: payroll deadlines, the new hire who keeps missing the shift start by five minutes, the nagging worry that I forgot to submit the inventory report. It’s almost ridiculous how much being a shift supervisor defines my days now—there’s a kind of comfort in the routine, but also this underlying sense that I’m just treading water. I keep telling myself that being skeptical is a strength, but lately it feels more like I’m second-guessing every decision, both at work and in my personal life. Maybe it’s the financial pressure, but I notice I’m hyper-aware of every dollar I spend, like the two dollars I saved by skipping the bus and walking yesterday. That kind of vigilance is exhausting, though I know it’s necessary right now. I find myself wondering if this is what adulthood is: constant calculation, trying to predict the next curveball. There’s a part of me that wants to believe something bigger is on the horizon, but I don’t have any evidence for that, just hope mixed with a lot of restlessness. I keep meaning to journal more, to look for patterns or answers in my own words, but sometimes writing it down just makes the uncertainty feel more real. The bedroom is quiet enough for reflection, but this morning, the reflection feels more like circling around the same questions I never quite resolve. I guess I’ll get up, make some oatmeal, and start the day, even if I don’t have any clearer sense of what I’m actually working toward.

My advisor sent another round of comments on my thesis chapter, and every time I look at that email, I freeze up. It all piles up—grading, research, invoices that haven’t been paid yet, and my own coursework. I try to remind myself that I’ve managed harder days before, and that I can get through this too, but tonight the overwhelm feels heavy. My mind keeps flitting from one unfinished task to another, and I can’t seem to settle on what actually needs my attention first. The gentle approach I try to take with students feels hard to apply to myself. Maybe I just need to get home, make some tea, and let myself breathe for a bit before I tackle another round of edits. I’m worried about the rent this month, but for now, I just want to focus on getting through tonight.

I woke up to the sound of my phone buzzing, which is never a gentle way to start the day—especially when it’s 6:45 and the sun is just barely creeping over the rooftops. I remember fumbling to turn off the alarm, knocking over the half-empty glass of water I left on the counter last night. Water spreading slowly across the laminate, my brain not quite ready to process cause and effect. Now it’s an hour later, and I’m standing in the kitchen, toes curled against the chilly tile, watching the condensation on the window as I try to decide if I want tea or coffee. My laptop glows accusingly from the kitchen table, full of unread emails and half-finished session notes. I keep telling myself I’ll set firmer boundaries, draw a line between work and home, but everything seeps together when your office is five steps from your bed. The kettle is taking forever to boil, or maybe I’m just impatient. I should probably meditate, or journal more often, or do literally anything that links me back to myself instead of just drifting between clients and chores and scrolling mindlessly. I wonder if I’m even good at this therapist thing, or if I’m just someone who knows the right words to say. Why do I always feel like an imposter when I’m supposed to help other people feel grounded? I have this recurring urge to shut my laptop for a week and just walk somewhere far away, but of course I don’t. I answer emails, schedule sessions, nod sympathetically through grainy video calls. Sometimes I think about who I’d be if I wasn’t doing this job, if I wasn’t the reliable one. Maybe that’s selfish, or maybe it’s just honest. The tea is finally ready. I hold the mug in both hands, feeling the warmth, trying to focus on how it smells instead of the list of things I’ve already failed to do this morning. I keep telling myself tomorrow will be different, but right now I’m not sure I even know what different would look like.

Christmas Day 2025 (Wednesday) The house is comfortably warm. The sky is dark and grey. It is 42 degrees at almost 9am. It should warm up to 50 later. I slept fine last night. I went to bed after 10pm. I had no dreams that I can recall. I woke once at 4am to pee. I was up at 8am. D is still asleep. Christmas morning is here. We have been together for 17 Christmases now. For us it is just another day. We don't do gifts. We'll eventually have a late breakfast or an early lunch, watch tv or a movie and chill. We are both so boring! hahaha. I have my coffee and I am content. The dogs are sleeping in the bedroom with D still. We'll eventually get up and get going. Right now the house is quiet. I like it. Our stockings are hanging on the front door. I already posted this on FB, but here it is: Today I will not wish people a Merry Christmas or a Happy Holiday. I think wishing that creates an expectation and pressure to be merry or happy which then leads to feeling bad when you are not. Instead I will say this: I hope today you can give yourself the gift of compassion and kindness.

I feel like I’m stuck in a loop, hyperfocused on this tiny issue that has somehow ballooned in importance.

Now that I’m on the couch and the sun is setting, the living room feels weirdly empty, even though there are boxes everywhere. It’s hard to concentrate on anything else, but I keep glancing at my phone, tempted to order yet another cable or adapter. I know I should probably step back, maybe take a walk or unpack something useful, but instead, I’m analyzing every little hiccup in the connection. When I was leaving the house today, I caught a glimpse of the old family photo tucked behind the microwave. It’s been there for years, but for some reason it stopped me in my tracks this morning.
