Steam curls from the ceramic mug in front of me, and the hum of voices around the coffee shop almost drowns out my own thoughts. It’s just after eight, and I’m tucked away in this corner, watching the rain patter against the window. Today was busy at the shop—two brake jobs, an oil change, and the never-ending paperwork that seems to breed in cardboard folders. I caught myself double-checking everything, worried I’d miss a step. Maybe it’s just habit, or maybe I’m still feeling out of place in this new city. The faces are mostly unfamiliar, even after a month. I overheard a couple at the next table laughing about how lost they felt when they first moved here, and I almost wanted to join in, but old habits die hard. I’m practical, I tell myself, and I should be able to adapt, but it’s not as simple as swapping out a filter or tightening a bolt. There’s a comfort in the routine of work—tools lined up, hands busy, mind focused. When I’m here, away from the garage, it’s easier for doubts to creep in. I’ll finish my tea, make a list for tomorrow, and try not to be so hard on myself tonight.

Warning: You may find some of this material distasteful.
Disclaimer: I don’t care. My opinion, my diary, and what I have to say, I think, needs to be said.
Terrorism has been around for millennia. It has taken different forms at different times, and under different guises. But it always involves power over someone else.
I have mentioned previously the Crusades and the Inquisition, but not in the context of power, although I think that must be implied. Ethnic cleansing comes under the heading of Terrorism.
Ethnic Cleansing: Another way of saying “wholesale murder.” In more recent times, we have seen apartheid in South Africa. Tribal warfare in other parts of Africa has been going on for years now. The Chinese invaded Tibet. Why? Because they could, it seems. Witness the clash between ethnic groups in what we used to call Yugoslavia. Witness the conflict between Afghans and Iran. Witness the persecution of ethnic Turks in Northern Iraq. It goes on and on.
Now it seems to be Arab against Arab. Recall the bombings in Saudi Arabia? Recall the open warfare between Sunni and Shiite in Iraq, both Muslim, but with different notions of how to practice their religion. And, Saddam Hussein’s own Baathist party has had its share of troubles. Arab against Arab. Muslim against Muslim. All terrorists.
This terrorism didn’t start with the Arabs versus the Israelis. No, we’ve just taken notice of it because Israel is fighting back and being called ugly names because of it. The newspapers and TV news reporters are horrified when the Israelis bomb a known terrorist training camp. But when an Arab “martyr” blows up a busload of innocent people, well tch, isn’t that too bad.
Now let me quote from the Associated Press:
“GAZA CITY, Gaza Strip (AP) – Palestinian Prime Minister Ahmed Qureia condemned an Israeli airstrike that killed 14 Hamas militants in unusually harsh terms Tuesday, warning the attack will invite a tough response from the militant group and saying retaliation will be ‘justified’….
“The Israeli attack, which struck a Hamas training camp in Gaza City shortly after midnight, came a week after Hamas suicide bombers blew up two Israeli buses in the Israeli city of Beersheba, killing 16 people.”
Yasser Arafat has made promises to control the terrorists, but he’s the leader of Hamas, a group that has trumpeted credit for the bombings, as reprisals, of course, against Israeli defense maneuvers. He has been totally intransigent when it comes to any meaningful peace moves. A terrorist leader.
And now, moving on to the horror in Russia. Quoting from an article by David Brooks in the New York Times, September 7. 2004, entitled Cult of Death:
“We’ve been forced to witness the massacre of innocents. In New York, Madrid, Moscow, Tel Aviv, Baghdad and Bali, we have seen thousands of people destroyed while going about the daily activities of life.
“We’ve been forced to endure the massacre of children. Whether it’s teenagers outside an Israeli disco or students in Beslan, Russia, we’ve seen kids singled out as special targets.”
And a further quote from the same article:
“The Dutch foreign minister, Bernard Bot, speaking on behalf of the European Union, declared: ‘All countries in the world need to work together to prevent tragedies like this….’”
TRAGEDY MY FOOT!!! It was a cold, calculated, planned act of terrorism of the worst sort. Mass murder is what it was. In a school full of children!
When terrorism was confined to the Middle East, we tsked-tsked, and worried how it was ever going to end.
People, let me tell you – It isn’t going to end. Unless….
EVERY nation in the world must condemn in the harshest terms possible any act of terrorism. Terrorists are criminals of the worst sort. Remember how Saddam Hussein refused to testify in Court, saying he was the President of Iraq, and the Court had no authority over him? What happened next? Where is he now? What judgment has the Court made?
My point is that terrorists and tyrants need to be dealt with on their terms, not ours. They have no respect for law, so why apply the law to them?...if the law is applied at all (see the previous paragraph).
In Russia, the police should have tear-bombed the place from the git-go, or used anesthetic gas, or whatever means to disable the terrorists. Then go in and shoot them all on the spot. Oh, you say, the hostages might have been harmed or killed. Yes, they were. And the police didn’t get there in time to prevent the torture and killing. But the police might have prevented some of it if they had acted quickly and in force.
Negotiation won’t work. Don’t even try it. Go in, use the terrorists’ tactics against them, and if some innocent hostages get killed, well too bad. They were marked for murder anyway. Terrorists don’t negotiate. They kill.
So let’s deal with them on their terms.

I know just how you feel.
I have a love hate relationship with poetry. I have written poetry most of my life. And I truly am thankful for this method of writing. But it is hard to read poetry. Oh, maybe not Emily, or Robert Burns, or Stevenson, but there are good poems that are hard to read. Even for those who love them. I *think* I might know just a little of the reason why. And the following poem talks about it.
Poetry demands that we slow down a minute. And in our headlong age, this is sometimes a monumental task. We are trained to get to the bottom line. Poems meander. Sometimes the best line, is right in the middle! They demand a slower pace than we are used to and we chomp at the bit. But there is a magic in a poem that no other form of writing contains. One has to have discipline to find it.
So with apologies :
Those Annoying Poems
Poems are the whispers of the universe.
The quiet breath of awe that goes so oft unnoticed
In the blazing glare of the cacophonous world.
They make us impatient with their nuance
And we chafe at their shy recitations
Get to the point! our logical mind demands.
But how does one shout at a sunset,
Describe an unexpected epiphany,
Or demand logic from a freefall of emotion ?
These things are one step away from silence.
Where no word can be uttered at all.
This is our task, to give words to the ineffable.
Be patient, oh reader, even in this headlong age,
Even in chaos, stop and find beauty
Take just one moment, listen for the whispers.
The still small voice . . .
may be the voice of God.

I hope you didn’t infer from my comments about Indians that I in any way condone what happened to them after the Europeans came.
Nothing can be further from the truth.
What happened is an egregious example of ethnic cleansing without the murder. The murders took place as an “act of war.” Hit the enemy before he hits you.
Indian children were forcibly taken from their families and sent to far away white Christian schools to be educated in the white man’s way (read civilized?) They were forbidden to speak their native language, and were severely punished if caught using it even in private conversations.
They were Christianized. Their culture was deemed unfit for civilized people. They were savages to be tamed.
The tribes were moved from their ancestral lands and put on reservations—land that nobody else wanted because it was worthless land. All treaties that were signed in good faith by the Indians were systematically abrogated, unilaterally.
But guess what? Some of the land wasn’t so worthless after all. The Cherokees in Oklahoma are sitting on one of the largest oil deposits, and consequently have become a very rich nation. They have schools. They have doctors and lawyers. And teachers who teach about their culture, as well as the academics of the White World. They have medical care. And the government can’t take it away from them, because the government gave it to them and they have enough money and power now to protect what has become rightfully theirs.
When the Indians tried to fight back, our brave Cavalrymen raided their camps and killed women and children, along with the braves. And killed women and children even when the braves weren’t in camp.
Now let’s go back several centuries. Remember the Crusades? These great knights were going to liberate the Holy City Jerusalem from the paynim, the Saracen, the heathens. OK, go read your history.
A century or two after that came the Inquisition in Spain and Portugal. Jews were forced to accept Christianity or die. Or leave the country. If they could. Go read your history.
Check out the Spanish Conquistadores and what they did to flourishing empires in South America, Central America, then the indigenous peoples in the lands that are now the USA. Go read your history.
Is it any wonder, then, what happened to the Native Americans when the great civilized White Man came to this country?
Don’t bother about reading the history books. You won’t find any criticism of the treatment of the Indians in any of the history books the school children read.
But I still say…Custer got what was coming to him.
Shalom

North Of Italy, 10:45 PM
I walk into the
neuropsychiatrist
’s office.
She called me in ten minutes early — I was right to leave at 10:30 AM and arrive in the waiting room just a few minutes later.
While I’m telling her that I won’t be seeing my psychologist for about six months and that changing doctors always unsettles me a little, she looks at me as if she feels guilty:
she too will be leaving for another city in a month
, for family reasons.
😵‍💫
“This is not possible! What on earth is going on?”
- I think to myself, but I reply with exaggerated and fake self-control.
It’s awful how the public healthcare system shows no real respect or consideration for emotionally fragile patients who actually need stability.
😡
I’ll be reassigned to one of the four psychiatrists on staff — all competent women — which reassures me a little.
The next time we’ll see each other will be Monday, March 30th, her second-to-last working day in my city.
After that, I’ll once again have to go back to my general practitioner to request yet another referral for an initial neuropsychiatric appointment.
To avoid thinking about it too much, since Friday is market day, I asked my father to drop me off near the main square, full of dogs and people.
Since life keeps throwing low blows at me, I’d like to defend myself by coloring it.
🌈
I rushed into
Douglas
and bought three nail polishes 💅🏻 in different shades:
purple
, which makes me think of this Lenten season — introspection, recollection, and penance;
lilac
,
like the walls of my bedroom, the
Lady of Avalon
, great enchantress and healer, and
Morgan le Fay
, great sorceress, witch and prophetess; and a delicate
pink
that transports me straight to
Barbieland.
As the cherry on top 🍒, I bought a nude lip gloss 💋 that brightens the lips.
I don’t love wearing makeup, but
it really takes very little to feel better.
I plan to play with the nail polishes in many ways: depending on my mood, my outfit, holidays, external circumstances, the weather, the seasons, the Sabbats, the planets, the lunar phases, the Liturgical seasons, the days of the week — even the hours of the day!
I can’t wait to experiment.
I immediately chose
purple
, since we’re approaching the
Second Sunday of Lent.
During the week, I might wear
lilac
— it’s softer and less bold.
It’s been so long since my nails were left natural.
I’m truly
grateful
that this creative impulse came to me. 🖌️
No permanent or semi-permanent manicure, though — I like to change, even within the same day.
I still don’t know which color I prefer to wear… maybe
fuchsia
💕, which, along with
red
, has always been my favorite color.

Found this on the net - made me think about our perceptions of others.
Cherie Carter-Scott's rules of life:
Others are only mirrors of you.
"
You love or hate something about another person according to what love or hate about yourself.
Be tolerant; accept others as they are, and strive for clarity of self-awareness; strive to truly understand and have an objective perception of your own self, your thoughts and feelings. Negative experiences are opportunities to heal the wounds that you carry. Support others, and by doing so you support yourself. Where you are unable to support others it is a sign that you are not adequately attending to your own needs..."
Indeed we have personal criteria for what's bad, what's good. How often those who can't find anything positive in themselves, can't find it in others too. Why miserable people attract miserable people? Why happy people seek the company of happy people?
We are too impatient to take time to learn about each other, we are so quick to judge instead, based on our personal book of laws: "what's good for me, should be good enough for you"...
I am guilty of this too. And never actually realised that my judgment based on my self-verdict.
If I would hate myself a lot, what is the chance that I could love the others?

Doesn’t the wedding procession always look lovely? And the bride – the fairy princess;And the guests…oh, how nice – gents in black ties, ladies – in elegant hats…Well, now – has anybody ever thought how painful the hat experience could be for women?!
I don’t know if there are those ladies, who managed to find that special “hat-you’ve-been-born-in”. For me hat hunting for the next weekend’s friend’s wedding has been a trip down to Frustration Lane.
I have always enjoyed looking at the other women in hats. There is something very stylish about them. Very posh and very smart. But I have never worn a hat in my life and never really noticed that I missed out on this terribly.
Well, this time all I needed – just to buy me a little decent hat for our friend’s wedding for next weekend...And how difficult do you think this might be?
After a plundering raid on the shops and hours of trying on all conceivable models of lady’s hats – a few philosophical notices:
1.Trying on hats could be fun…for all those who happened to be around. It is nothing but sheer embarrassment for the “model head”.
2.On some the hat could be a stylish fashion accessory. A beautiful supplement to natural elegance. A character feature to accentuate style. On others hat is just a monstrous excrescence of sinamay on top of a poor wretch’s head.
I’ve seen so many unrecognisable appearances of me while trying on stacks of hats that almost lost myself among those surreal images…
I’ve tried on Mushroom hats, Mad Hatter hats, Scarecrow hats, Frivolously Plumaged hats, hats with Extremely Wide Brims that seemed to grow straight from the scalp, Gambler hats and Rodeo Queen hats, finally, Lampshade hats…Oh, and Panama hats as well…And none of those hats was anywhere closer to the look that I’d fancy or at least could’ve put up with…[*sigh]
I wish there would be a good explanation why on earth should women wear hat to the wedding?! Especially, if it is only for some 45 minutes of the ceremony itself, and then – off you go – you can safely lose your head…or hat for that matter…
Oh, and also – add to this hat-wearing ordeal the embarrassment of misshaped hair-do after removal of a hat for the evening reception! Do you really believe that you can be careless and comfortably relaxed wearing a stunning hat, when for all that time deep inside you are aware of that dreadful moment you will need to take your hat off and reveal sleeky locks of what cost you a fortune at hairdresser's the day before…
Anyway, after long run around all shops in town, I’ve managed to find a more-or-less suitable head gear, that I can live with for 45 mins. And if it will be out of style, I certainly can't care less - I’ll probably never see these people again anyway.
Sometimes I think that weddings could be a way for bride and groom to put their friends in embarrassing situations and mock at them during the wedding. Can easily imagine them laughing up their's sleeve...

When I lost J1 last year, yes: I was a federal employee. I was on a my very first actual work trip (EVER!!!) when we first got the Fork In The Road email. Honestly, most people were instructed to ignore it, it's clearly a phishing attempt. It certainly seemed scammy. I lost my job on what us feds (current or former) called the Valentine's Day Massacre. We were ALL fired under the guise of "poor performance".... except obviously that's not true. My boss (and their boss) were IN TEARS bringing me into the office. My boss kept saying "this isn't true. We didn't write this. Don't sign this. This isn't how we are supposed to operate." While their boss kept apologizing, saying there was nothing they could do. I worked in a particularly dream world of a place, as I mentioned before: it was really the least toxic environment I'd ever worked in. In fact, apparently DOGE had ordered our firing days earlier, but the higher ups and heads of the bureau all worked tirelessly to save us. They really did. They added up the total cost of keeping the number of employees they were told to terminate (including benefits and everything) and they spent the whole week working to find a way to cut costs here and there. By the week's end, they were very proud; they found a way to save EVERY SINGLE PERSON ON THE LIST. Every. Single. One. It wasn't ideal, because we lost some important funding as sacrifices, but they knew we were already short-staffed and they fought for us. Valentine's Day 2025, they proudly walked into a meeting with DOGE. ....why are they even dealing with DOGE? THEY SHOULD NOT ANSWER TO A NON-GOVERNMENT ENTITY (unless it is the general people because: duh! That's WHO WE SERVE). Anyway, they were so proud they did it. It would not be an easy path ahead, but they did it! They walked out AUDIBLY saying, "....apparently it was never about money, it was just numbers." They told DOGE their ideas, how to cut costs/save money, and DOGE said? "No. Fire them." Just like that. It's so stupid that almost a year later typing this out still brings me to tears, but damn if that doesn't sting. I'll never forget that they FOUGHT FOR US though. Never. My coworkers were sobbing as I consoled them and packed up my stuff. The job that took me 16 long years to finally get, and I lose it for the sake of a façade to present savings to the American people. I can't actually delve into details on my position because I still want to maintain complete anonymity, but enough departments, bureaus, and various types of staffing positions were eliminated that if I leave it there it's still okay. Suffice to say my positions was actually important, though. Most of them were, really. I'm sure there are some people in some places that might have been best replaced, but the key there is replacing because the POSITION is still important. Anyway, I consoled my colleagues as they helped me to my car with my stuff. Namely the mail cart we had to bring to hold all my plants. 😖 🌿🌿🌿🌿🌿 As soon as work hours were over, I got a text from my boss with a link to a lawsuit. Zero people wanted this to happen. Maybe elsewhere, but not in our office. We were valued. Really seems like a fairy tale job, eh? A job where you are respected and treated as a human and not a machine!? UNHEARD OF! Honestly, that was the first time I had experienced that. I was just shy of 40 years of age before I finally got this job… what was supposed to be my final job because I was not going to leave a place that let me leave at the end of the day without any stress or a sense of dread at the thought of returning. I was so happy to finally have my place. The next handful of weeks I spent struggling. I applied to jobs left and right, editing my resumes and cover letters for each, but only applying to things I realistically thought I could get. I also applied for food stamps, state medical coverage, and unemployment. Just over a month later my (former) boss called me to say they (boss + 2 higher ups) wrote us (fired employees) letters of recommendation to use, and please let them know if there is anything they can do or use them as a reference and they are sorry they can't get us back but they tried… I offered to come INTO office to pick them up since I was taking my daughter downtown for Honor Band practice anyway. It was an hour later. I showed up and THEY WELCOMED ME BACK. In that hour we were gone, a court determined it was illegal and my boss JUMPED at the chance to get us back in office ASAP. They said "a butt in the chair is harder to justify firing than one sitting at home". I got to go back to work the next week. I then had to pay back the unemployment I got (all like, 3 weeks of it), but I was happy to do such because I HAD MY JOB BACK! After 2 weeks it felt normal again. Well, normal minus having to report to DOGE every week with 3 things we did that week that were productive. I mean, I get wanting to verify productivity in the workforce, but nobody, and I mean NOBODY trusted them. Some people sent them with read receipts and would get notification they were deleted unopened. Some people responded with snark, like sharing mental health resources with colleagues due to the hostile work environment it has become. Those people got written up or fired. Thing is, they had algorithms. It didn't matter what you said, so long as you said something and it wasn't aggressive. This is my first real usage of AI: my boss showed me how to put in my job description, write briefly what I did this week, and then have AI write up a bulleted list of what I could report I did that week that would appease the assholes in power. My boss heavily encouraged the use of AI. Big proponent. I didn't really like it at first, though I've come around to appreciate it more. Still, it greatly simplified that menial task which actually was pretty daunting to someone that was just fired for supposedly "poor performance" while their supervisor kept telling them "you've been an exemplary employee; we didn't write this. We had no say in this." I appreciated learning how to speak to AI to get the results needed: it came in handy later. Not much later, actually, because after 2 weeks I was feeling settled in again… when word of the looming Reduction In Force (RIF) hit. Let's be real: this is a normal thing when new administrations come in, but historically we were not touched. We are different. We are more important, our role is vastly more critical than some, and while RIFs are common, they aren't to our bureau. I low-key thought, "yeah, I'll decide later whether or not I follow up on that…" But here's the thing: she also offered me HRT therapy for my perimenopause symptoms… which means I could maybe start sleeping better at night. Score! But, wait: you can't take hormones if you have a tumor. So she told me she wouldn't prescribe the HRT until we got the results of the MRI. So this was the dilemma: how bad did I want the HRT? Bad enough to schedule the MRI, it turns out. I knew it was going to be rough, and it was. I mentally prepared myself as much as possible for being stuck in a tube, not able to move, with very loud noises going on all around me… but I don't know how much it helped. They gave me headphones and put on some "easy listening" soft rock, but I could barely hear it because the machine was so loud. I can't breathe! Yes, you can. That's just your tongue sliding back into your throat. Push it forward. I can't breathe! Yes, you can. This is just your brain trying to panic. Ground yourself and take deep breaths. I need out now! No, you don't. You're fine. And if you move you're going to have to start over. I was eventually able to cope by counting and gently tapping with one finger. It worked against me once, though, when I tapped a little too hard and got a blurry image and had to repeat a scan. I kept track of time by counting songs. Last night, while walking around the block after everyone was asleep, I caught myself replaying the conversation with my sister from earlier that day. It wasn’t anything surprising but there was this moment when she asked about Dad’s last wishes and I realized I had no clear answer. It felt like a weight pressing down harder than I wanted to admit. Between the noise of the street and the quiet in my head, I found it hard to line up my thoughts, like they were all scattered puzzle pieces I couldn’t quite fit together.

I’m usually the one helping others sort through their messier feelings, but trying to do that for myself in something so close to home feels almost impossible. I want to be optimistic about what Dad would want, focusing on gratitude or acceptance, but the grief sits stubbornly on my chest. Maybe that’s why I kept turning the same thought over and over as I walked, hoping to land on some clarity, some peace. Instead, it was more like a slow unraveling with moments of cold air and the faint sound of a car door slamming. I’ll try again tomorrow, maybe with a little more patience and less expectation.

I keep adding things to my planner and then ignoring them. Sometimes I wonder if other people are just better at handling all this, or if they’re faking it too. I keep telling myself I’ll take a walk or do something for myself, but the day slips away and I just sit here, scrolling through my phone, waiting for energy to come back.

I’ve been going through some self reflection, which interestingly is kind of the reason I started writing here a couple years ago, but then I settled into a habit of writing about stuff going on in my personal life instead of writing deeper things. When I started my prosebox account I actually wanted to write about dealing with the changes in my life having recently left the church, but that also seems like ancient history to me now.

It started because a couple weeks ago I was talking to Darby and we had the idea to plan some kind of girls trip in January. We didn’t have a real idea of what we wanted to do or where we wanted to go, we just thought we’d take a road trip the three of us. Abby, Darby, and me. We talked about heading somewhere up the coast like Savannah or Charleston but that’s close to where I grew up and I wanted to go someplace different. So then we talked about the panhandle which felt like a bad choice in January, so we finally settled on Atlanta.

When I talked to Abby about it, her immediate response was to ask if she could invite Vickie, her girlfriend. I hesitated a little because I didn’t want to seem like I was excluding anyone, but I had the thought from the beginning that it would only be the three of us. I wasn’t planning on including Clay, so I didn’t think Vickie should be part of it either. So that’s what I told her.

I was surprised when she responded with anger. I thought my reasoning for not wanting to invite Vickie was fine (and I still do). But then she told me that it feels like I want nothing to do with Vickie and called me homophobic.

My first impulse was to defend myself. I do feel like it’s true that I’ve made little effort to connect with Vickie, but it has nothing to do with her sexuality. Abby is my best friend and if she identifies as queer and I love her unconditionally, how could I possibly be homophobic?

Then Abby says that the difference is that she looks and acts like a straight girl, and that allows me to stay in my comfort zone while still being her friend. Vickie has a shaved head and tattoos and a nose ring and is the type of person who you immediately recognize as gay when you look at her. I’m not saying that having a nose ring makes you a lesbian. I don’t know if I’m being clear. But there’s a certain look that she has that is probably intentional so that it announces her sexuality without her having to say anything.

As soon as Abby said that to me I felt this guilty feeling my chest and I realized that everything she was saying was true. I grew up religious and being told that it’s wrong to be gay, and I feel like I’m super open-minded now compared to how I was just a few years ago. But I really do have a hard time accepting someone like Vickie. And I feel terrible saying that, but it’s the honest truth.

I didn’t argue with Abby. I told her I think she’s right and that I need to work on myself. And writing about it here is hopefully going to help. I’m officially acknowledging that I’m a little homophobic still and I want to be better. I want to work through this and be more accepting of people that are different from me.

And I don’t even know where to start. How do you train yourself to not feel a certain way?

I read an article on Sunday about how many of our technological marvels are becoming so complex that people are beginning to balk at buying and or using them. It was like music to my ears, since I have been feeling like a curmudgeon, cum Luddite, and quite a bit out of touch with the latest gadgets. I have had this feeling for a few years now, that the technology was going to make some quantum leap and I would eyeball the chasm and opt out of the whole game. Right now I resist the cell phone and the palm pilot, ( even though if those geek types that create them would make a palm pilot bigger and a lot more attractive, more like a book , I might be tempted ). I do like learning how to use my own computer, and still get a kick out of creating documents with great graphics and sending emails with cool stationary and music attached. But honestly, I can see the font on the monitor, telling of the day when I officially join the curmudged Luddites in earnest. It wasn’t always this way. My boys grew up in the 70’s and 80’s, and I joined them in the wonder of the rise of the computer revolution. I remember slaving over middle son's Commondor 64, (the first computer in our household ) entering 150 lines of code to get a program that produced tones so I could tune my guitar. And we used to play this goofy Indiana Jones game for hours on end, and then when you actually got through all the levels, the ending payoff sequence would never work! Which precipitated our first call to tech support….. we never got through to a real person as I recall. We upgraded, struggled with learning how to install new software, which used to be quite an undertaking before the wizards and then, OH MY GOSH, youngest son started opening up the CPU and sticking things in slots……! While I looked on feeling like I was witnessing open heart surgery, and the only thing I could think of was, “Put the thing in and put that other thing back on or something really awful is going to happen !” The whole experience early on was much like solving complex puzzles, something humans have been enjoying for millennia. ( Who can describe their glee when you finally figured out how to use “copy” and “paste” in a document ?) But lately I am more than a bit disillusioned with the whole thing. It seems like in the last several years, the only thing about computers that is new, is that they are faster, and can store more stuff. But they still crash, lose your files, are hard to use, and there are many programs that “do not play well with others.” And now I come to the really weird and very hard to admit element in all of this….. pause for deep breath…. I think part of my disappointment with computers is that I sort of expect the computer to “interact” with me. Oy, there I have written it. With all the time I spend in front of the screen, doing all manner of reading and writing and searching and surfing and coaxing it to operate properly, my computer does not, well. . . . . know me. This may seem ridiculous to you, but in some obscure corner of my psyche with all this investment of time with this technological marvel, you think it might just take a moment to say “hi!”…. Of course I am not completely alone in my delusion. One time when oldest son had gotten a new computer…. ( I think it was a 486) he called me to tell me all the great things it could do, and concluded breathlessly…”Mom, it does everything but have sex with you!” ( Sorry dear, but I needed a real life example ) The idea that computers were going to make our lives easier has turned out to be a lie. They have made our lives more complex. They are frustrating to use. They suck up wallets full of money. They don’t have the answer to “Life, the Universe, and Everything” and frankly I suspect my computer doesn’t even like me. So if you don’t see me up on the latest software and running the latest pentium chip 5 years from now, you will know why. I am ready to start treating my computer like the monkey wrench that it is. And stop expecting it to ever say “good morning” unless forced to do so, by some obscure config.sys file in the bowels of the hard drive. See….. there I go again, computers don’t have bowels. Obviously I have a long way to go in my paradigm shift from geek to Luddite. At this point, I am going to make my callous and unfeeling computer print out this document on paper where it will be safe from digital mayhem. Then I am going outside and play…. among the real people. And who knows, maybe one of them will actually say , “Hi ! “

Imagine – driving along the motorway, no rush, just enjoying as much as driving can be enjoyed. Saw a sign on the roadside, telling that there is a museum somewhere on the left…”Excellent”, - I said to myself, and turned to my left, like any normal tourist would do [in the end of a day its been decided to dedicate those 3 days to full time sightseeing anyway] …
Well, first of all – a comment about how stupid those who put up such signs are:
What would you expect to know about places of interests, when driving by on motorway? I would expect – direction and distance, right? Maybe I expect too much. But if I’d knew that the museum that I was so interested in was not only on my left, but also – in about half-distance of my initial route from home to the wedding venue, only in completely different direction! The most annoying thing – that you’d find this out only by actually driving there! [Why, oh why they never mention distance on the road signs for the places of interest?! Saving on paint, perhaps?]
Anyway, all is well, what ends well. And we finally arrived to the destination. Good thing that it was well worth it! The place called Beaulieu. It is the estate that has been in Lord Montagu's family ownership since 15 century. There are lots of things to see in there. A little Abbey used to be a Cistercian monastery since 12 century - a place of tranquillity, planted with fragrant herbs. The house itself with a nice collection of art. And of course – a Motor Museum - with the Collection of some 250 vehicles - from some of the earliest examples of motoring to legendary World Record Breakers like Bluebird and Golden Arrow. Absolutely fascinating stuff!
Actually, I can’t even say which part I liked the most. I suppose, old Abbey – such a peaceful place – you can hear own thoughts!.. Most of it in ruins now, only little yard left and a church, and with not that many visitors this time of a year; somehow it felt pacifying…
OK, that was my Friday – a great beginning to the great weekend.
Next morning after Saturday’s wedding we woke up with the thirst for more adventures. And adventurous spirit brought us to the
Isle Of Wight.
Even the bad rainy weather [*read: normal British weather] didn’t prevent full enjoyment of the most beautiful landscape I’ve ever seen! It is a diamond shape island, thirteen miles north to south and twenty three miles east to west. And we’ve been driving around all of it! Was absolutely happy about my day…It’s a shame that it had to end at some point – 2.5 hours drive home through the stormy night has been somewhat a peculiar conclusion to the memorable 3 day’s adventure…
Anyway, wherever I’ve been, whatever I’ve seen, I will remember for the sensation of the inevitable dawning of the Autumn in all Her glory and all Her solemn bleakness…
Having returned home after 3 days trip to New Forest, I am now back into the office as well – to my deep regret 2 weeks holidays elapsed just at a time when I’d need a lil bit more rest…But life is going on and so are my duties…[~sigh]. Needless to say that first few days will be dedicated for dealing with all the backlogs. Such a sad ending for so immense beginning!

"...It happened with one woman. She was invited to review her life as a series of footprints along a beach. "See," said the angel, wherever you walked, I walked beside you." "But look," she cried, "There, in a really bad phase of my past, I can see only one set of prints in the sand. Why did you abandon me then?" "Abandon you?" retorted the angel. "Why, that's when I was carrying you..."
What a nice story it is! And do I believe it? Nah, don’t think I do. The idea of someone walking along our life path, helping us, when in need, carrying us? Oh, please…
People supposed to deal with their problems themselves, not expecting someone to hold hands and show the light. Isn’t it ironic, that we often wish to have that Someone in life, but fail to be that Someone for somebody else? Are we able to pass the light? Or are we too selfish to give without looking forward for repayment?
It is natural to wish good things for yourself (hmmmm...I wonder if there would be anyone in the World, who would wish bad things for themselves instead?) They say: your wish will be granted if it’ll be someone else – to make that wish for you, someone with good intentions, someone who cares. I don’t know about anyone else, but I’ve certainly seen that working in real life…A sincere good wish for someone is a special gift one can share. And sometimes it happened, that when we wish someone to be happy, we realise that that happiness can only be balanced with somebody else’s sorrows…
Ah, isn’t life – all about – BALANCING?

Like, am I missing something or is this just what life is for someone like me? Had a weird moment where I stared into a window, saw my reflection, and it looked like a stranger for a second. My mind was racing about work stuff, emails I forgot, did I shut down my computer right, and then suddenly I’m thinking about where I’ll be in five years. It’s all jumbled together, hard to untangle. I like the quiet and the predictability, but then I get restless, anxious that I’m not doing enough, or being enough. I caught myself counting steps, not because I care about fitness but just to have something to focus on. The smell of someone’s laundry vent hit me, reminded me I need to do mine, and then I was thinking about how much I hate folding shirts. I guess I feel like I should want more, or at least know what I want, but I don’t. Patient with myself, trying not to judge, but also kind of frustrated. Sometimes I wish something would happen, just to shake things up, but I also know I’d probably panic if it did. Wrapped up the walk by checking my phone for no reason, nothing new. I’ll probably snack and watch that documentary before bed, and tomorrow’ll look a lot like today.

The glow from my laptop screen is the only thing keeping this room from going completely dark. I should be asleep, but my mind is full of tabs—some actual, some metaphorical. Today started at 7:23 AM with my phone alarm blaring far too close to my ear and a calendar reminder for three client calls, two invoices, and a note to send flowers to Mom. The mundane details are somehow comforting, even if they are relentless. The real distraction is the message I got from Mark this morning, which I’ve reread at least six times. It was funny, offbeat, and a little distant. Maybe he’s just busy, or maybe that’s optimism talking.

I keep asking myself if I’m reading too much into things, which, knowing me, is likely. The last time I tried to predict where a relationship was going, I ended up eating leftover lasagna alone for a week, so I’m not exactly trusting my instincts. Still, there’s hope buried under the sarcasm. Juggling deadlines used to be the main source of my stress, but now it’s mixed with this uncertainty about whether I want this relationship to go somewhere or if I’m just afraid of being alone. I can’t decide if I’m overthinking or just being practical. Maybe both. For now, I’ll just close some tabs—on the screen, at least.

I was trying to decide what to make for lunch this afternoon as I stood in the kitchen this morning, and I realized I barely know anyone well enough to invite them over. The plan was to use cooking as a way to connect with some classmates, but the idea of reaching out feels weirdly intimidating. It’s not that people here aren’t friendly, but everyone seems to have their own circles already, and I always feel like I’m intruding. I spent a while going through my phone, debating whether to text Maya from my seminar group, but then convinced myself she was probably busy.

It’s strange because I’ve always thought of myself as pretty organized, but when it comes to social stuff, I get scatterbrained and overthink everything. Maybe I just need to force myself to make the first move, even if it feels awkward. I keep making lists of who I could reach out to, what to say, but never actually follow through. The fact that I’m so focused on my research right now probably doesn’t help, since it gives me an excuse to avoid the discomfort. Still, I know building connections here is important if I’m going to feel settled. Maybe after class today I’ll try again and actually send that message instead of just thinking about it.

I dropped the spoon into the sink this morning and it made a sound much louder than it should have. The clock said 6:18, but it felt like I was still somewhere around midnight, eyes gritty, everything a little out of focus. The kitchen was half-lit and chilly and the cat’s tail kept brushing against my ankle, which was somehow both comforting and annoying. I stared at the mess of dishes from last night and thought, again, about how I ended up talking in circles with Greg. Or was it arguing? Hard to tell at that hour. 

He wanted to talk about “where things are going.” I wanted to talk about the dishwasher. There’s probably a lesson in there, but I’m too tired to figure out what it is. I remember laughing, the dry kind, not because anything was funny but because it was easier than saying I don’t know what I want. I think he noticed. I wish I could see this whole thing more clearly, but lately my brain feels like it’s wading through soup. Maybe that’s just how new relationships go at my age, or maybe I’m overcomplicating everything (again). The cereal was stale, the coffee was strong, and I still have no idea what I’m doing.

This morning I woke up to the sound of my roommate’s alarm through the wall (again), and I realized I still hadn’t done my share of the dishes. I felt a little guilty, but also kind of annoyed at myself for not getting to them last night. When I finally made it out to the kitchen, she was already there making toast, so I just muttered a quick “sorry about the plates” and grabbed my mug. She just shrugged and said it was fine, but there was this pause, and I couldn’t tell if she was actually okay with it or just being polite. I keep replaying that moment, and now I’m wondering if I should bring it up again or just let it go. Honestly, I overthink these little things, and I wish I could just let them slide the way she seems to. Maybe she’s just better at not sweating the small stuff, or maybe I’m projecting and she’s secretly frustrated. The funny thing is, we get along well most of the time, but I always worry about these small frictions turning into bigger issues. My mind kept drifting back to that weird pause while I was logging into work, which did not help my already sluggish brain. Customer support calls don’t exactly cure tiredness, but they do keep me busy enough to forget for a while. I want to talk with her later, but I also don’t want to make a big deal out of nothing. I’m probably being ridiculous, but I can’t help it. Maybe I’ll just do the dishes tonight and hope that’s enough. Or maybe I’ll actually try to have a normal conversation and see if she wants to order takeout later. Ugh, why is adulting so full of these tiny puzzles?

My head keeps bumping against the window as the bus jerks down Main Street. The lights outside blur together, and I feel more like a passenger in my life than just on this bus. I spent all day staring at a blank document, trying to force words that weren’t ready to show up. It’s like I’m chasing something that keeps slipping ahead, and I’m too tired to keep running but too restless to stop. 

Work deadlines are stacking up, and every email feels heavier than it should. I keep thinking that if I just finish one more chapter, maybe I’ll feel better, but each one just leads to the next. On top of that, I’m not sure what’s going on with me and Sarah. We had a decent dinner last night, but half the time I was analyzing every thing I said or didn’t say. I hate how much I overthink this stuff, but I can’t turn it off. Is it supposed to be this confusing? I want things to work, but I don’t know if we’re moving forward or just treading water. 

The bus is almost at my stop. I keep telling myself I’ll get a better handle on all of this tomorrow, but tonight I’m just glad to be heading home. Maybe I’ll just order takeout and watch something dumb. I wish I could quiet my mind for five minutes, but I know I’ll probably just lie in bed replaying conversations and deadlines in my head until I finally crash.

The kitchen is quiet except for the faint hum of the fridge and the occasional clink of a spoon against the mug. I thought this morning would feel different, maybe calmer, but instead there’s this tightness in my chest that won’t go away. I tried explaining to my mom last night why I’m so exhausted, both from the startup and from being her main support now, but she just looked at me like I was complaining. Maybe she doesn’t understand how heavy everything feels.

I wonder if I’m too harsh on myself for not doing enough, or if I’m not clear enough about my limits. Sometimes I think I’m supposed to have all the answers already, but I don’t. I want to be honest without making her feel like a burden. Maybe I should try again, find new words. Maybe it’s just the anxiety talking. I’ll make more coffee and sit here a bit longer before the day begins.

Sunday morning. 4:30 AM
Why the heck to we have sinuses ?
A drippy, sloppy, cloggy, boggy, cough inducing, streaming eye creating, kleenex using, sleep depriving, routine disrupting bit of anatomy if I ever knew one!
If you ever find out the purpose of the common cold, please keep it to yourself. I don’t think we could handle the added burden of finding out it’s “good for us” in any way.
The part about being ill that annoys me most is how it narrows one’s world down to the size of a bathrobe and a kleenex box. This is barely a world worth living in. Especially when you get to the stage where the kleenex begins to feel like sandpaper. . . (okay, it’s a hackneyed analogy but I truly cannot think of another right now, I think it’s the mouth breathing that’s doing it to me)
Anyway, when you get to the sandpaper stage any sentient being must begin to get philosophical. Or run the risk of drifting into the black hole of despair where the meaning of Life the Universe and Everything has definitely fled to The Restaurant at the End of the Universe and may not even be on the menu any more.
Of course, if you are not quite so close to the precipice, you could take a nice hot bath. My remedy for whatever ails the human body or soul. What would make this hot bath particularly comforting for me would be that nice rubber ducky floating in the steamy water. Unfortunately I have yet to find said ducky and will have to manage without him. Maybe if I floated my kleenex box ?
No?
You may be right, my brain is muddled by fluids being secreted by those pesky . . . .sinuses.
Why the heck DO we have sinuses ?
A drippy, sloppy, cloggy, boggy…..
(Muffled noise….followed by kleenex box hitting the floor.)
“Somebody get the thermometer, I think she has a fever.”

The kitchen floor is a little cold under my feet this morning, and I can hear the dishwasher humming from last night’s load I forgot to unload. There’s a faint smell of toast from someone’s midnight snack, and crumbs everywhere, but I just don’t have the energy yet to sweep. My head still feels heavy, as if I didn’t really wake up all the way, even though the clock says it’s already past 7. I poured myself some coffee but left it sitting on the counter, distracted by searching for a clean mug for my husband, only to realize he’d already left early. Sometimes I get frustrated at myself for being so scattered, forgetting simple things like coffee or where I put my wrench yesterday. I know I’m too hard on myself, but it’s hard not to be when the day starts off with little forgetful moments. The kids are still asleep, which gives me a few minutes of quiet, but knowing they’ll wake up soon keeps my mind half-focused on what has to be done—lunches, uniforms, reminding everyone to grab their things. I wish I had a better system, or maybe just more patience with myself. Being the one who fixes things at work doesn’t always translate to fixing things at home, especially with the constant noise and lack of privacy. I catch myself wishing I could just have a few hours where nobody needs me, not even the machines. The fog in my head isn’t clearing up like I hoped, and I keep thinking I must be missing something important, but I can’t put my finger on it. Maybe it’s just tiredness, or maybe I’m outgrowing the pace I used to keep without even thinking. I look at the grease stains on my hands, even after scrubbing, and it’s a small comfort—the proof that I do get things done, even if it never feels like enough. The sun is just starting to come through the window, catching on the dust I should wipe off the table, but for now, I’ll just sit for a minute and try to let myself be gentle about it all.

Just finished washing the dishes after dinner, which somehow feels like a task that drags on forever when you’re feeling restless. It’s like every day is a slightly different variation on the same theme, and it’s starting to feel less like a steady rhythm and more like a stubborn glitch in the system. I thought living alone would give me some mental clarity, but all it does is make the silence louder. No distractions, sure, but also no one to bounce these thoughts off of. Some days I think I’m just waiting for a sign to shake things up, but I’m not even sure what that sign would look like. Maybe I’m overthinking it, which is definitely something I’m prone to doing. I can’t even watch a show or read something without my mind wandering to all the things I haven’t done or the ideas I haven’t explored yet. The funny thing is, I’m curious about a lot of stuff, but turning that curiosity into actual progress feels like a full-time job in itself. OK…Time of catching up. Amazing – I’ve been away for only 3 days but there are so many things happened in DDLand, that it seems like I’m returning from at least a one year trip around the World.
Well, this weekend I’ve had a chance to try on my new hat, which to my relief didn’t turn up to be a real “try-on”, for as soon as the church service finished and all of our crowd cheerfully galloped outside for the “great outdoor fun” – picture taking, the weather suddenly decided to take care of our head gear for us. The wind was so strong that we had our bride almost kidnapped by him. (That day I’ve learnt that one should be very careful choosing their all-weather wedding dress, tho not that I’ll ever need to use this knowledge).
So, the Wind was so persistent to take of our hats, that eventually my brand new hat ended up in a bag instead of my head. Oh, well, it wasn’t for nothing, that I never wanted hat in the first place [~mental note to myself: next time be careful with my wishes].
Apart from stormy rain in the morning right up until the very time of the ceremony, and apart from ghastly wind for the “picture frame”, otherwise it was a splendid Perfect British Wedding. (I wonder if this has got something to do with the groom being actually the German… Ahem)
The whole day event has been running like a German train – minute-to-minute to the schedule. And the guests haven’t had a time to waste with all the meals, drinks, speeches and even dancing late at night. I’ve heard the rumours that the couple spent about a year in preparation! (well, even if this isn’t true, it certainly looks like the one – the amount of things being thought over is quite impressive! [~second note to myself: never volunteer to organize my son’s wedding – buy them tickets somewhere far far away instead].
So, that’s the wedding and the whole Saturday nicely spent.
Since it was my last 3 days of vacation, and the wedding being somewhere away from where we live, we’ve decided to go to the area in advance,take a look around, do some sightseeing. And so – off we went on Friday.
The wedding was in Christchurch and in Burley - the New Forest. What can I say? The place impressed me so much! The New Forest was created by William the Conqueror as a hunting area.
Actually, “forest" in a medieval sense was a legally defined area – with a special laws - where the "beasts of the chase" (deer & wild pig) and their food were protected for the pleasure of the monarch. It was not necessarily a wooded area in the modern meaning - nearly half the New Forest is open heath, grassland and bog…
…Walking among the magnificent trees, listening to the whisper of the fallen leaves, sound of the wind, playing with the naked branches, touching the wet grass and bushes, I walked pass, I wished I could capture all this mystery of the Melancholic Nature...I haven't got enough words to describe it - most of the times I would just stand there, unable to take my eyes off gorgeous views...A wish I’d be a poet. For any other genre cannot tell enough of what was uncovering in front of my eyes! ...I definitely love the Fall the most of all the seasons…
Well, those 3 days have been filled not only with the hassles of the wedding and tranquillity of the nature. Since we were in area anyway, we’ve decided to see as much as we can…[~and – oh boy, wasn’t this completely “as much” and very little of “we can”?!]

We live about 5 miles from a rendering plant where they boil down animal carcases. This plant emmits the most astonishingly horrible smells ! But it only becomes a problem when the wind blows from just the right direction. And thankfully that means it's not a problem ALL the time :-) I wrote a poem about it not long ago.... here it is:
Ode To Stench
Oh Bovine stench of epic proportions
Your seething cauldrons spew evil concoctions.
Your most offal potions stew in darkness of night
Those odiferous emissions are truly a fright.
Turning crisp spring air to foul smelling eruptions
With more than a hint of horrific corruptions.
I’ve heard your malodors can be partially muzzled
Why you don’t do it keeps me thoroughly puzzled.
Instead under cover of midnight so deep
You create new meaning of disruption of sleep.
The smelliferous fumes from your boiling heap
Odious and loathsome through our windows do creep.
Cease I say, your obnoxious pollutions
Desist emitting your olfactory intrusions.
Else some dark night after rising from bed,
We will come and install a big bag on your head.

I’m tucked up in bed early with my book. It’s October and the days are getting shorter. Night has fallen and there’s a fine drizzle falling outside. I almost always sleep with my window open if just a little. I am listening to the rain making plop, plop noises onto the matted leaves under the maple tree outside.
A small breeze is blowing chill air laden with the moist moldy smell that makes autumn the best time of the year. What is contained in that smell that touches some primal place and urges us to shelter ourselves, store up food, and indulge in long convoluted story telling ?
I feel compelled to fry donuts, bake bread, make soup, start a quilt, knit a sweater, write a friend. All from breathing deeply of a chill autumn breeze.
Our harvesting is over and now we shall have time to gather our thoughts and think them more deeply and mayhap we shall become wise this winter. The seeds of doubt that we may have planted in the spring have grown into great heaps of thoughts that must now be sorted out and understood. More lessons learned that must be distilled to sustain us in the slumber time of winter.
Every year, I am surprised by this fall phenomenon. It is as if winter, spring and summer erase my memory of this tender time of year out of sheer jealousy of it’s power. Somehow I wonder if that power is the secret that what seems like the ending is really the beginning. A tantalizing thought, a conundrum worthy of a long debate with a good friend. But my eyes begin to droop from the long days’ work. I pull the covers up to my chin but refuse to close the window. I must breathe the air and fall under the spell before autumn turns to winter. Perhaps this time I will not forget… perhaps.

This morning I remembered how I almost left my phone on the kitchen counter, the charger tangled with my badge for work. It’s like every little thing is half-done lately. Right now, I’m just trying to eat my sandwich in peace at my desk, but my mind keeps running through the list of things I need to sort out. There’s the project deadline moving up, the car needs servicing, and I still haven’t booked that plumber for the leaking faucet. At lunch, I scrolled through my messages and saw a few from her, asking about plans for the weekend, which I haven’t replied to yet. I want to, but I honestly don’t know what I’ll be able to commit to. Between work, trying to keep the grocery shopping under control, and those endless emails, social things feel like another job. Maybe that’s why last night, when she called just to chat, I felt weirdly tense. I like her, but I don’t know where we’re headed, and my mind is just so tired. It’s easier to focus on the next thing I have to check off the list than talk about feelings or what comes next. I keep telling myself things will settle down, but every day lately just feels like a bunch of little fires to put out. Even finding time to call my brother back has been impossible, and he left a voicemail about Dad’s birthday next week, which I totally forgot. I know I’m dropping the ball with people, but I can’t think straight with so much unfinished business everywhere I look. Maybe after work I’ll just sit in the car for a few minutes and breathe before heading home. Not sure if that helps, but it’s something.

The fridge hums louder than usual in the early morning quiet, and the first light is barely creeping across the counter. My laptop is already open next to a pile of bills and my planner with sticky notes everywhere, but I can’t remember if I actually put the laundry in last night or if I just meant to. There are three emails flagged from my manager about the quarterly close, and I still haven’t finished the spreadsheet for Dad’s insurance paperwork (it’s been sitting open on my desktop for days). I keep making these lists, but then I lose them or rewrite them and somehow the same things are always there: submit mileage report, call the bank, book Mom’s checkup, send receipts for the new monitor. I had planned to get up early to get a head start, but I just end up staring at the to-do app, feeling like everything blurs together. My brother texted about arranging something for next weekend, and I need to reply, but my brain just skips it. I keep thinking I should go for a walk or do something to snap out of this fog, but I can’t seem to make myself move past the kitchen table. There’s a weird comfort in the routine of making tea, even if half the time I forget it and it gets cold. Work and home feel like the same endless loop lately, and it’s hard to tell what’s urgent and what can wait. I keep telling myself I’ll catch up, but the list is always longer than the day feels.

This afternoon, I kept replaying that moment in the grocery store when I caught myself reaching for the same brand of cereal he always bought, and then stopped—almost dropped the box. It’s strange how little things like that can just catch me off guard. At the time, it felt like someone pressed pause on everything else and I was just standing there, holding this dumb box and feeling out of place. Now, after dinner, I’m still at the table, staring at a half-empty glass of water and the stack of unopened mail next to it, feeling the weight of it all. The apartment is too quiet except for the hum of the fridge, and I keep wishing I could just call someone—maybe him, maybe not—but I can’t decide what I’d even say.

We barely spoke at lunch. There was this tension, like neither of us knew what to talk about, or maybe we were both avoiding the things we really needed to say. I keep wondering if it’s just the move, or if it’s me—maybe I’m too restless, too uncertain about where I fit now. I used to feel so sure about everything, but lately I second-guess myself about the smallest things. I can’t seem to settle, can’t distract myself with work the way I used to. Even washing the dishes tonight felt like some big effort. I know I’m supposed to give it time, but I’m impatient, I guess. I just want to feel like myself again, or at least figure out who that is here. Maybe I’ll go for a walk before bed, even if it’s dark—at least it’s something to do.

Earlier today I caught myself snapping at Sam in the kitchen, something about the dishwasher, I can’t even remember exactly what I said. I keep replaying it in my head now, sitting at the table with my laptop open but not really working. The house is quiet except for the dishwasher (ironic) and I’m trying to make sense of my own reactions, but everything feels jumbled, like I’m half here and half somewhere else.

I know I’m stretched thin, with classes piling up and seeing clients during the day, but I hate how easily I get irritable with people I care about. I thought I’d be better at this, being a therapist and all, but instead I just feel exposed, like my own nerves are always on the surface lately. Sam didn’t even seem that bothered, but I could tell it made a weird distance between us for the rest of the evening.

What am I doing, really? There’s this constant low-level buzz in my chest, like I’m chasing after something but not sure what I’m supposed to catch. Am I becoming the person I want to be, or just scrambling to keep up with a version of myself that isn’t real? I keep wondering if everyone else feels this lost sometimes, or if it’s just me pretending to have answers for other people while I fumble through my own life.

I told myself I’d apologize tomorrow and try to be more present, but right now I mostly just want to shut my brain off for a bit. I wish I knew how to slow down. Maybe I need to let myself be a mess instead of constantly trying to fix everything. Maybe that’s okay. Or maybe I need to get some actual sleep for once. I don’t know.

This morning I found myself staring at the pill organizer by the sink, just counting through the compartments for Mom, making sure I didn’t miss anything even though I’ve checked it three times already. Felt like it set the tone for the day—always double checking, triple checking. Now, after dinner, the kitchen is still a mess. There’s a half-eaten plate of lasagna, my laptop open next to a bottle of Tylenol, and I keep thinking about how much I hate that work emails are coming in even now, when all I want is a few quiet minutes with my thoughts.

I keep hearing the hum of the dishwasher and the clink of someone’s fork, but my mind drifts to Dad, how he used to clear the table with this big showy sigh like he was the only one who could do it right. It’s hard not to feel the gap he left, especially when things get quiet. I try to be hopeful, I really do, and I keep the family calendar updated and the to-do lists on my phone, but these days feel like they’re piling up faster than I can sort them. Even organizing things doesn’t bring the relief it used to. I know tomorrow will bring more of the same, but maybe I’ll find a way to carve out an hour for myself. For now, I’ll just sit here and listen to the dishwasher until it’s done.

I keep playing Battlefield 6 for the PS5. I want to say that I've gotten about as good as I'm going to get in the game. I get kills. I die. In fact, I die a lot. My intent when I play this game is to contribute to the team effort and not be the reason why my team loses. I like to be a team player in the game and if anything, I've discovered that I have a penchant for being a team healer, or as the game would identify me, as a combat medic. For the most part, I'm playing the game according to these simple expectations. Don't die so much. Kill more than I die. Revive as many of my fallen teammates as I possibly can. I'll even go so far as to run like a rhino, head down into gun fire, if it means being able to revive a downed teammate before they die. I'm all about the team effort, at least in the game, I am. In the real world, not so much. I'd like to get to bed in just over an hour and a half, in preparation of the work day tomorrow, but I'm going to be honest. For the first time in a long time, I don't feel like busting my ass to wake up so early just so that I can get to the office at 4:45am. I've maintained that modified work schedule for just over two years. When I first started this schedule, I was motivated. I wanted to come in early and get some work done before anyone else arrives. I obviously liked the bloated paycheck that comes with working as early as I do and working as many hours as I do. Going into the office as early as I did was fun and it felt good being able to improve upon my productivity. Now, I'm starting to question why I even bother. I think a lot of this has to do with the reality that management doesn't care how good my work is. They're content with the mediocre and even poor work that my coworkers are doing. It makes me wonder why I continue to put in the considerable effort that I do, when so much less will suffice. Why am I working at a level 10, when working at a level two will work just as well? I'm still going to go to bed early, just as I always do, but when that alarm goes off at 3:40am tomorrow, I can't readily say that I'll spring out of bed and start my day with that morning shower. I might not even give a shit because I'm gradually starting to wonder what the whole point is. As I wrote in my previous entry, it was nice and cold outside for once. I'm hoping that this starts a trend that will continue for at least the next month, if not longer, because I've about had it with this 80-degree weather. Hell, even 70 degrees is way too damn hot for this time of year. I'm not asking that it snow, but damn, can it at least kind of look like winter, even for Southern California? I don't know if my optimism is going to pay off here. I don't know what prompted me to write yet another entry, which would be my second entry on the day. I guess I'm still testing out this keyboard. I don't think I had much to say, so I just decided to write whatever the hell came to mind. Battlefield 6. My reluctance to go to work tomorrow. Wishing for continued cold weather. Yeah, there's not really a whole lot going on in my world at the moment. As for this keyboard, I still don't know.

This morning, while scrambling eggs in the kitchen, I could hear my roommate’s alarm blaring through the wall even though he’d already left—another reminder of how out-of-sync our lives have gotten lately. Now I’m at my desk, laptop open, half-finished draft glaring at me in the harsh glow of my desk lamp. It’s already late, maybe close to midnight, and my eyes sting every time I blink. I keep thinking I’ll find a rhythm with these deadlines, but every time I sit down to write, I just feel this heavy mix of pressure and exhaustion. The words aren’t coming as easily as they used to, and I wonder if it’s just one of those days or if I’m burning out. I tried taking a walk around the block earlier to clear my head, but when I got back, the to-do list looked even longer somehow. There’s a half-eaten apple next to my keyboard, forgotten hours ago. I know I should probably sleep, but I can’t seem to close the laptop without feeling like I’m giving up for the night. Maybe I’ll just write a few more sentences and see if anything clicks before I crash. The apartment is finally quiet, but my mind’s still buzzing.

Hi, gorgeous.

We watched Barbie and spent a lot of the time laughing, remembering some of the parts we used to enjoy with you, the memes shared, your reactions when we saw it in the theater. Danny and Flash will always have a special place in my heart, but the story with Taika and the Blade was something really special to me. In my mind they will always live in a small cottage in the middle of a dark forest, with legends of the witch and her red-furred guardian werewolf whispered in hushed tones in the nearby towns.
You're my forever, Madelaine. I miss you so much. I love you. I hope Merlin and Morgan are behaving.

The sunlight is sneaking through the blinds and making a weird pattern on my desk, right across my planner that’s already filled with color-coded reminders. I felt on edge this morning during my walk around the block, thinking about the talk I had with Mark last night. Things have been tense between us lately, even though I know we're both trying to improve how we communicate. I tried to bring up how I've been feeling about my mom's health, but he seemed distracted, and I wasn’t sure if I was making sense or just rambling. Maybe I expected him to know what I needed without me saying it outright, which isn’t fair. I get restless when I can’t express things clearly, and I ended up feeling more alone, even with him sitting right next to me.

Walking helped me sort through some of the jumbled thoughts, but not all of them. I want to be honest with him, but I also worry I’ll come across as too needy or overly sensitive. It’s hard to find the balance, especially when life feels unpredictable. I’m trying to stay optimistic and gentle, not just with Mark but with myself. I keep hoping that if I’m patient, we’ll understand each other better, but I’m not sure how long it will take. For now, I guess I’ll try again tonight, maybe with fewer expectations.

Just cleared the dinner plates and left them stacked by the sink, not even in the mood to rinse them right away. The kitchen light feels too bright, almost buzzing, and I keep rubbing my eyes like that’ll help me think straighter. Today started early—somehow I was up by 5:15, even before the alarm, mind already ticking off deadlines and those unfinished tax forms at work. I thought about texting Mark (funny, still feels strange to write his name in here) but held back, not sure if it’s too soon for a good morning message or if I’m just overthinking it, which I probably am. I keep replaying little bits of our last conversation, trying to figure out if I missed anything, if I should have said more or less or something different entirely. My head’s fuzzy, like I’m moving through a mist, and I can’t decide if that’s just tiredness or something else—not unhappy, just uncertain. 

Work was the usual blur, numbers and emails and people dropping off receipts in messy piles. Sometimes I catch myself wondering if I’m really present or just moving through everything on autopilot. Still, there was a moment around lunch when the sun came through the office window and I let myself smile, thinking about the weekend and maybe seeing Mark again. I haven’t told anyone at work yet, feels too new and fragile to put out there. The fork in my hand now is cold, and I keep fidgeting with it instead of getting up and actually cleaning up. Really, I’m grateful for this, even if I don’t know what will happen next. I guess I’m hoping for the best and trying to let things unfold, even if my brain feels like it’s wrapped in cotton. Maybe tomorrow will be clearer—or at least I’ll get the dishes done before bed.

As i dealing through my illness thirteen years ago I had a lot of What If's, Should Have's, and Could Have's on my thoughts, but the main one was What If. The one question raised on my mind often while dealing with my illness. "What if I died?" That was a scary question because I would not have known what would have happened after I died because I would not been able to see. "What would my parents and family do without me?" Questions like that raised in my mind constantly. It was horrible for a seventeen year old to think when her life was only yet young - not yet a grown up in the adult world just yet. Honestly questions did rise in my mind a lot and during my illness lots of questions arose and I never shared those thoughts with anyone - not even my closest friends and family members.

Just sent out another round of job applications while waiting for the bus, which felt like both a relief and a waste of time at the same time. I keep rereading my cover letters and thinking they sound too desperate, but then again, not sending anything would be even worse. The bus ride home is long enough to get lost in my head, and tonight I kept flipping between checking my messages from my kid’s mom about switching weekends and scrolling job boards. It’s like my brain can’t focus on anything for more than a couple minutes. I wanted to text her back with a clear answer, but then I remembered I need to double-check my own schedule, and now I’m worried I already committed to something else next Saturday.

There’s a weird mix of hope and frustration, like maybe something will finally work out, but also expecting to screw it up somehow.
